title: [test] golden tests for percentile interpolation methods (linear/lower/higher/nearest/midpoint)
close_reason: COMPLETE, no defect found. percentile_methods_match_numpy_golden already covered all five methods but only on the odd length 7 at four quantiles. Four tests fill what that leaves. (1) percentile_methods_match_numpy_on_even_length_and_endpoints: n=8 where the median falls between samples and lower/higher/nearest stop agreeing, plus q=0/q=100 and the n=1 degenerate case, against numpy goldens. (2) percentile_midpoint_uses_numpy_lerp_not_the_naive_mean: numpy's midpoint is _lerp(a,b,0.5)=b-(b-a)*0.5, NOT (a+b)/2; those agree on ordinary inputs so the only discriminator is a case where the naive mean OVERFLOWS - (1e308+1.5e308)/2 is +inf where numpy returns a finite 1.25e308 - and linear at q=50 shares the t>=0.5 branch and is checked alongside. This is the one assertion nothing else in the suite could have caught. (3) percentile_methods_agree_with_closed_form_on_the_parallel_path: the method arm is duplicated THREE times (serial reduce, parallel reduce, radix-select) so a fix to one copy can miss the others; sorted values of a permutation of 0..n-1 are the index itself, giving each method a closed form a 2^20 input must reproduce. (4) percentile_nearest_breaks_halfway_ties_to_even_like_numpy: four CONSECUTIVE ties on n=5 with alternating parity plus the other methods at the same points. HONESTY NOTE: I initially justified (4) as closing the half-to-even discrimination gap, then checked and found the existing golden ALREADY pins one tie of each parity (q=25 -> lo=1 odd, q=75 -> lo=4 even on n=7); I corrected the comment and commit message rather than keep the overclaim. Its remaining value is catching a parity taken off the wrong index. No source change needed. EVIDENCE: timeout 120 cargo test -p fnp-ufunc --lib = 2275 passed / 0 failed in 47.53s (2271 before); cargo fmt --check -p fnp-ufunc exit 0 run UNPIPED. Commit 5d425da8.

title: perf(nanargmax/nanargmin): the cold-extract residual is 15.45x slower than numpy on a STRIDED operand the sweep never tests, and 1.37x on the contiguous band below the parallel gate
description:
MEASURED, TanBridge, thinkstation1, numpy 2.4.3 live, fnp .so sha256
984a2dc0cfd86f7f4ec579432742c94e8443bf190b62aa4446c216523e054104 (at abdf2d33).

## HOW THIS WAS FOUND, AND WHY THE SWEEP UNDERSTATES IT ~50x

`nanargmax[f64]` / `nanargmin[f64]` are among the eight sweep losses that survive a dual-null
re-measurement (1.260x / 1.270x, ~13 us each). Scaling in n and varying the operand's CONTIGUITY
turns up something much larger that the sweep never touches, because its ladder is all
C-contiguous:

```
  operand (n=2^16)                 numpy_ns      fnp_ns   ratio
  C-contiguous (what the sweep uses)  37848       51890    1.37x
  NON-contiguous a[::2]               48748      753376   15.45x   <- 705 us delta
```

A strided view is entirely ordinary - `a[::2]`, a column of a 2-D array, any slice with a step.

## MECHANISM - THE COLD-EXTRACT RESIDUAL, THIRD TIME THIS SESSION

After the zero-copy gates decline, `nanargmax`/`nanargmin` reach

    let a = extract_numeric_array(py, a.bind(py), "nanargmax(a)")?;   // COPIES the whole array
    let result = a.nanargmax(axis)?;
    let output = build_numpy_array_from_ufunc(py, &result)?;

Same shape as `take`'s residual (`deadlock-audit-yphwc`) and `meshgrid`'s cold branch
(`deadlock-audit-bvihx`): a "native" path that copies its operand and is far SLOWER than simply
delegating. numpy's own nanargmax is `_replace_nan` (also a copy) plus argmax, and still beats it
15x on a strided operand.

**BOTH losses have this one cause.** The contiguous 1.37x is the same residual: at n=2^16 the
operand is below `NANARG_PARALLEL_MIN = 1 << 19`, so the parallel kernel declines and control falls
into the same extract.

## THE RESIDUAL IS NOT ALWAYS WRONG - IT WINS AT SMALL n

```
  n       numpy_ns    fnp_ns   ratio
  2^11      8807.8    7195.6   0.82x  WIN
  2^12      9976.2    8661.8   0.87x  WIN
  2^13     23115.7   18628.2   0.81x  WIN
  2^14     24492.8   18285.6   0.75x  WIN
  2^15     24922.6   30824.0   1.24x  LOSS
  2^16     40447.4   55429.8   1.37x  LOSS
```

Sharp crossover between 2^14 and 2^15. So this is a GATE problem, not a delete-the-path problem -
the same conclusion `deadlock-audit-dc6mz` reached for `APPEND_PAR_MIN`.

## THE FIX

Two guards before the residual, in both `nanargmax` and `nanargmin`:

1. NON-CONTIGUOUS -> delegate. `noncontiguous_ndarray()` already exists and `take` uses it for
   exactly this reason ("Non-contiguous (transposed/strided) source ndarrays bail into the cold
   extract; delegate to numpy's strided take"). Worth 15.45x.
2. CONTIGUOUS AND n >= 1<<15, axis=None -> delegate, because the residual loses from 2^15 and the
   parallel kernel does not open until 1<<19. That band currently has no good route.

Below 1<<15 the residual keeps its 0.75-0.87x win; at and above 1<<19 the parallel kernel keeps its
0.40x/0.17x win.

## ACCEPTANCE

Same-session interleaved A/B of two builds, across the contiguity axis AND the size band, plus a
dual-null contract. Values are integers (an index) so bit-exactness is trivially covered, but the
all-NaN-slice ValueError path and the axis= forms must be re-verified: numpy raises
`ValueError("All-NaN slice encountered")` and the guards must not change which arm raises it.
close_reason: SHIPPED 377a6280, banked. Two guards before the cold-extract residual in both nanargmax and nanargmin: non-contiguous delegates (precedented by take), and contiguous axis=None with size>=1<<15 delegates. Strided n=2^16 goes 7.365x LOSS -> 1.022x; contiguous band 1.479x -> 1.019x; both the small-n (0.89x) and large-n (0.26x) wins preserved. Contract: DECIDABLE_REGRESSION 0.944235 (nanargmax) and 0.941209 (nanargmin), i.e. ~1.06x, down from 1.34x - still a regression, NOT parity, and quoted that way. exact_bytes passed. Zero parity divergences across contiguity x size x axis x 6 dtypes x the all-NaN ValueError path.

title: perf(strided vein): the loss sweep's ladder is ALL C-contiguous - a strided sweep finds 39 losses it cannot see, topped by deg2rad at 7.08x strided vs 0.15x contiguous
description:
A NEW OPERAND AXIS THE LOSS SWEEP CANNOT SEE, and 39 cells on it.

TanBridge, thinkstation1, numpy 2.4.3 live, fnp .so sha256
76a87a296ad998c382c6... (at 377a6280).

## WHY THIS AXIS WAS INVISIBLE

`bench_vs_numpy_loss_sweep`'s operand ladder is entirely C-contiguous. `deadlock-audit-0e1q5`
(nanargmax/nanargmin) was the first crack: the contiguous cell read 1.37x while a strided view read
7.365x. That suggested the ladder, not the ops, was the limit.

A Python-side sweep over `dir(fnp) & dir(np)` with a STRIDED ladder (`a[::2]`, a strided pair, and
a transposed 2-D), each cell timed against its own CONTIGUOUS control of the same values:

```
  strided   contig   numpy_ns      fnp_ns   case
    7.08x    0.15x      77547      549052  deg2rad[strided]      <- 47x swing on layout alone
    7.06x    0.16x      77507      547318  rad2deg[strided]
    5.90x    0.18x     124827      735897  modf[strided]
    4.44x    0.82x     809957     3599301  concatenate[transposed]
    4.38x    0.79x     812963     3562000  concat[transposed]
    3.11x    0.47x     249333      774770  extract[strided_2]
    2.68x    0.08x     184580      494258  spacing[strided]
    2.23x    0.00x     166276      371455  trim_zeros[strided]
    1.72x    0.27x    2749428     4722953  isin[strided_2]
    1.69x    0.92x    1112712     1879376  divmod[strided_2]
    1.36x    0.29x    1029103     1401519  sinc[strided]
    1.35x    1.01x      46869       63370  append[strided_2]
```

220 comparable cells, **39 strided losses above 1.15x**, and the ones above are STRIDED-ONLY - the
contiguous control is a win or parity, so the existing instrument scores them as healthy.

## MECHANISM - one shape, many sites

Every top cell has the same structure: a zero-copy fast path that requires a contiguous buffer, a
dtype check that PASSES (the operand really is f64), and then
`extract_precise_numeric_array`, which copies the whole operand to get a contiguous one. NumPy's
strided loop beats that copy comfortably.

`extract_precise_numeric_array` appears at **116 sites** in `crates/fnp-python/src/lib.rs`. Not all
are reachable with a strided operand and not all have a delegation path handy, but the 39 measured
losses say the pattern is live.

This is the third distinct systematic vein of the same family, after `deadlock-audit-6lzmo`
(95 `num_threads` chunkers) and the cold-extract residuals already fixed in `take`, `meshgrid` and
`nanargmax`/`nanargmin`.

## THE FIX SHAPE, ALREADY PROVEN THREE TIMES

    if noncontiguous_ndarray(numpy, x)? { return <delegate to numpy>; }

placed where the zero-copy path declined for LAYOUT rather than dtype. `take` carries it, and
`nanargmax`/`nanargmin` gained it in `377a6280`.

## DONE IN THIS BEAD

`native_angle_conversion` only - shared by `deg2rad`, `rad2deg`, `degrees`, `radians`, the two
largest cells at 7.08x/7.06x.

## NOT DONE - the rest of the vein

`modf`, `spacing`, `concatenate`/`concat` (transposed), `extract`, `trim_zeros`, `isin`, `divmod`,
`sinc`, `append` and ~30 more. Each needs its own site inspected: the guard is only correct where a
delegation path exists and where the zero-copy decline really is about layout. **Do not sweep this
by script** - AGENTS.md forbids it and the sites differ.

## ACCEPTANCE, per site

Strided AND contiguous timings (the contiguous control is what proves the guard did not cost the
existing win), a dual-null A/B, and a parity probe over the dtypes that route through the changed
helper. Re-run the strided sweep afterwards to confirm the cell left the list.
close_reason: DRAINED across three ships: 0ecf6f44 (deg2rad/rad2deg/degrees/radians 10.979x -> 1.008x), 30895dd7 (isposinf/isneginf/logical_not 35.343x -> 1.032x), d33d94d7 (all/any/ediff1d/frexp/modf 19.793x -> 1.047x). Ledger b47125ed, 9373a772, and this one. Strided sweep went from 39 losses above 1.15x with TEN above 5x (worst 32.485x) to 27 with NONE above 1.47x. Every contiguous control preserved, including any's 15.6x win unchanged to three decimals. Closed 3 pre-existing ediff1d(bool) divergences and avoided introducing a layout-dependent one. corrcoef's 20.78x triage entry was checked and DROPPED as an artifact (1-D input, degenerate). Remaining sub-1.5x entries whose strided and contiguous ratios AGREE are entry overhead, not layout defects.

title: [perf][fnp-linalg][no-gaps] eigvalsh 4.2x slower than numpy at n=1024 (symmetric eigenvalues)
description: np.linalg.eigvalsh on SPD f64: n=512 fnp 46.9ms vs numpy 26.3ms = 1.79x; n=1024 fnp 300.9ms vs numpy 71.6ms = 4.20x (perf_linalg sweep 2026-06-14, box load ~6, numpy NOT thrashing — legit gap that WORSENS with n, classic sign of a lower-order-parallelized or less-cache-blocked kernel). numpy uses LAPACK dsyevd (divide-and-conquer tridiagonal eigensolver). LEVER (no-ceiling): profile fnp's eigvalsh path (eigvalsh_nxn in fnp-linalg) — likely the Householder tridiagonalization (O(n^3), the bulk) and/or the QL/bisection eigenvalue stage is serial or poorly blocked. Attack the tridiagonalization with a BLOCKED (panel + rank-k symmetric trailing update, dsytrd-class) reduction that reuses the existing parallel SYRK/GEMM microkernels (same panel-reuse structure just landed for cholesky in ff302aa3), and/or parallelize the eigenvalue iteration. Bit-identity: eigvalsh has an exact-repr/golden test (batch_lanes ... uses eigvalsh_nxn to_bits) — blocking changes Householder accumulation order so this likely needs allclose relaxation (numpy eigvalsh is allclose-contract) OR a same-order blocked reduction. Target >=2x at n=1024, no regression at n<=512. NOTE: fnp-linalg/lib.rs is currently peer-hot (concurrent cholesky edits) — land via isolated worktree on a disjoint function (eigvalsh_nxn), verify 0 peer tokens staged. Found by cc 2026-06-14.
close_reason: Routed deeper; no bounded production microlever remains. Pass 1 baseline: remote RCH vmi1153651 eigvalsh_nxn/size/512 [80.865, 82.475, 84.615] ms; no 1024 Criterion row exists. Pass 2 excluded prior rejected families: terminal Sturm bisection, dense adjacent-Givens full-to-band/band-to-tridiag, direct rank-2k/SYR2K streaming, matvec threshold lowering, simple panel-width retunes, scratch reuse, and const-specialization. Current profile still points at tridiag_reduce/dlatrd data movement (~293ms / 93% at n=1024), so the honest next primitive is the new successor franken_numpy-ixs5y.196: SBR stage-1 dense-to-band proof slice, followed by a separate compressed-band bulge-chase production route. No source change kept for deadlock-audit-0kqvd.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: PROFILED (cc 2026-06-14, isolated worktree off ff302aa3). eigvalsh time split (instrumented, n=1024): tridiag_reduce=293ms (93%), tridiag_eig_qr=22ms (7%); n=512: tridiag=46-54ms, qr=5.9ms. So eigvalsh perf == tridiagonalization perf; the QR iteration is negligible. Within tridiag_reduce_blocked, TWO serial bottlenecks: (1) the dlatrd panel matvec u=A·v (lines ~3884-3910) is ~85% of tridiag (~250ms@1024) and is MEMORY-BANDWIDTH-BOUND on one core (~2.8GB traffic for n=1024 matvecs / ~12GB/s single-core ≈ 230ms, matches). It re-reads the full trailing submatrix once per panel column (nb sequential dsymv). (2) the rank-2k trailing update was serial (k=nb=64 < packed_gemm's k>=128 gate). TRIED + RESULTS: (a) band-parallel trailing rank-2k update (BYTE-IDENTICAL, golden 00cda7e2 unchanged) → only ~15% (320→275ms@1024, 4.85→4.34x) since the trailing update is only ~15% of tridiag. (b) lowering TRIDIAG_MATVEC_PAR_MIN 1024→256 to parallelize the matvec → REGRESSED (4.34→5.18x): the per-column par_iter pays rayon wakeup latency ×~768 dispatches AND the matvec doesn't speed up with cores — memory bandwidth does NOT aggregate (NUMA: single-allocation work matrix lives on one node; remote cores throttled). So the one-stage dsymv panel is a hard memory/NUMA wall. REAL LEVER = TWO-STAGE SBR (dsytrd_2stage): stage-1 dense→band reduction is ALL BLAS-3 GEMM (cache-blocked, compute-bound, parallelizes + NUMA-tileable — reuses the existing packed_gemm), stage-2 band→tridiagonal via bulge-chasing (O(n²·b), cheap). This REPLACES the memory-bound dsymv panel entirely. Target 2-3x@n>=512. Effort: large (bulge-chasing is intricate); the byte-identical band-parallel trailing update (a) is a ready sub-piece to fold in. Alternative medium lever: symmetric-storage scatter matvec (read only lower triangle = halve traffic) but it CHANGES summation order → needs eigvalsh parity relaxed to allclose (numpy IS allclose) + golden updates (batch_lanes to_bits + eig goldens).

title: [perf][fnp-python][no-gaps] cov/corrcoef Gram 8-accumulator dot — beats numpy for n_vars>=128, allclose
close_reason: Shipped. cov_gram_rowvar_f64 computed each symmetric-Gram cell as a single-accumulator dot (one dependent FP-add chain, latency-bound ~3 GFLOP/s) — numpy's dsyrk is vectorized ~11 GFLOP/s, so cov/corrcoef were 1.06-1.5x slower for n_vars>=128 and ~3x for few-vars. Replaced with an 8-independent-accumulator dot (dot8, chunks_exact(8)) that breaks the dependency chain and lets LLVM pack the accumulators into AVX registers (autovectorized). allclose (reorder), NOT bit-identical for n_obs>=8; for n_obs<8 (all exact-repr cov/corrcoef unit-test sizes) chunks_exact(8) is empty so the fold is the original left-to-right sum and those tests stay green. INVESTIGATION (this turn, on cov): (1) route Gram through UFuncArray::matmul = REGRESSED 6x (fnp matmul is slow for thin-output/fat-k cov shape; the matmul profile-gate defers such shapes to numpy precisely because fnp loses there). (2) cell-flattened par_iter = WORSE (into_par_iter+collect+sqrt-decode overhead). (3) 8-acc row-parallel = the keeper. Score (self vs naive): (200,5000) 5064->4088us 1.24x, (50,2000) 759->709us; vs numpy now 0.76-0.92x (FASTER) for n_vars=128..500, still 3-4x for few-vars (n_vars<=50: too few rows for parallelism, small total work where numpy dsyrk has near-zero overhead — the remaining gap). allclose verified across 6 shapes x 5 kwargs; cov fast-path golden sha256 re-pinned a66b74e9->80bb612d (allclose-verified, deterministic); all 27 conformance_statistics + 5 lib cov/corrcoef unit tests green. REMAINING: few-vars-many-obs cov needs a register-blocked SIMD dsyrk microkernel (shared primitive with cholesky-SYRK) to beat numpy there — research-grade. NOTE: peer concurrently working cholesky_ordered_dot in fnp-linalg (5th cholesky lever).

title: [perf][fnp-python] isolate whether the f64 divide loss is the NORMALITY ACCUMULATE or our divide codegen - one accumulate-free control arm vs numpy
description:
MEASURED ON thinkstation1 (elf ef5467cb2a43c00b, numpy 2.4.3, existing binary, no build):

  n=2^20, SAME zerocopy route, same host, same invocation class:
    multiply (no hazard scan)  numpy 411972 ns  fnp 421781 ns  ratio 0.965590  excess   9809 ns
    divide   (fused scan)      numpy 498471 ns  fnp 591864 ns  ratio 0.845461  excess  93393 ns

  divide excess / multiply excess = 9.52x
  each side vs ITS OWN multiply: numpy divide 1.2100x, ours 1.4032x -> ratio-of-ratios 1.1597

DECIDED BY THAT: the divide loss is NOT the wrapper/route. multiply shares every route stage by
construction and sits at 0.9656 at the same n, and the route sweep shows excess_ns roughly CONSTANT
across 2^8..2^24 (2044, 2159, 2991, 9809, 5425 ns) reaching at_parity=true by 2^24. The route is a
per-call floor that amortises away. ~84 us of divide's ~93 us deficit at 2^20 is divide-specific.

NOT DECIDED, and this is the bead: whether that ~16% is the NORMALITY ACCUMULATE that
deadlock-audit-vqxoa fused into the divide loop, or our divide CODEGEN (unrolling/scheduling around
vdivpd). The subtraction above is across two different ops, so it cannot separate them. The existing
bench_divide_fe_hazard_serial / _fused_serial groups compare our-before vs our-after - self-speedup -
and structurally cannot settle it either.

THE CONTROL: one arm running the f64 divide loop with the normality accumulate REMOVED, measured
against numpy.divide in the SAME invocation under common::run_dual_null_median_ci_contract at
n=2^20, alongside the existing accumulated arm.
  - lands near multiply's 0.9656  -> the accumulate is the cost; vqxoa's 'close to free' is refuted
    against the incumbent and the fusion needs a cheaper formulation. The untried direction is
    already named by deadlock-audit-ae85t's retry predicate: a reduction over the quotients IN PLACE,
    no round-trip through a temporary (the round-trip is what broke vectorisation in the rejected
    blocked form).
  - still reads ~0.845 -> the accumulate is innocent, the cost is our divide codegen, different lever.

WHY vqxoa's CLAIM NEEDS THIS: vqxoa fused the flag into the divide loop and argued the accumulate is
'close to free' because vdivpd is throughput-bound with idle integer slots beside it. That was a real
SELF-speedup against the two-pass form, but it was never checked against the incumbent, and measured
that way ~16% sits on the divide path that multiply does not pay.

HARD CONSTRAINT - NEGATIVE CASE a naive implementation would fail: the accumulate-free arm MUST NOT
SHIP. Removing it drops the FE-hazard deferral and reintroduces the six divergence rows
deadlock-audit-2nmd1 closed (numpy raises a RuntimeWarning we cannot, so bit-identical values are not
parity). It is a MEASUREMENT control living in the bench binary only. A patch that deletes the
accumulate from the shipped route to win this number is the reward-hacking failure this bead exists
to forbid; the correctness gate is conformance_diagnostics green with the deferral still firing.

CONSTRAINT: needs a build - defer below the disk brake. Everything above was measured build-free on
an existing ELF.

title: [perf][reduction] Parallel exact flat min/max/argmin/argmax for float64
description: NumPy runs every reduction single-threaded (measured cpu/wall=1.00x at 64M f64); fnp delegates min/max/argmin/argmax. CORRECTION to the original description: NumPy's float min/max tie rule is NOT 'last tied element wins'. That holds for small arrays and adjacent elements but BREAKS at scale — measured at 2,200,000 elements, NumPy's choice between +0.0 and -0.0 flips exactly when the tied zero sits at a 65,536-element boundary (positions 0/65536/131072 disagree with positional-last; 1/65535/65537 agree), so it follows NumPy's internal blocking and SIMD lane order, not index order. Bit-exact reproduction of that tie is therefore NOT portable. Implemented instead as: parallel band scan, with DEFERRAL when the extremum is a zero AND both signs of zero are present (uniform-sign zeros are unambiguous under any rule, so the common non-negative case keeps the fast path), plus deferral when the result is NaN (payload is path-dependent: scalar preserves a planted payload, SIMD at n>=8 strips it). argmin/argmax still owe the FIRST index on ties — opposite convention, not yet implemented. 6/6 conformance green; min/max UNMEASURED so far.
close_reason: Shipped parallel vectorized flat float64 min/max: 2.482527x/2.344672x at 4M and 3.582805x/3.524936x at 64M over live NumPy 2.4.6 under same-invocation corrected dual-null measurement, all four rows DECIDABLE_WIN. Vectorizing the band scan took throughput from ~53 GB/s to ~116 GB/s. Mixed-sign-zero extrema and any-NaN buffers defer (NumPy's tie choice follows internal blocking, not index order; NaN payload is path-dependent). 6/6 conformance. argmin/argmax NOT included - they owe the FIRST index on ties, the opposite convention, and are left for a separate bead.

title: [bug][fnp-python] count_nonzero return TYPE does not track the installed numpy: fnp always int64, numpy 2.2.4 returns a Python int
description:
FOUND by SandySpring while writing the container-conformance shard for deadlock-audit-vyyk3.

SYMPTOM. On a numpy 2.2.4 host, fnp.count_nonzero and numpy.count_nonzero return DIFFERENT
Python types for the no-axis case. Captured left=numpy right=fnp, args [0, 2, 0, 3]:
  left:  "ok\nint\nint64\n()\n2"
  right: "ok\nint64\nint64\n()\n2"
The dtype (int64), shape (()) and value (2) all agree. Only type(value).__name__ differs:
numpy 2.2.4 returns a PYTHON int, fnp returns a numpy.int64 scalar.

VERSION-DEPENDENT, and fnp is pinned to the NEWER side. Verified live:
  numpy 2.2.4 (rch worker ovh-a)        -> type(np.count_nonzero([0,2,0,3])).__name__ == 'int'
  numpy 2.4.3 (local thinkstation1)     -> 'int64'
  numpy 2.4.6 (vmi115xxxx fleet majority) -> 'int64'
So numpy itself changed between 2.2.4 and 2.4.3 and fnp matches the newer behaviour. On
2.4.x hosts there is no divergence at all; on 2.2.4 hosts EVERY no-axis count_nonzero call
diverges on type. axis= and keepdims=True return an ndarray on both and are unaffected.

WHY IT IS NOT OBVIOUSLY A BUG TO FIX ONE WAY. This is the version-keying decision class,
not a plain defect. Precedent in this repo cuts both ways: commit b1932c8d ISA-keyed a
golden rather than pinning NumPy's own environment-dependent answer, and the standing rule
from the vendored-oracle work is to DEFER to numpy where upstream is mid-change instead of
encoding either side. But fnp cannot cheaply defer here without giving up the native
count_nonzero fast path, and hard-coding either type breaks the other half of the fleet.

DECISION REQUIRED (operator/structure call, which is why this is a bead and not a silent fix):
  (a) declare numpy >= 2.3 (or whatever the real boundary is) the supported oracle, record a
      row in docs/DIVERGENCES.md for older numpy, and land the shard as-is; or
  (b) make the return type track numpy at runtime (detect once at module init), which is the
      only option that is correct on both, at the cost of an init-time probe; or
  (c) find the exact upstream commit/version boundary first - this bead did NOT bisect it,
      it only has the three data points above.

PROBE THAT MUST PASS TO CLOSE: the held-back shard at
crates/fnp-python/tests/conformance_count_nonzero_containers.rs (written, NOT committed
because it is red on 2.2.4 workers and a red test must not land). Run
'cargo test -p fnp-python --test conformance_count_nonzero_containers' on BOTH a 2.2.4 host
and a 2.4.x host; both must pass. It covers list/tuple/bool/nested/3-D containers, empty and
all-zero lists, mixed int-float, signed-zero and NaN, object truthiness, scalars, 0-D
ndarray, python bool, axis 0/1/negative/tuple, keepdims with and without axis, ragged-list
ValueError and axis-out-of-bounds AxisError.

DOES NOT BLOCK the perf campaign; it is a type-surface parity defect on one numpy version.
close_reason:
RESOLVED BY OPERATOR DECISION, implemented in commit 469969ca. Supported-oracle floor: NumPy >= 2.3. NumPy 2.2.x is out of scope as an oracle.

OPERATOR RATIONALE, recorded here so it is the bead's reasoning and not one agent's say-so:
  1. The evidence is one-directional across FOUR independent instances, and it was proven not
     merely convenient by DECLINING to sweep in oo52g - which reproduced on numpy 2.4.x and got
     a kernel fix instead (commit 3a1fe6ec, f16 multiply_add addend-NaN quieting, closed 32/0).
     That contrast is what makes the pattern meaningful.
  2. The alternative surrenders a DECIDED 17.9-20.9x win on every 2.2.4 host in exchange for
     supporting a version whose own reduction strategy changed - paying a real cost to match an
     outlier.
  3. A floor is a declared, checkable contract; version-keying assertions inside test files is
     exactly the gate self-weakening that was refused four times in this chain.

THE FOUR SURFACES, all measured on the 2.2.4 class (ovh-a, vmi1149989):
  count_nonzero returns Python int vs int64 (this bead);
  inspect.signature(np.add) lacks x1/x2 (6nr1a);
  a[mask].sum() departs from numpy's OWN documented pairwise tree above ~25k selected, verdict
    NUMPY_DIFFERS on all 13 cells against a pure-numpy reference (m8z69);
  'import numpy.char' FAILS - numpy.strings has no 'slice', which landed in 2.3 (smr32).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
RECOMMENDATION by AzureHill 2026-08-06 (structure owner). Five independent symptoms, one asymmetry, one decision. Recommending option (a), the supported-oracle floor, so this stops gating other work.

THE ASYMMETRY, stated plainly. In every instance found so far, fnp matches the NEWER numpy and the 2.2.4 worker class is the outlier. NOT ONCE has it gone the other way - there is no case where fnp is wrong and 2.2.4 is right.

  1. count_nonzero (this bead). fnp returns int64; numpy 2.2.4 returns a Python int; 2.4.3 and
     2.4.6 return int64. fnp matches the newer.
  2. 6nr1a  inspect.signature(np.add) exposes x1/x2 on 2.4.3, not on 2.2.4. fnp exposes them.
     The test's two asserts are JOINTLY UNSATISFIABLE on 2.2.4 - no implementation can pass.
  3. m8z69  masked_sum byte-identity. Verdict NUMPY_DIFFERS on all 13 failing cells: fnp
     reproduces numpy's DOCUMENTED pairwise tree bit-for-bit, and 2.2.4's own a[mask].sum()
     departs from it above ~25k selected. Confirmed against a pure-numpy reference that
     touches no fnp code, and validated on 2.4.3 where reference == numpy at every size.
  4. smr32  'import numpy.char' FAILS on 2.2.4 with "module 'numpy.strings' has no attribute
     'slice'" - numpy.strings.slice did not exist until 2.3. numpy 2.2.4 cannot import its own
     char module in that environment; fnp correctly declines and ships without it.
  5. (contrast, and it PROVES the pattern is not laziness) oo52g was ALSO a byte-identity
     failure and I did NOT sweep it in here. It reproduced on numpy 2.4.x, so I fixed the
     kernel - f16 multiply_add now takes the addend's NaN, quieted. Closed on 32/0. When fnp
     IS wrong, it gets fixed; that is why the one-directional pattern above is meaningful.

WHAT IS BLOCKED RIGHT NOW: vyyk3, 6nr1a, m8z69 (P1), and smr32 partially. Four beads waiting on one unmade call. keqog was mistakenly blocked here too and I have already removed that dependency - it is red on 2.4.3, so it is a genuine defect and NOT this class.

RECOMMENDATION - option (a) from this bead's own list: declare a SUPPORTED ORACLE FLOOR of numpy >= 2.3, record it, and treat 2.2.4 workers as out of scope for conformance.

Why (a) rather than version-keying each site:
  - Version-keying means encoding TWO expectations per divergence in four separate places, and
    the standing rule from the vendored-oracle work is to DEFER where upstream is mid-change
    rather than encode either side. A floor IS that deferral, expressed once.
  - The evidence is one-directional. Version-keying is the right tool when both sides are
    defensible; here 2.2.4 is simply behind, and in case 4 it is outright broken.
  - It has a cost we can name and bound: m8z69's masked-reduction byte-identity is FALSE on
    2.2.4, which I have already annotated on the banked ledger row. Under a floor that
    annotation becomes a scope statement rather than a caveat on a live claim.
  - 6nr1a closes with NO code change at all once the floor lands.

If (a) is refused and 2.2.4 must be supported, the honest consequence must be accepted
explicitly: masked_sum would have to DEFER to numpy on builds whose reduction tree it cannot
reproduce, surrendering the 17.9-20.9x win on those hosts. That is an operator trade, not a
test edit, which is exactly why none of these four were closed by relaxing an assertion.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT for whoever decides: rch worker selection cannot be pinned for this repo
(RCH_WORKER refused, alias_wrong_target:/data), and the fleet is mixed - ovh-a and vmi1149989
are the 2.2.4 class, vmi1227854 is 2.4.x. A shard's pass/fail depends on which host it lands
on, so any green claimed without naming the worker AND its numpy version is not decidable.

title: [perf][fnp-python] localize the fnp.divide vs numpy loss: is it the FE-hazard scan or generic route overhead?
description:
deadlock-audit-su0i6 established the loss: fnp.divide reads 0.865383x (hz2) and 0.817054x (vmi1149989) vs numpy.divide, both DECIDABLE_REGRESSION, plus an undecided 0.905098x third host. We do not know WHICH part of our route costs that.

Two candidate causes, and they call for completely different levers:
(a) THE DIVIDE-SPECIFIC FE-HAZARD SCAN. Our Div arm accumulates a per-element normality flag that numpy does not compute at all (deadlock-audit-2nmd1 added it for IEEE-warning parity; jw7vk measured it cost 1.96-3.39x against our own former loop; vqxoa's fusion recovered most of that). If this is the cause, the remaining ae85t-untried direction - widening the fast accept - is the lever.
(b) GENERIC ROUTE OVERHEAD shared by every fnp binary ufunc: PyO3 dispatch, dtype/contiguity sniffing, numpy.empty output allocation and its first-touch page faults (see the large-buffer mmap-churn finding: a*b+c vs out=-reused was 2.81x at 64MiB). If this is the cause, no amount of divide-kernel work helps and the lever is the route itself.

THE CONTROL THAT SEPARATES THEM: measure fnp.multiply vs numpy.multiply on identical operands, same size, same contract, in the same invocation. Multiply takes the SAME zerocopy_f64_binary_flat route with the SAME allocation and dispatch, and has NO hazard scan. So:
 - multiply near 1.0 while divide loses  -> the scan is the cost, attack (a)
 - multiply loses by a similar margin    -> route overhead, attack (b), and the whole divide-kernel line of work cannot close it

Acceptance: a row naming WORKER and HARNESS with both nulls, giving the multiply ratio beside the divide ratio measured in the SAME invocation on the SAME worker, and a one-line verdict naming which hypothesis survives. Reporting that the scan is NOT the cause would be a success - it would retire a lever family.
close_reason: Answered, and then superseded by its own follow-up. The control worked: fnp.multiply (no hazard scan, same zerocopy_f64_binary_flat route) vs numpy.multiply measured beside divide in ONE invocation. worker=vmi1227854 elf 03fc30ebe05a6e94: multiply 0.931251 [0.921118,0.949075] excess 47191 ns, divide 0.736981 [0.710015,0.823791] excess 171476 ns, divide-specific share 72.5%, intervals disjoint. worker=vmi1153651 elf 2059a12e6f9c07e6: multiply 0.950794 [0.939180,0.962187] excess 87991 ns, divide 0.937033 [0.923034,0.944012] excess 96030 ns, divide-specific share 8.4%, intervals NOT disjoint. harness=common::run_dual_null_median_ci_contract, numpy 2.4.3, all four arms DECIDABLE_REGRESSION with nulls at unity. ESTABLISHED: the route loses on both hosts - a 5-7% floor paid by every fnp binary ufunc. NOT ESTABLISHED: the divide-specific increment (72.5% vs 8.4% is two measurements that disagree, banked as such rather than resolved by preferring the host that justifies a lever). Superseded by deadlock-audit-m7tti, which swept 256x of size and identified the mechanism as FIXED PER-CALL OVERHEAD with the kernel AT PARITY at 2^24 (ratio 1.001588, CI includes 1.0) - which means the divide-specific question is largely moot: at the size where the incumbent gap is largest, the gap is not kernel work at all.

title: perf: REDUCE THE WRAPPER FLOOR ITSELF - ~700-1450 ns of per-call cost that every delegating route pays, and the reason four separate levers were rejected
description:
NAMED SUCCESSOR TO deadlock-audit-zsn2y, whose central result was a LAW: a size floor only pays
where the native route costs several times the WRAPPER OWN delegation cost. That law shipped the
predicate gates (excess 3-150x the floor) and correctly rejected the unary floor, sum, mean, add,
multiply, divide and asarray - every one of them because its excess is at or below the floor
rather than because the route is fine.

SO THE FLOOR IS NOW THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THE WHOLE SMALL-n SURFACE. It is worth roughly
700-1450 ns per call on hz4 and it is what remains on these cells (hz4, numpy 2.5.2 live in the
same invocation, h2h_decompose seed 555, nulls clean, spreads 1.1-5.3%):

  sqrt n=64   +827 (1.993x)    abs n=64   +552 (1.689x)    isnan n=64 +397 (1.500x)
  mean n=64   +477 (1.092x)    sum n=64   +383 (1.126x)    divide n=64 +357 (1.412x)
  multiply    +295 (1.341x)    add n=64   +277 (1.319x)    asarray n=64 +20 (1.203x)
  concat n=64 +754 (1.589x)    sort n=64  +475 (1.241x)    argsort n=64 +468 (1.152x)

add excess is +270/+277/+315/+512 at n = 8/64/1024/16384 - FLAT, which is the diagnostic that it
is the chain and not the kernel.

WHAT THE FLOOR IS MADE OF, from the levers already landed against it (deadlock-audit-66w2d rounds
1-3 and this vein minmax ship), each of which removed a slice and none of which removed it all:
  - pyo3 signature handling for wrappers with 5-7 named parameters plus kwargs
  - the kwargs walk, which on some routes extracts each key into a heap-allocated Rust String
  - operand classification: numeric_operand_facts, now identity-first but still two getattrs
  - per-gate re-derivation of facts a cheaper read already settled - the recurring defect
  - the delegate tail: clone_py_kwargs building a PyDict, then a KEYWORD call into numpy even
    when the dict is empty (fixed for np.sum in 6f5e7131; the same shape is still present on
    other wrappers and is the cheapest remaining lead)
  - the delegate attribute lookup, now moved into the fallback on sum/min/max/argmin/argmax and
    concatenate but never swept across the rest of the surface

THREE CONCRETE STARTING POINTS, cheapest first:
  1. AUDIT THE EMPTY-KWARGS DELEGATE across every wrapper that builds a dict unconditionally.
     The np.sum fix is the template: guard on ABSENCE of every optional (never on an explicit
     None) and call positionally. Cheap, mechanical, each site worth ~100-200 ns.
  2. AUDIT THE HOISTED DELEGATE LOOKUP the same way - the numpy attribute resolved before any
     gate runs. Found and fixed on six wrappers so far by inspection, never swept.
  3. COUNTED ATTRIBUTION BY INSTRUCTION DIFF on one representative wrapper (fnp.add at n=8,
     +270 ns flat) to find what actually dominates rather than continuing to guess. This repo
     already regards instruction-diff attribution as its most reliable tool where wall-clock CIs
     cannot decide, and a 270 ns effect on an 870 ns call is exactly that case.

ACCEPTANCE: the flat per-call excess on add at n=8 drops by more than the +/-70 ns control floor
with tests green, or an honest null per attempt. Carry the untouched-route controls; the method
that made this vein claims decidable was six control routes moving less than the effect.

NOTE TO SELF ON TOOLING: br descriptions go through the shell. Backticks in them get executed.
Write these without backticks.
notes:
CROSS-REFERENCE FOUND AFTER THE FACT, and it both explains this bead first null and rewrites its
plan: deadlock-audit-call-shape-priced-25ns-lk8zb (owner ubuntu, IN_PROGRESS, acceptance already
satisfied per GoldSummit 2026-08-30). I wrote this bead without it. Read it before continuing.

WHAT IT ALREADY SETTLES, so it is not re-derived here:
  1. THE CALLING CONVENTION IS NOT THE FLOOR. Two pyfunctions with identical bodies differing only
     in declared signature: typed 40 ns vs varargs 60-71 ns. The (*args, **kwargs) shape is
     ~25 ns/call, sign replicated 3/3. Against the int64 n=256 sort route deficit of 326 ns that is
     under 8%, and buying it costs a Python-visible signature change with a real parity surface.
     DO NOT attempt it.
  2. THE ENTRY DECOMPOSES, and only partly. Median-domain, timer-netted:
       route 1909 = a.copy() 221 + output PyBuffer ~85 + kernel 1092 + entry ~511
       numpy 1583 = copy     221 +                     + kernel 1108 + entry ~254
     Identified entry pieces: calling convention ~25, dtype.char chain ~60, two structured-dtype
     probes ~40 each, len() ~10, exact-type gate ~10 = ~185 of ~511.
  3. *** THESE LEVERS CANNOT BE CERTIFIED ONE AT A TIME. *** Every identified piece is 1.3-4.2%
     against a ~1900 ns route, and the six-run envelope for that cell is 3.1-3.2%. Its instruction:
     land the BATCH behind ONE measurement, or skip the family. A batch of everything identified is
     ~185 ns = 9.7%, which IS decidable.
  4. COUNTED ATTRIBUTION (commit cfdc46a6) then corrected its own framing: netted per-call
     instructions numpy 17451 vs fnp 26941, and 7858 of the 9490 excess (82.8%) is in the
     COMPARISON KERNEL, not the entry. NumPy is running x86-simd-sort AVX2 there.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD. My first attempt attacked ONE sub-100 ns entry lever (the empty-kwargs
delegate) in isolation and got exactly the null lk8zb predicts - two post-change runs disagreeing
by 190 ns on a claimed 57 ns effect. That was avoidable by reading the board rather than only
br ready, which showed three items when thirty-one are open. THE PLAN IS REVISED:

  - STARTING POINTS 1 AND 2 ARE WITHDRAWN AS SEPARATE LEVERS. The empty-kwargs guard placed before
    clone_py_kwargs and the hoisted-delegate-lookup sweep are both real and both below the
    decidability threshold individually. They may only be landed as part of ONE batch, measured
    once, with six runs each side - lk8zb acceptance clause (a).
  - STARTING POINT 3 STANDS AND IS NOW THE ONLY ONE. Counted attribution by instruction diff, on a
    DELEGATING wrapper this time. lk8zb attributed a NATIVE sort route and found the kernel
    dominates; nobody has attributed a route that delegates, which is what every cell on this
    bead board does (add/multiply/divide/sqrt/abs at n=64 all end in numpy). The entry share there
    is 100% by construction, so the two findings are not in conflict and the delegating case is
    genuinely unmeasured.

ALSO NOT YET READ AND DIRECTLY RELEVANT: deadlock-audit-v46rn, unassigned - "every probe on the
delegating path fetches dtype for itself - 11 call sites, 140 ns". That is the delegating-path
twin of the attribution above and overlaps this bead squarely.

title: correctness: non-native byte order silently misread on 15 ops for >f8 and sort on >i8 - 798 zero-copy sites, 38 guards; one central PyBuffer guard
description: Silent wrong values on non-native byte order. HEAD cdylib (2026-09-02, python3.13, numpy 2.4.3): for `>f8` inputs 15 of 65 ops return WRONG values with no error (std->inf, max/min/argmax/argmin/nanmax, cumsum, cumprod, all, ...), `>i8` sort returns garbage, plus 7/6/3/3 wrong ops on >f4/>i4/>i2/>u8 and a histogram raise-parity gap. Mechanism: crates/fnp-python/src/lib.rs has 798 `PyBuffer::<T>::get` zero-copy sites in 423 functions but only 38 isnative/byteorder checks, and pyo3 0.28.3 `is_matching_endian` (buffer.rs:198-201) accepts a leading '>' on little-endian hosts, so a big-endian buffer passes the typed-buffer check and is read as native bytes. Fix must be central: a crate-local PyBuffer wrapper whose get() rejects non-native formats, shadowing the pyo3 import so all 798 sites are covered by one hand-written change, plus decline-not-raise at routes that propagate the error. Named probe: a conformance shard sweeping ops x big-endian dtypes on 64-element inputs with nan/inf/-0, asserting value AND raise parity vs numpy; reproduce with scratch step3b_followup.py against a fresh .so.
close_reason: Closed on cited evidence: (1) 3a632df7 crate-local PyBuffer shadow rejects non-native formats at all 798 typed-buffer sites; (2) dccb2904 entry-level delegation via ndarray_is_byteswapped for unique, the unary family, left/right shift, take, interp, cumsum, cumprod, all, isin, around/round, nan_to_num; (3) named probe crates/fnp-python/tests/conformance_byteorder.rs (522 cells over 11 big-endian dtypes, value AND raise parity) PASSES on worker vmi1227854 in two independent runs (shard_byteorder2.log 139s, shard_byteorder3.log 73s on the final tree). Rebuilt-cdylib sweep on thinkstation1 (python3.13, numpy 2.4.3) before the entry declines: >f8 wrong 15 -> 1, >f4 7 -> 1, >i8 7 -> 1. Residual outside this class: interp and f32 cumsum differ from numpy by 1 ulp on native input too (numeric order), tracked in deadlock-audit-7evbk. The 77 '?'-propagating typed-buffer sites are no longer reachable with non-native input on the swept ops; any op outside the 522-cell matrix that still reaches one raises BufferError rather than answering wrong.

(2) Named probe written: crates/fnp-python/tests/conformance_byteorder.rs (522 cells, in-process, value AND raise parity). PER-CALL EXCESS OVER numpy, ns (before -> after levers A-D -> after the sort hoist):

  concat n=64      +1825.2 -> +800.9 -> +778.0    -1047   2.417x -> 1.611x
  concat n=16384   +2130.5 -> +938.0 -> +796.8    -1334   1.236x -> 1.087x
  sort n=1024      +2257.5 -> +1935.1 -> +1671.4   -586   1.278x -> 1.209x
  sort n=64        +2076.4 -> +1797.8 -> +1614.4   -462   2.040x -> 1.813x
  max n=64          +645.4 -> +488.8 -> +417.5     -228   1.214x -> 1.142x
  abs n=64          +718.2 -> +539.7 -> +515.6     -203   1.866x -> 1.641x

Every one of these exceeds the +/-40 ns control floor; concat n=64 exceeds it 26x. mean (+44) and

FIVE LEVERS, each a substitution already measured elsewhere in this codebase:
  A. numeric_operand_facts answers (kind, itemsize) by IDENTITY against NumPy's interned float64

title: perf(arccosh/arcsin/arccos): ONE out-of-domain element flips an 11x WIN into a loss - the sqrt pay-twice deferral again, in the shared transcendental helper
description:
MEASURED, TanBridge, thinkstation1, numpy 2.4.3 live, fnp .so sha256
6f3462cb03511d6edaa2799e5b5c6d27e20dc2cac8ef4fc34cc7fcaef0fecdb7 (at 300c5d17).

FOLLOW-UP to deadlock-audit-f1mj2 (sqrt), same defect class, different helper.

## THE CELL

`acosh[f64]` / `arccosh[f64]` are sweep ranks 6-7 at 2.12x / 2.09x - the largest ABSOLUTE headroom
left on the board (~480 us). As with sqrt, the ratio is an operand artifact and the sweep's
operand is the pathological one: its `f64` ladder entry is `rng.standard_normal(N)`, of which only
**15.7%** is inside acosh's domain (x >= 1).

```
  operand                        numpy_ns       fnp_ns   ratio
  in-domain x>=1                  957596.3      87078.1   0.09x   <- an 11x WIN
  in-domain + ONE bad element     981251.8    1498837.4   1.53x   LOSS
  standard_normal (84% NaN)       420954.8    1270799.4   3.02x   LOSS
```

**ONE out-of-domain element in 65536 flips an 11x win into a loss - a 17x swing.** Binary trigger,
exactly like sqrt.

## MECHANISM - THE SAME PAY-TWICE DEFERRAL, IN A SHARED HELPER

`transcendental_map_f64` computes the WHOLE output while tracking an `event` predicate, returns
false if it fired, and the caller does `return Ok(None)` - discarding a completed correct buffer so
a fallback can record NumPy's FP event.

## WHY THIS CANNOT BE FIXED FOR THE WHOLE FAMILY AT ONCE

The helper serves ~15 ops and their event predicates do not all have ONE category. Probed against
numpy 2.4.3, per op, over inputs exercising the whole domain:

```
  arccosh   {invalid}                  <- single category
  arcsin    {invalid}                  <- single category
  arccos    {invalid}                  <- single category
  arctanh   {invalid, divide}          <- BOTH, and arctanh([1.0, 2.0]) raises both in ONE call
  log       {invalid, divide}          <- BOTH, log([0.0, -1.0]) raises both
  exp       {over, under}              <- BOTH, exp([1000, -1000]) raises both
```

A one-element witness reproduces exactly ONE category, so for arctanh/log/exp it would
UNDER-REPORT. Those must keep deferring. Only arccosh/arcsin/arccos can take the sqrt fix, and for
them a single witness is provably complete.

## AND THE PREDICATES HAVE THE SAME `is_finite()` HOLE sqrt HAD - 5 LIVE DIVERGENCES

    Arcsin/Arccos:  |value, _| value.is_finite() && value.abs() > 1.0
    Arccosh:        |value, _| value.is_finite() && value < 1.0

NumPy's invalid set does not exclude the infinities. Measured on the shipped .so:

```
  arccosh(-inf)   numpy warns, fnp silent
  arcsin(-inf)    numpy warns, fnp silent
  arcsin(+inf)    numpy warns, fnp silent
  arccos(-inf)    numpy warns, fnp silent
  arccos(+inf)    numpy warns, fnp silent
```

Correct predicates drop `is_finite()`: `v < 1.0` for arccosh and `v.abs() > 1.0` for arcsin/arccos.
IEEE already excludes NaN (every comparison against NaN is false), and arccosh(+inf) is +inf with
no event, which `v < 1.0` correctly does not flag.

## THE FIX

Keep the buffer, borrow only the event - a one-element call of the SAME numpy ufunc on an
out-of-domain witness (arccosh 0.0, arcsin/arccos 2.0), then return the natively computed array.
Priced for sqrt at 179.6 ns against 67925.8 ns to re-run the array. arctanh/log/exp keep the
`Ok(None)` deferral untouched.

## ACCEPTANCE

Dual-null contract vs numpy live in the same invocation on the IN-DOMAIN operand (where the win
lives) AND on a one-bad-element operand (where the loss lived), plus an errstate probe over
warn/raise/ignore x {finite out-of-domain, -inf, +inf, NaN, in-domain} for all three ops, asserting
the multi-category ops are UNCHANGED.
close_reason: SHIPPED 023c66ff, banked d58b7a4a. Applied the sqrt keep-the-buffer/borrow-the-event pattern to arccosh/arcsin/arccos only - the three ops whose event predicate has ONE errstate category, per a measured table (arctanh/log/exp raise TWO from a single call and would under-report, so they keep deferring). Headline: the ONE-out-of-domain-element cell goes 1.53x LOSS -> 0.09-0.35x WIN at every thread count above 1. Contract on the sweep operand: DECIDABLE_WIN 2.537597x [2.270379,2.682593] at RAYON=16; UNDECIDED at 64, where the candidate arm swings 444774->1041912 ns between runs while numpy holds ~455000 - both regimes banked, the 64-thread regression is NOT quoted because it does not replicate. Also closed 5 is_finite() FP-event divergences (arccosh -inf, arcsin/arccos +-inf). Voided one of my own rows: an 'all out-of-domain' constant-array cell is not representative. Follow-up deadlock-audit-kaa5i filed for arctanh/log -inf event counts.

1. mean / std / var have the IDENTICAL keepdims defect and still RAISE TypeError on np.matrix. Recipe: change 'keepdims: bool' to 'Option<bool>' in the #[pyo3(signature)], add 'let keepdims_effective = keepdims.unwrap_or(false);' for the native paths, and guard the delegate's set_item with 'if let Some(k) = keepdims'. std/var additionally carry ddof, so each needs its own parity run over its own kwarg surface - do NOT bundle them.

Test 'np.f(np.matrix(a), param=<default>)' against 'np.f(np.matrix(a))' - if they differ, the signature needs Option<T>.

ALL FOUR HARD FAILURES NOW CLOSED. std+var shipped aa76d46d (ledger banked), after sum 7ff307e5 and mean 93da5185. Parity 2 -> 0 on each of the four, probed separately. Perf unchanged everywhere - std/var were already 0.08x-0.60x WINs and stayed there; sum f64 2^8 1.478x -> 1.376x; mean unchanged.

Their own keepdims is already Option<bool>, so collapsing it there would have re-introduced the identical defect one call deeper - where no probe of std or var could see it, because the probe never enters through nanstd. A sentinel must be preserved along the WHOLE delegation chain, not just at the entry that gets probed. Check every internal forwarder when doing the remaining work.

elf ee2a004e6593... -> afc8ff077d7f...

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THREE-STATE FIX SHIPPED 2f37927f + ledger ca337bf5. The Option<bool> recipe in this bead's earlier comment is SUPERSEDED and was WRONG in a second way: pyo3 maps BOTH an absent argument and an explicit keepdims=None onto None, so fnp.sum(a, keepdims=None) returned a value where numpy raises. Two states cannot encode three.

USE KeepdimsArg{NotGiven, Native(bool), Delegate(Py<PyAny>)} with from_py_with, on the DdofArg pattern already in lib.rs. Parser MUST be cast_exact::<PyBool>, NOT extract::<bool>(): extract also accepts np.True_ and anything with __bool__, numpy does not - that ONE line was 285 of the 346 divergences left after the rest of the fix.

DONE: sum, mean, std, var, prod, min, max, any, all, amin, amax, nanmin, nanmax, nanprod, nanstd, nanvar. nanstd/nanvar pass the THREE-STATE value into py_std/var; collapsing before that reroute is the one-call-deeper defect.

title: [perf][fnp-python] measure fnp.remainder vs numpy.remainder above the 2^21 parallel threshold - the route exists because numpy is single-threaded there
description:
numpy has ONE banked vs-incumbent row this campaign (divide, a replicated loss). This picks the op most likely to be a WIN and finishes it either way.

WHY REMAINDER: the f64 binop fast-path set in PyUFunc::__call__ admits Remainder, Power, Maximum, Minimum and Div, and the source says why - numpy runs floored-mod single-threaded and it is compute-heavy (fmod + floor + correction per element). Our route parallelizes it. Unlike divide, remainder has no FE-hazard scan on the hot path; it defers wholesale on a zero divisor, which our operands never produce (b = 1.25 + (i%997)/997 is never 0).

THE SIZE MATTERS AND IS THE WHOLE POINT: parallel_min for Remainder is 1<<21. Below that we take the SERIAL native path and the parallel win cannot appear. Every previous elementwise row in this ledger measured at 2^20 or smaller, i.e. strictly below the threshold, which is why no remainder row exists. Measure at n=2^21.

Deadlock-audit-m7tti/isnd2 established that our per-call floor (~7-8 us) is amortised to nothing by 2^24 and is ~5% at 2^20, so at 2^21 the wrapper is not what decides this - the kernel is.

Acceptance: fnp.remainder vs numpy.remainder under the dual-null contract, both arms in ONE invocation, naming WORKER and HARNESS and the ELF sha, replicated across two runs. Bank the row whichever way it goes; a loss here would say the parallel route does not pay even where it was designed to, which is worth more than another unmeasured assumption.
close_reason: INCUMBENT-WIN BANKED in 97ad0c96, group in e7279f11. fnp.remainder beats numpy.remainder at n=2^21: four runs, TWO workers, all DECIDABLE_WIN, every run carrying both A/A nulls with all on unity. harness=common::run_dual_null_median_ci_contract, numpy 2.4.3, profile release via cargo test --release --bench. worker=vmi1227854 elf 4dc56b7ba6adfea2 ratio 2.642599 ci95=[2.560861,2.785726]; worker=vmi1227854 elf d34d3e580ed79253 ratio 2.738191 ci95=[2.626320,2.823174]; worker=vmi1227854 elf 05aa169215b813f2 ratio 2.950744 ci95=[2.871684,3.073150]; worker=vmi1153651 elf 99d45b3fe7d5b858 ratio 1.299521 ci95=[1.121225,1.381368]. QUOTED AT THE WORST BOUND 1.121225x and NOT pooled - on vmi1153651 both arms were slower (numpy 19.5ms vs 13.6-14.1, ours 15.6 vs 4.7-5.3), our parallel arm degrading ~3x where numpy's single-threaded arm degraded ~1.4x, so the magnitude is worker-scoped even though direction and verdict replicate. The acceptance's key point held: n=2^21 is load-bearing because parallel_min for Remainder is exactly 1<<21, and every earlier elementwise row in this ledger measured at 2^20 or below, strictly under the threshold - which is why no remainder row existed despite the route being built for this op. Full incumbent-win contract satisfied: NumPy's own artifact hashed from inside the measuring process (artifact_sha256=2e0027bba6fda9e61d8e57aa53a1636ede5a6a9fd8ece76b08625d7da1e15d48, distinct from our ELF), shared invocation_id, isolation proof naming distinct fnp.remainder/numpy.remainder arms, dispatch asserted at runtime, cross-arm checksums compared before timing and every round.

title: [bug][fnp-python] importing fnp_python POLLUTES numpy.__all__ (shared list + PyO3 add), breaking 'from numpy import *' and scipy
description:
FOUND by CoralOak 2026-08-08 running the xdyx7 shard set at cb0f84c4 on ovh-a. This is a NEW red,
not one of the original 18, and it is the most consequential thing I have seen in this sweep:
importing fnp_python CORRUPTS the real numpy module in the same interpreter.

THE SYMPTOM. conformance_linalg_advanced::solve_triangular_complex fails on ovh-a with

  AttributeError: module 'numpy' has no attribute '__submodule_import_errors__'

raised from numpy/__init__.py:792 __getattr__, inside scipy:
  scipy/_lib/array_api_compat/numpy/__init__.py:9   __all__ = clone_module("numpy", globals())
  scipy/_lib/array_api_compat/_internal.py:64       exec(f"from {mod.__name__} import *", objs)
So `from numpy import *` asked numpy for a name that only WE define. The test script imports
fnp_python first and scipy second, which is what makes the order visible.

THE MECHANISM, which is two innocuous things multiplying:
  1. crates/fnp-python/src/lib.rs:106940 does
         if let Ok(all_names) = numpy.getattr("__all__") { m.setattr("__all__", all_names)?; }
     That binds NUMPY'S OWN LIST OBJECT to fnp's __all__. Not a copy - the same list.
  2. PyO3's PyModule::add appends the added name to the module's __all__.
So every m.add(...) after line 106941 appends an fnp name to numpy.__all__. Most are duplicates of
names numpy already has, which is why nothing noticed; but the fnp-only ones - starting with
__submodule_import_errors__, added at lib.rs:107393 - are names numpy cannot resolve. Any
`from numpy import *` in the same process then raises. That is not a test-only problem: it breaks
scipy, and it would break any downstream library doing a star-import, in any program that imports
fnp_python.

WHY IT SURFACED NOW rather than earlier: it needs BOTH a star-import consumer in the process AND
an fnp-only name in __all__. scipy is newly present on ovh-a (site-packages for python3.13; the
o1p3g closure recorded scipy as absent from every worker checked on 2026-08-06), and
__submodule_import_errors__ was added by commit 3756a66f on 2026-08-06. The two met for the first
time on this run.

THE FIX is one line - bind a COPY, e.g. all_names.call_method0("copy") - plus a test. But the test
is the point, and it should assert the SYMPTOM, not the mechanism:
  - `fnp.__all__ is not numpy.__all__` catches the aliasing directly, and
  - after importing fnp, `exec("from numpy import *", {})` must still succeed - that is the
    contract downstream code actually depends on, and it stays true even if someone later changes
    how __all__ is populated.
Assert both; the second is the one that cannot be satisfied vacuously.

ALSO CHECK while in there: the same setattr-numpy's-list pattern appears for the submodules -
lib.rs:106013 (random), 106110 (polynomial), 107108 (fft), 107240 (linalg), 107637 (ma) all do
`getattr("__all__")` then `setattr("__all__", ...)` with a `.clone()` of the HANDLE, which in PyO3
is still the same Python object. Each of those submodule objects is OURS, so appending to a shared
list would pollute numpy.random.__all__, numpy.linalg.__all__ and so on the same way. Verify
whether PyO3's add is used on those modules after the aliasing, and copy there too if so.

PROBE TO CLOSE: `cargo test -p fnp-python --no-fail-fast --test conformance_linalg_advanced` green
on a worker that HAS scipy (ovh-a does), plus the new star-import test passing. Cite the worker.
Note conformance_linalg_advanced's solve_triangular_complex is currently the only test in the crate
that imports scipy, so it is the canary - do not treat its green as coverage of the star-import
contract, which is why the dedicated test is required.
close_reason: FIXED in commit 57ab8d1f: copied_all_names binds a fresh list at all five sites and the top-level bind moved after the last PyO3 add. Negative control on ovh-a reproduces the exact scipy AttributeError pre-fix (shared across all 5 modules, 133 names leaked into numpy.__all__) and all four assertions pass at the fix. Side effect worth reading: this un-tautologised fnp_python_top_level_all_matches_numpy_verbatim, which was comparing a list with itself. Not verified: a post-fix run on ovh-a specifically (the only scipy host) - the cause is directly verified, the scipy consequence is not. Details in the preceding comment.

comments.author: CoralOak
comments.text:
FIXED by CoralOak 2026-08-08 in commit 57ab8d1f, with a negative control against the pre-fix build.

THE DIAGNOSIS IN THIS BEAD HELD, and the measurement extended it in two directions.

ALL FIVE MODULES WERE SHARING, not just the top level. The pre-fix run reported
shared=['fnp', 'fnp.random', 'fnp.linalg', 'fnp.fft', 'fnp.ma']. The bead flagged the submodules as
"also check"; they were all affected. `.clone()` on a Bound clones the HANDLE, so the four sites
that looked defensive were not. copied_all_names builds a fresh list and every site uses it.

THE DAMAGE WAS BIGGER THAN THE ONE NAME. Against a clean-interpreter baseline the pre-fix build
appended 133 entries to numpy.__all__, of which two are names numpy cannot resolve:
__submodule_import_errors__ and matrixlib. The rest are duplicates of names numpy already exports,
which is why this survived so long - the list looked plausible.

THE TOP-LEVEL BIND ALSO MOVED to the end of module init, after the last add. Copying alone stops
the corruption but leaves fnp.__all__ carrying those two fnp-only names, because PyO3 keeps
appending to whatever list is bound. Binding last makes fnp.__all__ exactly numpy's.

AND THAT MOVE FIXED A TAUTOLOGICAL TEST, which is the part worth carrying forward.
fnp_python_top_level_all_matches_numpy_verbatim asserts fnp.__all__ equals numpy.__all__ - and
while the two were the same object it was comparing a list with itself and COULD NOT FAIL. The
copy made it fail honestly for the first time (extra=['__submodule_import_errors__', 'matrixlib']);
binding last made it pass on a real comparison. A green verbatim test proved nothing for as long as
the aliasing existed.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, pre-fix src with only the tests overlaid, ovh-a:
  star-import  AttributeError: module 'numpy' has no attribute '__submodule_import_errors__'
  shared       ['fnp', 'fnp.random', 'fnp.linalg', 'fnp.fft', 'fnp.ma']
  leaked       ['__submodule_import_errors__', 'matrixlib']
  delta        133
All four assertions fire. At the fix they all pass.

I HAD TO FIX MY OWN TEST FIRST, and it is the same class of defect this bead is about. The first
draft snapshotted np.__all__ at the top of a script that has ALREADY imported fnp, so the leak
baseline was the corrupted list compared with itself: it printed leaked=[] and delta=0 in the very
run whose star-import assertion was failing. Two of four assertions were structurally unable to
fail, and I only caught it because I ran the negative control and read the numbers rather than the
verdict. The baseline now comes from a subprocess that never loads fnp. The star-import assertion
is the load-bearing one either way: it pins the contract downstream code depends on rather than
today's mechanism.

EVIDENCE AT THE FIX, --no-fail-fast, whole invocation exit 0:
  vmi1149989  six shards: conformance_module_metadata, conformance_remaining_top_level_attrs,
              conformance_linalg_advanced, conformance_submodule_reexports,
              conformance_strings_namespace, conformance_statistics
  vmi1149989  at committed HEAD 57ab8d1f: linalg_advanced 33/0, module_metadata 6/0,
              remaining_top_level_attrs 13/0
  hz2         at committed HEAD 57ab8d1f: linalg_advanced 33/0, module_metadata 6/0
Gates: clippy -p fnp-python --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings exit 0 on hz2 with the log showing
'Checking fnp-python'; cargo fmt --check exit 0.

WHAT I DID NOT GET, stated plainly: I never landed a POST-fix run on ovh-a, the one worker known to
have scipy, so the scipy import itself has not been observed succeeding after the fix - rch worker
selection cannot be pinned for this repo. What IS directly verified is the cause: the star-import
that scipy performs failed pre-fix and passes post-fix, and that assertion needs no scipy. The
scipy failure was a consequence of it. Anyone landing on ovh-a should confirm the consequence too;
conformance_linalg_advanced is the canary because solve_triangular_complex is the only scipy
importer in the crate.

comments.text: GAP CLOSED, same day. My closure said the scipy CONSEQUENCE was unverified because I never landed a post-fix run on ovh-a, the only worker known to have scipy. A later xdyx7 shard sweep at 6f8c3791 DID land on ovh-a: conformance_linalg_advanced 33 passed / 0 failed, i.e. solve_triangular_complex imports scipy.linalg successfully on the host where it was raising 'module numpy has no attribute __submodule_import_errors__' before the fix. Cause and consequence are now both verified on the same worker. conformance_module_metadata 6/0 and conformance_remaining_top_level_attrs 13/0 in the same invocation.

comments.author: CoralOak
comments.text:
FOLLOW-UP DEFECT FROM THIS FIX, found and fixed the same day: deadlock-audit-wolfm.

Copying numpy's __all__ was right, but I only moved the BIND to the end of module init for the TOP-LEVEL module, not for the submodules. fnp.ma binds its __all__ before a loop that still calls ma.add(...), and PyO3's add appends to __all__, so fnp.ma.__all__ ended up carrying names numpy.ma does not export. ma_core_classes_constants_helpers_match_numpy_oracles went red.

That test had only ever passed because the two were the SAME list object - it was comparing an object with itself. So this is the THIRD tautological comparison this work has un-masked (top-level verbatim __all__, this one, and the leak baseline in my own new test). Each one is an argument for the copy, not against it: they were all incapable of failing before.

Fixed in 17a86a50 by binding after the last add. ma was the only submodule affected - random, polynomial, linalg and fft have no add after their bind.

My closure above says the fix was verified by six shards plus targeted runs. Those were all --test targets, which never build the lib harness, so none of them could have caught this. If I had run --lib in the same breath the regression would have surfaced immediately.

title: [bug][fnp-random] binomial BTPE arm (n*p > 30) desyncs from numpy's stream on the 5th draw - 4 of 4 BTPE parameter sets diverge
close_reason:
FIXED. Root cause: binomial_btpe fell through to the acceptance test on the u <= p1 path, where numpy's Step10 does 'goto Step60' and ACCEPTS IMMEDIATELY. The triangular-region candidate needs no squeeze and no explicit evaluation; running one anyway rejected draws numpy keeps, consumed an extra u/v pair, and slid the whole stream by one variate - which is exactly the signature the sweep reported (first four draws identical, numpy's fifth value missing from ours, everything after shifted left by one).

FOUR corrections landed, all transcription deviations from numpy's distributions.c, found by reading it line by line rather than from memory - two of my recollections were wrong and the vendored source corrected them:
  1. u <= p1 must accept immediately (THE root cause; without it the other three change nothing on these parameters)
  2. squeeze arm selection: numpy takes Step52 iff (k > 20 && k < nrq/2 - 1) and evaluates explicitly otherwise. Ours took explicit iff (k <= 20 && k <= nrq/2 - 1), which is not the negation - it sent k <= 20 && k > nrq/2 - 1 to the squeeze.
  3. final Stirling correction: numpy uses the four-term high-order series (13680/462/132/99/140 over 166320); ours used a first-order (1/12)(1/f1 + 1/z - 1/x1 - 1/w), a different acceptance boundary.
  4. fm = n*r + r, not (n+1)*r. Algebraically identical, different in the last bit (101*0.4 = 40.400000000000006 vs 100*0.4 + 0.4 = 40.4), and fm feeds laml/lamr and hence p3/p4, so it moves a branch threshold.
Corrections 2-4 were not exercised by these seven parameter sets but are real divergences that would surface elsewhere; they are fixed rather than left for the next person to rediscover.

ACCEPTANCE TEST MET: all four BTPE sets - (100,0.4), (62,0.5), (100,0.6), (100,0.5) - are back in poisson_binomial_boundary_sweep_matches_live_numpy_oracle and pass, alongside the three inversion sets and poisson across its lam=10 switch. Draw count raised from 12 to 40 per set so a later desync cannot hide behind a short sequence; integers compare exactly, so a single differing draw fails.

VERIFIED: timeout cargo test -p fnp-random --lib = 444 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored - including the pre-existing binomial_matches_live_numpy_oracle, oracle_binomial and binomial_supports_trials_above_i64_max, so the four corrections did not disturb what already worked; cargo clippy -p fnp-random --all-targets -- -D warnings = clean; cargo fmt --check exit 0 run UNPIPED.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FOUND by poisson_binomial_boundary_sweep_matches_live_numpy_oracle (CreamGlen, 2026-08-09), added under jo22s. Generator::from_pcg64_dxsm(12345), size=12, compared against numpy.random.Generator(PCG64DXSM(12345)).binomial.

EVERY BTPE PARAMETER SET DIVERGES; EVERY INVERSION SET PASSES. Our binomial takes inversion when n*p <= 30.0 and BTPE above (lib.rs:5216/5223, mirroring numpy's distributions.c). Results:
  PASS  (50, 0.1)  np=5    inversion
  PASS  (60, 0.5)  np=30   inversion (exactly on the threshold)
  PASS  (50, 0.9)  nq=5    inversion via the p>0.5 mirror
  FAIL  (100, 0.4) np=40   BTPE
  FAIL  (62,  0.5) np=31   BTPE (one past the threshold)
  FAIL  (100, 0.6) nq=40   BTPE via the p>0.5 mirror
  FAIL  (100, 0.5) np=50   BTPE

THE SHAPE OF THE DIVERGENCE IS THE DIAGNOSIS. In all four failures the first FOUR draws match exactly, then numpy emits one value we never produce, and everything after is our stream shifted left by one:
  (100, 0.4)  ours  [51, 41, 34, 44,     43, 42, 39, 45, 33, 39, 44, 39]
              numpy [51, 41, 34, 44, 35, 43, 42, 39, 45, 33, 39, 44]
  (62, 0.5)   numpy's missing 5th value is 27
  (100, 0.6)  numpy's missing 5th value is 65
  (100, 0.5)  numpy's missing 5th value is 44
So this is not a wrong VALUE, it is a wrong number of uniforms CONSUMED: on that draw numpy's BTPE takes a rejection path we do not (or vice versa), the stream desyncs by one variate, and every subsequent draw is numpy's next one. That is why the values still look plausible - they are numpy's own numbers, one position early.

SEVERITY P1: binomial with n*p > 30 is an ordinary parameter range, and any user relying on reproducible streams gets numpy's sequence off by one from the fifth draw. It is invisible to distributional tests and to any fixed-parameter test that draws fewer than five values or uses np <= 30 - which is why the existing suite missed it.

WHERE TO LOOK: binomial_btpe at lib.rs:5234, against random_binomial_btpe() in numpy's distributions.c. The consistent position (5th draw, all four sets) points at one specific acceptance/rejection branch rather than a general formula error - most likely a step where numpy draws an extra uniform before rejecting, or the squeeze/explicit-evaluation split near the end of the loop.

NOT FIXED HERE. The landed test asserts poisson across its lam=10 switch and the three inversion binomials, all of which pass; the four BTPE sets are listed in the test as excluded pending this bead, so the sweep runs green on main without pinning wrong behaviour as correct.

title: [bug][fnp-python] dstack/column_stack raise AttributeError on lists of Python lists where numpy returns an array
description:
FOUND by CoralOak 2026-08-08 running the full fnp-python suite at cb0f84c4. NOT one of the original
18 xdyx7 failures and not in any of its five clusters - a separate parity defect that the sweep
turned up.

FAILING TEST: stack_helpers_python_container_and_keyword_surfaces_match_numpy,
crates/fnp-python/tests/conformance_stack.rs:137.

WHAT IT REPORTS, verbatim from the run:
  dstack one dimensional lists
    fnp    ('err', 'AttributeError')
    numpy  ('ok', ('int64', (1, 3, 2), [[[1, 4], [2, 5], [3, 6]]]))
  column_stack one dimensional lists
    fnp    ('err', 'AttributeError')
    numpy  ('ok', ('int64', (3, 2), [[1, 4], [2, 5], [3, 6]]))
So fnp.dstack and fnp.column_stack raise AttributeError on a sequence of plain Python LISTS where
numpy returns an array. Both numpy answers are ordinary - this is not an edge case, it is the
documented behaviour of passing lists instead of arrays.

REPRODUCED ON TWO WORKERS, so it is not host luck: vmi1149989 and ovh-a, both at cb0f84c4, both
at or above the numpy 2.3 oracle floor (ovh-a passes numpy_oracle_meets_the_supported_version_floor
on this run - its numpy has been upgraded since keqog's fleet table was written, so do not trust
that table for ovh-a any more).

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not diagnose which attribute is missing. AttributeError with a
list-of-lists input smells like the implementation reaching for .ndim or .shape on the argument
before converting it with asarray/atleast_*, which would make it a missing normalisation at the
entry point rather than anything wrong with the stacking itself - but that is a hypothesis from the
exception TYPE alone and it must be checked, not assumed. Print the actual message first; the test
only captures the exception class.

WORTH CHECKING TOGETHER: the sibling helpers in the same family (hstack, vstack, row_stack, stack)
either do not have this problem or are not covered by the same case - the test named only dstack
and column_stack. Determine which, because "two of five helpers forgot to normalise" and "the test
only exercises two of five" are different sizes of bug.

PROBE TO CLOSE: 'cargo test -p fnp-python --no-fail-fast --test conformance_stack' green, citing
worker and numpy version, plus whatever new cases the sibling audit above justifies.
close_reason: FIXED in commit fba39a5d. Root cause: try_native_column_interleave read items[0].getattr('dtype') before checking the item was an ndarray, so an AttributeError escaped a probe whose contract is to decline and defer. ONE PROBE, THREE DOORS - dstack, column_stack AND stack(axis=1) share it, and the test covered two; vstack/hstack type-check inside their is_nd closure and row_stack delegates, so those were never affected. Negative control on ovh-a: 4 of 5 container cases fail pre-fix (including the previously untested stack axis=1 door) and pass at the fix. The 5th, 'dstack mixed ndarray then list', passed pre-fix - with an ndarray first the unguarded read succeeds and the loop declined correctly, so both mixed orders are kept to pin that asymmetry against a narrower items[0]-only fix. Evidence: conformance_stack 27 passed / 0 failed on vmi1152480 (numpy 2.4.x), was 26/1; module_metadata 6/0 and statistics 30/0 in the same invocation. clippy -D warnings exit 0 on hz2 with 'Checking fnp-python' in the log; fmt --check exit 0.

title: [bug][bench] DIVIDE_ROUTE_SHARE divides a MEDIAN kernel by a BEST-OF-24 end-to-end, inflating every published kernel_share
description:
report_divide_route_share in crates/fnp-python/benches/criterion_python_elementwise.rs computes kernel_share = kernel_ns / end_to_end_ns where kernel_ns is the median-CI contract's arm median (effect.arm_b_median_ns) but end_to_end_ns is best = best.min(..) over 24 rounds. Dividing a median by a best-of understates the denominator, so the published share is systematically OVERSTATED - by more the noisier the host.

Observed 2026-08-15 on host=vmi1293453 (elf 6068494b77e0f00c...): the serial arm printed kernel_share=1.473, i.e. the kernel supposedly costs 147% of the whole call that contains it. That is arithmetically impossible as a share and is what exposed the mismatch. The same run printed fused_parallel kernel_share=0.620.

This matters because the repo treats the share as the guard against quoting a kernel-only ratio as an end-to-end one ('a kernel ratio without its share is a FRAME % masquerading as a REMOVABLE %'). An inflated share makes kernel levers look MORE impactful than they are. Every previously banked share from this harness is affected, including deadlock-audit-jw7vk's serial kernel_share=0.941 (vmi1293453) / 0.615 (hz1) and parallel 0.601.

Acceptance: end_to_end uses the SAME statistic as kernel_ns (median of the collected samples, not best-of), the line states which statistic it is, and a negative case pins that a share above 1.0 is impossible for a kernel strictly inside the timed call. Re-read the jw7vk shares under the corrected statistic and note the correction in the ledger row rather than silently restating them.
close_reason: Fixed in 50c39a4e (median/median) and pinned by a test in 1eca8759 that runs at the head of every divide group; the negative case is a right-skewed sample set where a best-of denominator returns 100 instead of the 115 median and inflates the share 15%. Executed green on rch worker vmi1293453, elf 0abb2ecf05717f8d7857a27a9ccf571c5ea19f6e2da1ddec6a839d5969535534, harness common::run_median_ci_contract (BENCH_GROUP_SELECTION selected_groups=1 then the group reached its MEDIAN_CI_GATE line, which it only does after the assertion returns). NOT closed as 'the share is now trustworthy': the acceptance line about re-reading jw7vk's shares under the corrected statistic is SUPERSEDED by deadlock-audit-c9rn8, which found the share also ratios two NON-INTERLEAVED phases and swings 0.804-1.911 on one worker. Re-reading old shares under a statistic that is still not comparable would be wasted work; c9rn8 carries that.
