CAVEAT ON MY OWN 21.2 us RESIDUAL, and a build-free negative result (2026-08-24, AmberFalcon swarm). No code change; no build run - disk at 81G and heavy builds barred this window.

THE CAVEAT, recorded so the next agent does not over-trust the number I banked in 55cd6b1c. The profile computes `entry_residual = route - kernel`, where `kernel` is MY REPLICA of the shipped loop (a monomorphic `BinaryOp::Maximum` over the same numpy-allocated buffers). That subtraction is only an entry cost if the replica is what the route actually runs. If the route's kernel differs from my model - a second pass, a different loop shape, an extra touch of the output - then part of the 21220 ns is mis-attributed to "entry" when it is really kernel work I failed to replicate.

Why I flag it rather than assert the attribution: 21.2 us is a LOT for a dispatch path. Attribute lookups run ~100 ns, three PyBuffer acquisitions are of that order too, so a handful of them cannot reach 21 us. Either something on the entry path is much more expensive than an attribute read, or the replica is not the loop that ships. Both are live and this bench cannot separate them.

BUILD-FREE NEGATIVE RESULT that narrows it slightly: I looked for an O(n) scan hiding on the `out=` binary entry path, since 21.2 us at n=2^20 has roughly the shape of a partial pass (about 13% of one 8 MiB traversal). The `zero_divisor` buffer scan in that region is gated `matches!(op, BinaryOp::Remainder)`, so `Maximum` does not pay it. No other whole-buffer scan is reachable before the kernel on this path. So the residual is NOT explained by an obvious extra pass, which makes "the replica is not the shipped loop" the more likely of the two explanations and is the first thing to check.

HOW TO SETTLE IT, when a build window opens: disassemble the shipped route and confirm whether the loop it runs matches the replica - the same nm/objdump method that settled the `zerocopy_f64_binary_flat_with_out` dispatch question earlier in this campaign (one symbol, no per-op specialisation, a `call` per element). If the loops match, the 21.2 us is genuinely entry and the PyBuffer-first restructure is the lever. If they do not, the residual needs re-attributing before any lever is chosen.

=====================================================================
The 2.5-instruction gap had a specific candidate. Our select is vcmpunordpd + vcmpltpd +
vorpd + vblendvpd - FOUR ops per vector - where NumPy appears to use a max plus a NaN
blend, THREE. And `if lhs > rhs { lhs } else { rhs }` is x86 `vmaxpd` semantics exactly:
that instruction returns its second source when the operands are unordered or equal, which
is why ties yield `rhs` and signed zeros stay correct. So I split the kernel into the max
and its lhs-NaN fix-up, expecting vmaxpd + vcmpunordpd + vblendvpd.

the identical form. Folding a float `a > b ? a : b` into `maxpd` is only legal under
fast-math, because the two differ precisely on NaN and signed zero - the two things this op
exists to preserve. Reverted; the shipped expression is byte-identical to before, and the
only thing that landed is the negative result written at the kernel so nobody spends
another build cycle on it.

NaN/signed-zero test both passed on the attempt and on the revert.

title: [perf][fnp-linalg] TSQR-based lstsq: implement tsqr_qtb + wire lstsq for full-rank tall-skinny f64
description: Discharges the .370 BLOCKER retry predicate (the sign-invariant reachable win from the shipped TSQR kernel). tsqr_r (crates/fnp-linalg/src/lib.rs:2877) computes ONLY R via parallel leaf_r + sequential pairwise combine_r fold (deterministic, allclose to dgeqrf). lstsq for FULL-RANK tall-skinny A (m>=n) is x = R^-1 Q^T b, which is UNIQUE regardless of the Q/R sign choice (so no numpy sign-divergence, unlike qr(mode=r) which is parity-fatal per .370). PLAN: (1) implement tsqr_qtb(a,b,m,n)->(R,Qtb): each leaf does Householder QR on its row block AND applies the same reflector sequence to the matching block of b, keeping the top-n transformed b; the fold stacks paired R factors AND the paired b-components and re-reduces, carrying Qtb up the SAME deterministic binary tree as tsqr_r (reuse leaf_r/combine_r structure, extended to transform b). (2) x = back-substitute R (upper-triangular n x n) against Qtb top-n. (3) Gate: 2-D f64, m>=n, full-rank (R diagonal all above a tolerance; rank-deficient falls back to lstsq_svd), finite. (4) Wire into the lstsq path (fnp-python lstsq wrapper or fnp-linalg lstsq_nxn/lstsq_svd dispatch) for that regime; everything else keeps the current path. VERIFY: allclose parity vs numpy.linalg.lstsq x (and residuals/rank/singular_values 4-tuple contract) on tall-skinny f64 (e.g. 1e6x8, 1e6x16, 2e6x8 - where numpy leaves 26-81x per the TSQR ledger), same-worker, rch. KEEP requires allclose parity + the 4-tuple shape/semantics + a measured win vs numpy + one-lever commit; correctness-critical, so verify thoroughly before shipping. Do NOT retry qr(mode=r) wiring (sign-divergent, .370 NO-SHIP). Needs a stable rch fleet for the allclose runs.
notes:
KERNEL BANKED (commit 67c01ad7, GoldKnoll) in fnp-linalg/src/lib.rs:
- householder_r_apply_b_in_place: extends householder_r_in_place, block arithmetic BYTE-IDENTICAL (R bit-matches tsqr_r), also reflects b.
- tsqr_qtb(a,b,m,n)->(R n*n, c=top-n of Qtb): same parallel-leaf+sequential-fold tree as tsqr_r (leaf_qtb/combine_qtb).
- lstsq_tsqr(a,b,m,n,rcond)->LstsqResult 4-tuple: x=back-sub(R,c); s+rank from svd_mxn(R,n,n) (sigma(A)=sigma(R)); residuals=||b-Ax||^2 (only if rank==n && m>n); rank<n falls back to lstsq_svd. Sign-invariant => allclose to numpy, NO qr(mode=r) sign divergence.
TESTS PASS (rch, 10 tsqr tests green) + clippy -D warnings clean: R bit-identity vs tsqr_r (single+multiblock); full 4-tuple allclose vs lstsq_svd (m<=1000 to keep m*m-U reference cheap); multiblock optimality A^T(b-Ax)~0 @16384x8; exact 3x2 fit; rank-deficient fallback; malformed rejection.

title: Add fail-closed Phase2C porting ledger freshness verifier

Add a focused verifier in fnp-conformance that reads artifacts/contracts/PORTING_ESSENCE_EXTRACTION_LEDGER_V1.md plus artifacts/phase2c/FNP-P2C-*/packet_readiness_report.json and fails when a packet row claims stale proof status such as anchor-only, open, partial, missing packet artifacts, or E-I pending while the packet readiness report is ready with zero missing artifacts/fields/parse errors.

The current stale-evidence wave was found manually. A fail-closed verifier turns that class of drift into an automated signal for future swarms.

Prefer a small Rust verifier/bin or test helper near the existing conformance control-plane validators. Parse the ledger conservatively enough to identify packet rows and status cells; avoid brittle global string bans that would flag legitimate historical words in unrelated sections. ## Tests
Add unit tests for ready-vs-stale row rejection, non-ready row allowance, and clean ready row acceptance. Include a command that can be offloaded via rch.

Add an e2e or bin invocation that writes a JSON report with checked packet count, stale row count, and diagnostics. Success requires zero stale rows for ready packets.

title: correctness: we ANSWER 14 calls numpy refuses (percentile/allclose/heaviside/clip on object operands) and return object where numpy returns float64 - plus 336 exception-TYPE divergences
description:
CLOSED WITH A DECIDED RESIDUAL, BlackThrush, 2026-09-01, commit 09d3094b. 5 of the 14 inverse
cells are fixed; the other 9 are decided, not left open, and two of them are reassigned.

FIRST, THE EVIDENCE THAT MADE THE DECISIONS POSSIBLE. Every one of the 14 calls was replayed
against the INSTALLED interpreter (numpy 2.4.3) at the exact argument position the sweep used.
All 14 raise there too, so none is a 2.5.2-only behaviour and no fix here is version-chasing.
That check mattered: replaying them at the WRONG position first made two of them look
version-dependent (np.percentile(obj, q) answers on 2.4.3 and raises on 2.5.2), and the sweep's
actual cell is np.percentile(f64, obj_q), which raises on both. READ THE POSITION, not the name.

FIXED (5 cells), measured 14 -> 9 inverse and both_raise 5812 -> 5817 on hz4:
  histogram_bin_edges  4  the explicit-bins shortcut returned `np.asarray(bins)` verbatim for
                          anything not an int or str. numpy wants an integer, a string, or a
                          1-D array of EDGES, and refuses a 0-d operand and a structured dtype
                          it cannot order. Both now reach numpy's own message.
  heaviside            1  a 0-d OBJECT array extracts to f64 via `__float__`, so the scalar
                          fast path computed a step numpy will not - it has no heaviside loop
                          for object. The branch declines an object-carrying step value.

REASSIGNED (4 cells) to [[deadlock-audit-defaulted-argument-three-state-parse-kqn3n]]:
  clip 4. numpy DISTINGUISHES `np.clip(a, x)` (TypeError: a_max required) from
  `np.clip(a, x, None)` (fine) and from `np.clip(a, min=x)` (fine). PyO3 collapses an omitted
  `a_max` into an explicitly passed `None`, so ours cannot tell the first from the second.
  This is the same constraint kqn3n exists for, and clip is its clearest case: not a corner,
  a call shape people actually write.

DELIBERATELY NOT MATCHED (5 cells), and this is the decision the bead asked for:
  percentile / nanpercentile with an object `q`   2
  allclose with an object `b` or `rtol`           2
  isclose with an object `rtol`                   1
  numpy refuses these because it runs `isnan`/`isfinite` OVER THE ARGUMENT - the refusal is a
  side effect of its implementation, not a documented contract. Ours converts the 0-d object
  through `__float__` and answers the arithmetically correct result. Reproducing the refusal
  would mean adding a dtype gate to the hot path of three reductions in order to become WORSE
  at a call no one writes deliberately. If a future policy says "bug-compatible with the
  incumbent, always", these five are the list to revisit; the sweep re-measures them free.

THE 3 RESULT-TYPE CELLS are unchanged and belong with the dtype-promotion audit
([[deadlock-audit-oxxzf]]), whose forms do not yet cover object inputs:

title: [perf][fnp-python] Widen native TSQR lstsq to the (M,K) multi-RHS form
description:
Follow-on to the 2026-08-04 INCUMBENT-WIN in deadlock-audit-i546h (2.08-2.56x on 1-D rhs; ledger row banked in 11b57f46). try_native_lstsq_tsqr currently declines b.ndim != 1 and hands numpy's (M,K) multi-RHS form straight back to gelsd, so the whole K>1 surface is unimproved.

THE WORK: tsqr_qtb carries ONE b vector through the reduction (leaf_qtb applies the leaf's reflector sequence to a length-rows b block, combine_qtb re-reduces a stacked 2n vector). Generalise both to a K-column block: the leaf applies the same reflectors to a rows x K panel, the fold stacks two n x K panels, and residual_sq becomes a per-column vector of dropped squared norms. Back substitution then runs per column against the same R. R is unchanged, so tsqr_r bit-identity must still hold.

NUMPY SEMANTICS TO MATCH (checked against the vendored _linalg.py lstsq): for 2-D b, x has shape (n, K); resids has shape (K,) when rank==n and m>n, else shape (0,); rank stays an int32 scalar; s stays (min(m,n),). Note numpy squeezes x only for the is_1d case and deliberately does NOT squeeze resids - the source comments say squeezing it would break compatibility, so do not 'fix' that.

WHY IT IS NOT FREE: a K-column right-hand side changes the arithmetic intensity of BOTH arms - gelsd amortises its SVD across columns, and our leaf work grows with K while the reduction over A does not. The 1-D win therefore does NOT transfer by assumption. This needs its own dual-null contract run before any claim.

ACCEPTANCE: allclose 4-tuple + exact dtypes + exact shapes vs live numpy across K in {2,3,8} at 1e6x8 and 1e6x16, plus the negative cases still declining; tsqr_r bit-identity preserved; and a same-invocation dual-null contract on a host-exclusive box (the criterion_python_linalg harness already does all of this for K=1 - extend it, do not build a second harness). Report the ratio whichever way it comes out; a measured loss here is a publishable REJECT row with the K at which it turns.
close_reason: SHIPPED + MEASURED. Code in f56d99c7, ledger row in 7fa1b86c. RESULT: 2.01-3.41x, nine DECIDABLE_WIN rows, and the bead's own hypothesis is REFUTED - the ratio RISES with K rather than turning, so there is no K<=8 to name. n=8: 2.950/3.273/3.413/3.308 for K=1/2/3/8. n=16: 1.832/2.006/2.571/2.368. MECHANISM: the bead's model counted our leaf growth but not gelsd's; the O(mn^2) reduction over A is paid ONCE regardless of K so our only marginal cost per column is the m x K b-panel, while gelsd applies its factorisation per column (NumPy 114.97->208.14ms K=1->8 at n=8 vs ours 39.13->61.06ms). CONTRACT: live NumPy 2.4.6 same invocation, invocation_id 000000000000000018c90f52173df530-003d8555, artifact_sha256 d527de76..., bench_elf_sha256 6992566c... (differs from the incumbent artifact), 21 interleaved rounds min_of=1, dual-null gate, shared timed component disclosed at share_of_candidate_pct=0.005252 MEASURED on the measurement host rather than reused from the banked row. ENGAGEMENT: byte_identical=false every row (a declined route returns NumPy's exact bytes and reads ~1.0x) plus OBSERVED_THREAD_ACTIVITY numpy=4 threads vs fnp=9. MATCHED CONFIG: OPENBLAS/OMP/MKL=8=RAYON_NUM_THREADS - gelsd IS threaded here and the harness rejected my first attempt that starved it to 1. CORRECTNESS: allclose 4-tuple + exact dtypes + exact shapes vs live numpy at K in {2,3,8} at n=8 and n=16; x is (n,K) for 2-D b and squeezed (n,) for 1-D; residuals one per column when full rank and m>n, empty otherwise, NOT squeezed; rank int32; K=0/3-D/rank-deficient-multi-RHS decline. K=1 route proven BIT-IDENTICAL to before over R, s, Qtb, x and residual at four shapes (cargo test -p fnp-linalg --lib tsqr = 13 passed; -p fnp-python --lib lstsq = 2 passed with NATIVE_ARM_REACHABLE). ledger_hygiene 19 passed / 0 failed. DISCLOSED WEAKNESS: post-run ps found an unrelated rustc at 225% that appeared during the run (drain stops rch routing, not direct ssh), so the tail was not provably exclusive; all ten per-contract preflights read clear with max busy 0.172 vs the 0.200 ceiling. K=1 rows are NOT differenced against the 2026-08-04 banked 2.08-2.56x row - different host, ~35% host effect in this fleet - they are only the in-invocation baseline. NOT measured: K>8, n>16, complex, float32, non-contiguous, wide.

title: [perf][fnp-python] pin the magnitude of the per-call route overhead by sweeping DOWN to where kernel work vanishes
description:
deadlock-audit-m7tti identified the binary-ufunc loss as FIXED PER-CALL OVERHEAD (ratio 0.708577 at 2^16 walking to 1.001588 at 2^24, per-element excess collapsing ~194x). Its excess_ns readings were 10184 (2^16), 100062 (2^20, called out as contaminated) and 13446 (2^24) - so the fixed cost looks like roughly 10-13 microseconds per call, bracketed by the two clean cells.

TEN MICROSECONDS IS A LOT. NumPy's own ufunc dispatch is on the order of 1 us. If our route really burns ~10 us before touching data, that is the single largest lever on every small-array call in the library, and it is worth knowing the number precisely rather than inferring it from two cells at opposite ends of a 256x sweep.

DESIGN: extend the existing bench_route_floor_size_sweep_vs_numpy down through n = 2^8 and 2^12, where the kernel has essentially nothing to do (2^8 x f64 = 2 KiB, L1-resident) and the per-call cost is therefore nearly the whole measurement. Same probe (multiply, no hazard scan), same dual-null contract, same invocation.

WHAT EACH OUTCOME MEANS: excess_ns roughly flat from 2^8 through 2^16 confirms a fixed per-call cost and hands us its magnitude directly. excess_ns falling toward zero at tiny n would REFUTE the fixed-cost reading of m7tti and point instead at something size-dependent that merely looked fixed across the sizes measured so far - which would be a correction to a row banked today.

Acceptance: a row naming WORKER and HARNESS with all five cells and their nulls, giving excess_ns per cell, and an explicit statement of which of the two outcomes above the data shows. If it refutes m7tti's mechanism, say so plainly and amend that row.
close_reason: CONFIRMED m7tti's mechanism and pinned the magnitude. worker=vmi1153651, harness=common::run_dual_null_median_ci_contract, numpy 2.4.3, multiply f64, ONE invocation, four cells all DECIDABLE_REGRESSION with nulls at unity: n=2^8 ratio 0.125948 ci95=[0.125197,0.126375] excess 6593 ns; n=2^12 ratio 0.279600 ci95=[0.277951,0.281856] excess 6988 ns; n=2^16 ratio 0.720000 ci95=[0.710439,0.727495] excess 10025 ns; n=2^20 ratio 0.947235 ci95=[0.919376,0.954287] excess 75070 ns. The acceptance asked which of two outcomes the data shows: excess_ns is FLAT (6593/6988/10025 while work grows 256x), so it CONFIRMS the fixed per-call cost rather than refuting it, and the magnitude is ~6.6-7 us measured rather than the ~10-13 us m7tti inferred. Headline finding: at n=256 fnp.multiply is 7.97x SLOWER than numpy.multiply (7539 vs 946 ns) - the campaign's worst vs-incumbent ratio so far, and pure per-call overhead. The 2^24 cell did not run because five dual-null cells exceed rch's 1800s SSH ceiling (RCH-E104); m7tti's 2^24 parity number was NOT borrowed into this row since it came from a different invocation. Banked in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md with a retry predicate naming the attack order: per-call Python attribute lookups for dtype/itemsize/c_contiguous on both operands, PyBuffer::get on each, then the numpy.empty allocation - measured at 2^8-2^12 where a lever will show.

title: [P0][correctness][fnp-python] f16 unique returns a THREAD-COUNT-DEPENDENT value set - passes on 8 cores, wrong values on 16
description:
MISATTRIBUTION CORRECTED. conformance_unravel_unique::f16_unique_presence_table_bit_exact has been failing and was assumed to be deadlock-audit-f7qjf, the upstream numpy x86-simd-sort fp16 defect. It is NOT. It is our bug.

EVIDENCE (TealOak, 2026-08-15, harness = cargo test --test conformance_unravel_unique, rch remote):
  WORKER hz2  (16 cores, AMD EPYC-Genoa, AVX-512, numpy 2.4.3, py3.14.4): FAILS
  WORKER hz1  ( 8 cores, AMD EPYC-Milan, AVX-512, numpy 2.4.3, py3.14.4): PASSES (63 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored)
Same source, same numpy version, same Python, same ISA class. The only axis that differs is CORE COUNT, i.e. the default rayon thread count. Reproduced on hz2 at base commit bf6cbe55 with --no-overlay (0 passed; 1 failed), so it is not introduced by any recent change.

WHY THE UPSTREAM STORY IS RULED OUT: I added a guard that decides brokenness from the ORACLE'S OWN output - np.unique must be strictly ascending, and np.unique sorts internally, so a mis-sorting numpy is detectable. On hz2 the guard reports lanes=[] and numpy=2.4.3, i.e. numpy's output IS strictly ascending. numpy is fine here; f7qjf's defect was on numpy 2.3.5 and this fleet has moved to 2.4.3.

WHAT ACTUALLY DIVERGES: not ordering - the VALUE SET.
  ['FAIL n=2000003 value multiset', 'FAIL nan defer']
The n=2000003 lane fails a bit-multiset comparison, meaning fnp.unique and np.unique return DIFFERENT VALUES, not the same values in a different order. The n=200000 lane of the same generator passes, so it is size/partition dependent. A 65536-slot f16 presence table cannot lose or invent values unless the parallel partitioning or the ambiguity-defer decision is per-partition rather than global.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS: the both-zeros / NaN ambiguity DEFER (which the test documents as the contract: inputs containing both +0.0 and -0.0, or any NaN, must defer to numpy) is decided per-partition or on a sampled prefix, so at 16 threads a partition that contains no -0.0 takes the native table path while the array as a whole contains both zero signs. That would produce exactly this signature: same values except the zero-sign pair and/or NaN patterns, only above the size where the extra partitions appear. A diagnostic that prints the symmetric difference of the two bit sets, plus ours_has_both_zeros / numpy_has_both_zeros, is already added to the test and will name it.

SEVERITY: P0. np.unique is a core surface, this is a silent wrong-answer (not a crash) on the more common large-core machines, and it is thread-count dependent so it will not reproduce for anyone debugging on a small box. It also means any conformance run on an 8-core worker is green while the same code is wrong on 16.

PROBE: f16_unique_presence_table_bit_exact passes on hz2 at its native 16 threads. Additionally: running it on hz2 under RAYON_NUM_THREADS=8 must be compared against its default-threads run in the SAME invocation-class; if 8 threads passes and 16 fails on the same host and same ELF, thread count is causal and that is the bug to fix.
close_reason:
REFUTED - NOT OUR BUG. I filed this and I was wrong twice; closing with the evidence rather than leaving a false P0 open.

Wrong story 1 (bead title): 'thread-count-dependent, 8 cores vs 16'. hz1 (8c, EPYC-Milan) passes and hz2 (16c, EPYC-Genoa) fails, but the causal axis is NOT core count - it is ISA. Checked /proc/cpuinfo directly: hz1 avx512f=0, hz2 avx512f=1 (neither has avx512fp16). Milan is Zen 3 and has no AVX-512 at all. hz2 is the fleet's ONLY avx512f worker. A RAYON_NUM_THREADS=8 run I queued as the causality test landed on vmi1149989 instead of hz2, so it was a cross-worker comparison and proved nothing - I am not citing it.

Wrong story 2 (my first comment): 'per-partition both-zeros defer'. Refuted by the diagnostic: ours_has_both_zeros=False and numpy_has_both_zeros=False, and no zero-sign pair appears in either symmetric difference.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS: numpy is the broken side, and it is deadlock-audit-f7qjf, alive on numpy 2.4.3. Minimal pure-numpy repro on WORKER hz2, no fnp loaded at all:
  rng = np.random.default_rng(20260716)
  a200k = (rng.standard_normal(200000)*2).astype(np.float16)   # consume the stream in order
  a = (rng.standard_normal(2000003)*2).astype(np.float16)
  e = np.unique(a)
  -> len 24403, dups_in_numpy_unique 2, strictly_ascending False
  -> np.unique(a.astype(np.float32)).astype(np.float16) -> len 24401  (the correct answer)
np.unique returns a result with TWO DUPLICATES and non-ascending order, violating its own contract. fnp returned 24401 distinct values, i.e. fnp was right and numpy was wrong. The n=200000 lane of the same generator is clean (dups 0, ascending True), so it is size-gated, consistent with x86-simd-sort engaging above a threshold.

The 'nan defer' lane is the same defect in payload form: input contained exactly one NaN, 0x7e00; we return 0x7e00, numpy returns 0x7c01 - a pattern never present in the input, and the smallest signalling-NaN bit pattern, a classic SIMD sentinel. An is-ascending check cannot see this because NaN is excluded from ordering, which is why my first guard passed it through.

Superseded by deadlock-audit-f7qjf. The test hardening lands there.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN DESCRIPTION - the divergence is NOT a lost-or-invented value set (TealOak, 2026-08-15). I overstated it; the diagnostic now names both lanes precisely. WORKER hz2, harness = cargo test --test conformance_unravel_unique, numpy 2.4.3, py3.14.4.

LANE 'nan defer' - NaN PAYLOAD, not ordering and not a value-set error:
  ours_only=['0x7e00=nan'] n=1   numpy_only=['0x7c01=nan'] n=1
Both sides return exactly ONE NaN. The input contained exactly one NaN, 0x7e00 (np.float16(np.nan), the canonical quiet NaN). We return 0x7e00 - the pattern that was actually present. numpy returns 0x7c01, a payload that was never in the input; 0x7c01 is the smallest signalling-NaN pattern and a classic sentinel in SIMD sort kernels. So numpy is the side that mutates here, and this IS plausibly the x86-simd-sort fp16 family (deadlock-audit-f7qjf) manifesting as payload corruption rather than mis-ordering. NOTE: an is-ascending check CANNOT catch this, because NaN is excluded from any ordering test - which is why the guard reported lanes=[] and passed it through to a hard failure.

LANE 'n=2000003' - a DUPLICATE, not a different value set:
  ours_only=[] n=0   numpy_only=[] n=0
The distinct bit patterns are IDENTICAL on both sides. The bit MULTISET still differs, so one side emitted some pattern twice. np.unique output must have no repeats, so whichever side duplicated is wrong. A re-run with lengths and the repeated patterns printed is in flight to name it.

SO THE HYPOTHESIS IN THE BEAD BODY (per-partition both-zeros defer) IS NOT SUPPORTED: ours_has_both_zeros=False and numpy_has_both_zeros=False on both lanes, and no zero-sign pair appears in either symmetric difference. Disregard that paragraph.

STILL TRUE AND STILL THE POINT: hz1 (8 cores) passes and hz2 (16 cores) fails on identical source, numpy, Python and ISA class, and it reproduces at base commit bf6cbe55 with --no-overlay. A RAYON_NUM_THREADS=8 run on hz2 is in flight to make thread count causal rather than correlated.

title: perf: fnp.sqrt(f64) is a 2.4x WIN on a settled buffer and a 1.2-1.4x LOSS on a buffer produced by the previous call - page faults and mmap churn are BOTH refuted
description:
CLOSURE, BlackThrush, 2026-09-01. MECHANISM FOUND, FIX SHIPPED in commit b64b5f78.
The bead's framing was wrong in two ways and its retry predicate was right.

FIRST: THE SIZES IN THIS BEAD ARE ONE TOO HIGH. h2h_sqrt_regime printed `n.bit_length()`, which
reports 22 for 2^21. So "compose 2^21 1.399x/1.388x" is n = 2^20, and the whole size sweep
shifts down one. Reproduced there exactly: 1.401x / 1.360x at n=2^20. Fixed in the harness
(3 sites); no other h2h example had the bug - they all use `- 1`.

SECOND: IT IS NOT ABOUT FRESHNESS, IT IS ABOUT CHUNK WIDTH. The kernel handed par_chunks_mut a
chunk of n/current_num_threads(), which on 64 cores is 16 KiB of f64 at n=2^17 - far below
SQRT_PARALLEL_MIN = 1 MiB, the size at which this same function has already decided a fan-out is
worth doing. The floor was checked per CALL and never per THREAD, so on a wide host it was lost
by a factor of the core count. The bead saw the mild end of a much larger defect: measured on
hz4 at loadavg 8-12, `fnp.sqrt(np.abs(a))` vs numpy was a 3.821x/5.344x LOSS at 2^17, 5.220x/
2.670x at 2^18, 2.111x/2.086x at 2^19 - four standing losses nothing had marked, because every
benchmark that looked at sqrt looked at ONE size.

HOW IT WAS DECIDED, since the bead's own two hypotheses were already dead. The probe
(crates/fnp-python/examples/h2h_sqrt_threads.rs) builds explicit rayon ThreadPools and runs the
timed statements inside pool.install(..), so n and T move INDEPENDENTLY in one process against
one numpy - RAYON_NUM_THREADS would have needed one invocation per point. Round 1 (full T ladder
at fixed n) found the shape. It could not, on its own, separate "small chunks are bad" from
"this 64-core host was at loadavg 48 and 64 threads were oversubscribed", AND A DUAL A/A NULL
CANNOT SEE THAT CONFOUND - it compares fnp to fnp, so a bias hitting the wide arm and sparing the
narrow one passes it perfectly. Round 2 swept n at fixed T instead, because only the chunk story
predicts a dependence on n: T=64/T=8 ran 1.97, 1.49, 1.23, 1.12, 1.05 as n went 2^20..2^24 while
loadavg fell from 15.5 to 7.5 and the 2^20 cell barely moved (1.401 -> 1.360). Oversubscription
predicts a constant. Round 3 measured the band below, where a gate would actually bind.

THE FIX, one line, no new constant:
    let threads = rayon::current_num_threads().min(n / SQRT_PARALLEL_MIN);
A chunk is one thread's share, so a chunk below the floor is a fan-out the function has already
judged not worth doing - reusing the floor keeps the per-call and per-thread decisions
consistent. It is the identity once n >= threads * floor.

MEASURED BEFORE -> AFTER at T=64 (the production path), hz4, loadavg 8-12, interleaved AB/BA,
dual A/A nulls, incumbent-spread gate, both sweep directions:
    2^17  3.821x/5.344x -> 0.591x/0.588x   6.5-9.1x
    2^18  5.220x/2.670x -> 0.869x/0.569x   4.7-6.0x
    2^19  2.111x/2.086x -> 1.001x/0.825x   2.1-2.5x
    2^20  1.260x/1.311x -> 0.925x/0.696x   1.4-1.9x
    2^21  0.945x/0.947x -> 0.758x/0.748x   1.25x
    2^22  0.816x/0.782x -> 0.747x/0.728x   1.09x
Every standing LOSS in the band is gone; the worst cell is now parity.

NULL CONTROL, and it is what licenses the cross-invocation before/after: at 2^23 and 2^24 the
expression is PROVABLY the identity, and those rows measure unchanged (0.668x/0.655x ->
0.659x/0.665x; 0.601x/0.601x -> 0.586x/0.571x). The T=1 arm and the numpy arm also hold across
both invocations (numpy 218-221 us at 2^17 in both).

THE COST, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED. On a SETTLED input the gate is neutral at 2^17-2^19, better
at 2^22, and 1.05-1.26x WORSE at 2^20-2^21 (0.169x -> 0.213x, 0.214x -> 0.243x) on cells still
winning 4-5x. Reducing chunk count does not reduce how many workers WAKE - see the successor.

VALUES: raw-BYTE parity (not allclose) over 10 cells at 2^17/2^19/2^21/2^22/2^24 with -0.0, inf
and nan planted: ALL BIT-IDENTICAL. Run from inside the example via append_to_inittab, because
conformance_sqrt cannot execute under rch at all - it dlopens libfnp_python.so as a sibling of
its own test binary and all 15 cases die on ImportError, square_* and cbrt_* included. Filed.

SUCCESSORS: the repo-wide vein (95 sites share this exact expression; worst-first candidate list
by floor/core-count, UNARY_PARALLEL_MIN first), the conformance_sqrt layout bug, and the residual
mechanism (the fresh-input surcharge scales with thread count - ~0 us at T=1, 706 us at T=64 at
n=2^17 - and pool WIDTH costs 1.35x independently of chunk count).

--- original bead follows ---

SPLIT OUT OF deadlock-audit-2nudi (vein 1). CHARACTERISED, MECHANISM UNKNOWN, NOT YET A LEVER.

worker=hz4, numpy 2.5.2 live in the same invocation, harnesses
crates/fnp-python/examples/h2h_compose.rs and h2h_sqrt_regime.rs, commits e5036b0d..(this).

THE FINDING. Neither call loses alone; the COMPOSITION does. At 2^19 f64, one invocation:
    abs alone              0.983x        sqrt alone (settled input)  0.403x   - a 2.5x WIN
    np.sqrt(fnp.abs(a))    0.980x        - our abs is exonerated
    fnp.sqrt(np.abs(a))    2.536x        - our SQRT, and only when its input is FRESH
    fnp.sqrt(pre_np_abs)   0.430x        - the SAME sqrt on a buffer allocated ONCE is a WIN
Composition per se is innocent: negative(abs) 0.970x, square(abs) 0.919x, abs(abs) 0.963x, and
'abs twice, no compose' 0.940x are all fine. It is sqrt, and it is the freshness of its input.

CLEAN, REPLICATED ROWS (nulls in 0.97-1.03, effect > incumbent spread), two phases x two sizes:
    compose 2^21  1.399x / 1.388x        settled 2^20  0.436x / 0.404x
    compose 2^22  1.207x / 1.190x        settled 2^17  0.519x / 0.520x
    compose 2^17  0.599x / 0.600x  (SERIAL-ish; the gate is SQRT_PARALLEL_MIN = 1 << 17)

TWO PRE-REGISTERED MECHANISMS, BOTH REFUTED BY DIRECT MEASUREMENT:
  H1 page-fault storm from 64 rayon threads first-touching a fresh output. REFUTED: minor faults
     per call (ru_minflt) are 0.0-0.4 for EVERY arm at every size from 2^17 to 2^22, against 1024
     pages in a single 2^19 f64 output. There is no fault storm to blame.
  H2 glibc mmap churn (munmap/re-mmap of the block each iteration). REFUTED: mallopt with
     M_MMAP_THRESHOLD and M_TRIM_THRESHOLD both raised to 512 MiB - both calls returned 1 - moves
     compose 2^21 from 1.399x to 1.388x and compose 2^22 from 1.207x to 1.190x. Nothing.
This matters beyond this cell: 'large-buffer mmap churn' is a banked repo-wide explanation and it
does NOT explain this one. The remaining candidate is producer-consumer cache locality - numpy's
sqrt reads the buffer from the same core that just wrote it, our 64-way parallel sqrt drags
16 MiB of singly-owned dirty lines across the coherence fabric - but that is a HYPOTHESIS and
deciding it needs cache/coherence counters, not wall clock.

THE MIDDLE BAND CANNOT BE MEASURED HERE. compose at 2^18/2^19/2^20 reads 5.396x / 7.849x / 3.681x
but its A/A null runs 0.854-1.565 and the incumbent spread 19.8-74.2%. Those are NOT measurements
and must not be quoted; the decidable statement is the 2^21/2^22 pair at 1.19-1.40x.

RETRY PREDICATE: do not raise or lower SQRT_PARALLEL_MIN on this evidence. The same constant is
what makes the settled regime a 2.3-4.5x win, and no run yet separates the two regimes by anything
the code can observe at call time. Re-open with coherence counters (perf c2c / HITM), or with a
probe that varies rayon thread count while holding n fixed - if the loss shrinks as threads fall
while the settled win holds, chunk-count is the lever and a minimum-chunk-size gate is the fix.
close_reason: chunk width, not freshness: chunk >= SQRT_PARALLEL_MIN removes 4 standing losses (up to 5.3x), values bit-identical (commit b64b5f78)

title: [correctness][fnp-ufunc] nextafter DISCARDS NaN sign and payload - returns +NaN where numpy propagates the operand
description:
BinaryOp::Nextafter returns a bare `f64::NAN` (0x7ff8000000000000) whenever either
operand is NaN, discarding the operand's SIGN and PAYLOAD. NumPy propagates the operand.

Found while writing the threshold test for deadlock-audit-hzl1w; deliberately NOT fixed
in that commit, since the failing size (n = 2^20 - 1) is BELOW the changed gate and runs
serially under both the old and new threshold, so no commit in that series caused it.

MEASURED against the installed numpy 2.4.3 (.venv-numpy314), raw bits, little-endian
hex shown big-endian below:

  x=7ff8000000000123 y=3ff0000000000000 -> 7ff8000000000123   (lhs NaN, payload kept)
  x=fff8000000000456 y=3ff0000000000000 -> fff8000000000456   (SIGN kept)
  x=3ff0000000000000 y=7ff8000000000123 -> 7ff8000000000123   (rhs NaN)
  x=7ff8000000000123 y=fff8000000000456 -> fff8000000000456   (BOTH NaN -> RHS wins)
  x=fff8000000000456 y=7ff8000000000123 -> 7ff8000000000123   (BOTH NaN -> RHS wins)
  x=7ff0000000000001 y=3ff0000000000000 -> 7ff8000000000001   (SIGNALING NaN is QUIETED)

THE RULE, and all six rows above satisfy it:
  if rhs.is_nan()      -> rhs with the quiet bit (0x0008000000000000) set
  else if lhs.is_nan() -> lhs with the quiet bit set
  else                    existing behaviour

We currently return +NaN in every one of those cases, so we are wrong on sign, wrong on
payload, and wrong on which operand wins when both are NaN.

SCOPE: BinaryOp::Nextafter in crates/fnp-ufunc/src/lib.rs, so every route reaching that
op is affected, not just the zero-copy f64 one.

ACCEPTANCE: a planted-negative test against the LIVE numpy that compares raw BYTES for
non-finite operand pairs including a negative NaN, a custom payload, a signaling NaN and
both-NaN, and fails on the current code.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED AND ON main (2026-08-24, AmberFalcon swarm). The kernel change and its test landed as d0dcbc68 - a PEER committed them while my batch was running, which is the documented shared-tree hazard here; the content is byte-identical to what I tested, and I verified d0dcbc68 is an ancestor of origin/main.

THE BUG. BinaryOp::Nextafter answered a bare `f64::NAN` (7ff8000000000000) whenever either operand was NaN. That is the POSITIVE default quiet NaN, so it lost the operand's sign, lost its payload, and returned the same value regardless of WHICH operand was NaN.

MEASURED against the installed numpy 2.4.3 (.venv-numpy314), raw bits:

  lhs=7ff8000000000123 rhs=3ff0000000000000 -> 7ff8000000000123   payload kept
  lhs=fff8000000000456 rhs=3ff0000000000000 -> fff8000000000456   SIGN kept
  lhs=3ff0000000000000 rhs=7ff8000000000123 -> 7ff8000000000123   rhs NaN propagates
  lhs=3ff0000000000000 rhs=fff8000000000456 -> fff8000000000456
  lhs=7ff8000000000123 rhs=fff8000000000456 -> fff8000000000456   BOTH NaN: RHS wins
  lhs=fff8000000000456 rhs=7ff8000000000123 -> 7ff8000000000123   BOTH NaN: RHS wins
  lhs=7ff0000000000001 rhs=3ff0000000000000 -> 7ff8000000000001   SIGNALING -> QUIETED

THE RULE, satisfying all seven rows: if rhs is NaN return rhs with the quiet bit set; else if lhs is NaN return lhs with the quiet bit set; else unchanged. The quiet bit (0x0008000000000000) is already set on a quiet NaN, so the OR only bites on a signaling one - which is what the last row requires.

TEST: `nextafter_propagates_nan_operands_bit_for_bit_like_numpy` (crates/fnp-python/src/lib.rs), 12 operand pairs covering negative NaN, custom payloads, signaling NaN, both-NaN in both orders, and the infinity edges so the fix cannot quietly move those while it is in the neighbourhood.

IT IS A REAL PLANTED NEGATIVE, and that property is ENCODED rather than claimed: for every NaN pair the test first asserts NumPy's answer is NOT 7ff8000000000000 - the value the old code returned - so a pair that stops discriminating fails loudly instead of passing vacuously. A test written with plain `np.nan` would have PASSED on the bug, because the positive default quiet NaN is the one case the old code got right by accident. That is how this survived.

Comparison is on `to_bits`, not `==`: every assertion here concerns a NaN, and NaN compares unequal to everything, so an equality-based check would pass no matter what the bits were.

TESTS (local, RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1, env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR, thinkstation1):
  cargo test --release -p fnp-python --lib nextafter  -> 3 passed, 0 failed
      (the new test plus the two PRE-EXISTING nextafter parity tests, so the fix does
       not regress the finite cases they cover)
  cargo test --release -p fnp-ufunc  --lib nextafter  -> 9 passed, 0 failed

SCOPE: the change is in BinaryOp::Nextafter in crates/fnp-ufunc/src/lib.rs, so every route reaching that op gets it, not only the zero-copy f64 one.

PROVENANCE NOTE: this was found while writing the threshold test for deadlock-audit-hzl1w and deliberately NOT fixed there - the failing size (n = 2^20 - 1) is BELOW that bead's changed gate and runs serially under both the old and new threshold, so no commit in that series caused it. Filing it separately was the right call and this is the fix.

No perf claim: this is a correctness change on a non-finite path that is not on any hot loop.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THE SAME DEFECT IN maximum/minimum - FIXED (2026-08-24, AmberFalcon swarm). Commit a5a88a2b, pushed to main and master.

HOW IT WAS FOUND: after landing the nextafter fix I read the neighbouring match arms rather than assuming the bug was isolated. `BinaryOp::Maximum` and `BinaryOp::Minimum` had exactly the same shape - a bare `f64::NAN` for any NaN operand, i.e. the POSITIVE default quiet NaN - losing the sign, losing the payload, and answering identically whichever side was NaN.

MEASURED against the installed numpy 2.4.3 (.venv-numpy314), raw bits, identical for both ops:

  lhs=fff8000000000456 rhs=3ff0000000000000 -> fff8000000000456   SIGN kept
  lhs=3ff0000000000000 rhs=fff8000000000456 -> fff8000000000456   rhs NaN propagates
  lhs=7ff8000000000123 rhs=fff8000000000456 -> 7ff8000000000123   BOTH NaN: LHS wins
  lhs=fff8000000000456 rhs=7ff8000000000123 -> fff8000000000456   BOTH NaN: LHS wins
  lhs=7ff0000000000001 rhs=3ff0000000000000 -> 7ff0000000000001   SIGNALING kept VERBATIM
  lhs=3ff0000000000000 rhs=7ff0000000000001 -> 7ff0000000000001

THE FAMILY DOES NOT SHARE ONE RULE - the most important thing in this comment. maximum/minimum prefer the LHS on a both-NaN tie and return the NaN VERBATIM (a signaling NaN stays signaling), while `nextafter` prefers the RHS and QUIETS it. I measured each arm separately instead of reusing the rule I had just established; copying it would have been confidently wrong on both the tie-break and the quieting.

THE `lhs == rhs` ARM IS PRESERVED AND IS LOAD-BEARING: NumPy returns the RIGHT operand for equal operands, which is what makes signed zeros agree - maximum(0.0, -0.0) is -0.0 and maximum(-0.0, 0.0) is +0.0, both measured. A `f64::max` shortcut answers +0.0 for both, and would pass any `==`-based test while being wrong in the bits.

TEST: `maximum_minimum_propagate_nan_operands_bit_for_bit_like_numpy` - 12 operand pairs per op (negative NaN, custom payloads, signaling NaN, both-NaN both orders, signed zeros both orders, ordinary values), compared on `to_bits`. PLANTED NEGATIVE, encoded not claimed: every NaN pair first asserts NumPy's answer is NOT 7ff8000000000000, the value the old code returned, so a pair that stops discriminating fails loudly. A test written with plain `np.nan` would have PASSED on the bug - the positive default quiet NaN is the one case the old code got right by accident, which is exactly how this survived next to the existing signed-zero tests.

TESTS (local, RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1, env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR, thinkstation1):
  cargo test --release -p fnp-python --lib maximum_minimum_propagate    -> 1 passed, 0 failed
  cargo test --release -p fnp-ufunc  --lib -- maximum minimum           -> 15 passed, 0 failed
       (includes binary_minimum_signed_zero and the masked min/max live-oracle tests)
  cargo test --release -p fnp-python --lib -- maximum minimum fmax fmin -> 5 passed, 0 failed
  cargo test --release -p fnp-python --test conformance_ufunc_edge      -> 73 passed, 0 failed

STILL OPEN, FOUND HERE, NOT FIXED: `fmax`/`fmin` match NumPy on quiet NaNs but diverge on SIGNALING ones. NumPy quiets: fmax(7ff0000000000001, 1.0) -> 7ff8000000000001, while ours returns the other operand (1.0). Different rule again, exotic path, and bundling it would have put two behaviour changes in one commit. Worth its own bead if anyone wants it.

NO PERF CLAIM: this is the NaN branch, not the common case on any hot loop.

WHY THIS AND NOT THE ASSIGNED CELLS: I was pointed at sort(int64,n=256) and searchsorted, and both are settled. ProudIbis posted REJECT-STANDS on the sort cell ("Remaining Python-entry/copy+PDQ cost is not licensed for another allocation retry. Stop this cell.") after taking it 0.2687x -> 0.4249x, and CERTIFIED the f64 array-needle searchsorted at 1.022342x vs live NumPy with clean dual nulls, then stood down at 04:51 with "no unowned losing row remains in this lane". The 3.17x searchsorted figure in my orders is stale.

title: [perf][fnp-linalg] eigvalsh residual ~3x: blocked tridiag_reduce_blocked still ~2.5x slower than numpy dsytrd (BLAS-3 fraction of symmetric two-sided update + FMA floor)
close_reason: Investigated, no-ship (residual is FMA-floor, not structural). The blocked tridiag_reduce_blocked is a proper dsytrd (BLAS-2 dlatrd panel + BLAS-3 rank-2k trailing update via packed_gemm). Tested the one candidate structural lever — lowering TRIDIAG_MATVEC_PAR_MIN (the panel symmetric-matvec u=A*v parallel gate, default 1024) — via clean same-binary env A/B at low load: parallelizing earlier REGRESSES (par-from-128: eigvalsh n256 9941->17416us, n512 56705->92361us; par-from-256 also worse at 384/512). The matvec is called nb*panels times with O(h) work/row, so rayon dispatch overhead dominates below ~1024 — the existing 1024 threshold is correctly tuned (the source comment was right). So the residual ~2.5x reduction gap vs numpy dsytrd is the per-core BLAS-2 panel-matvec efficiency: fnp's dot products autovectorize to AVX2 but WITHOUT FMA (.cargo disables +fma for bit-parity), ~2x behind numpy's AVX2+FMA dsymv. That is the FMA floor = arch bead 8vdtg (hardware FMA via target_feature/std::arch, human sign-off). Not a safe-Rust structural fix. The threshold win (a44dbead, eigvalsh 5x->3x) was the available lever.

title: [perf][fnp-python] make_mask_none/make_mask/mask_or -> numpy (560-1030x->1x)
close_reason: Shipped. Three pure boolean-mask utilities each stored masks as f64 UFuncArrays (8 bytes/elem) and rebuilt element-by-element, catastrophically slower than numpy's native bool ops: make_mask_none((4M,)) 68ms vs 66us (1030x), make_mask(int8 4M) 74ms vs 132us (564x), mask_or(bool,bool 4M) 101ms vs 113us (892x). All three are pure mask construction/combination with no arithmetic, so numpy is the parity reference. make_mask_none now defers to numpy.ma.make_mask_none (calloc np.zeros bool); make_mask defers after its O(1) nomask/dtype short-circuits; mask_or defers entirely (numpy logical_or). All now at parity (44/77/113us). Parity verified across bool/int/float inputs, all-false->nomask shrink, shrink=False, dtype, nomask operands, shape cases. 2 make_mask/mask_or conformance + 9 masked-constructor tests green. Found via gap_sweep24.

title: [test][fnp-random] parameter-sweep oracle differentials for the remaining branching distributions
close_reason:
COMPLETE. Four passes over the branching distributions; the enumerated set is now swept.

PASS 1 (8307d87b) gamma across shape=1.0, beta across Johnk — clean.
PASS 2 (17c00b83, f29dce90) poisson across lam=10 clean; binomial's BTPE arm BROKEN in all four parameter sets, fixed as 36ilk (four transcription corrections, root cause being a missing immediate-accept on u <= p1).
PASS 3 (d503cbd6) geometric across p=1/3, hypergeometric across both edges of the HRUA window, chisquare across df=2 — clean.
PASS 4 (this commit) standard_t, f and noncentral_chisquare's three arms — TWO MORE DEFECTS, both operation-order divergences that broke bit-exact parity:
  standard_t   numpy is sqrt(df/2) * num / sqrt(denom) with denom the RAW standard_gamma(df/2). Ours formed chi2 = 2*gamma and returned z / sqrt(chi2/df): identical mathematically, different rounding.
  f            numpy is subexpr1 = chisquare(dfnum)*dfden, subexpr2 = chisquare(dfden)*dfnum, ONE division. Ours divided each chi-square by its own df first, then divided.
Six of seventeen parameter sets diverged; after matching numpy's expression shapes all seventeen are bit-exact.

A REGRESSION CAUGHT BY THE FULL-SUITE RUN, worth recording: correcting f_distribution alone broke noncentral_f_zero_nonc_matches_central_stream, because noncentral_f still carried the old (a/dfnum)/(b/dfden) shape and the two no longer agreed. numpy's noncentral_f uses the same single-division shape as random_f (t = ncx2*dfden; t / (chisquare(dfden)*dfnum)), so correcting it too restores the invariant AND parity. Fixing one half of a pair of expressions that must agree is how a targeted parity fix becomes a regression.

DISTINGUISHING DESYNC FROM ROUNDING mattered here. The pass-4 failures looked like the BTPE bug at first glance, but the sequences were position-aligned and differed only in the last one or two digits - rounding, not a switched algorithm. The BTPE failures were the opposite: values identical until one went missing and the rest shifted. Reading the shape of the divergence before reaching for a cause is what separated a formula-order fix from an algorithm fix.

VERIFIED: timeout cargo test -p fnp-random --lib = 446 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored; cargo clippy -p fnp-random --all-targets -- -D warnings = clean; cargo fmt --check exit 0 run UNPIPED.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
RATIONALE (CreamGlen, 2026-08-09). Distributions branch on their PARAMETERS, and a fixed-parameter oracle test sits on one side of the branch forever. gamma_beta_parameter_sweep_matches_live_numpy_oracle_bit_for_bit now covers gamma across its shape=1.0 algorithm switch (numpy's distributions.c uses a rejection scheme below 1.0 and Marsaglia-Tsang at or above; our implementation mirrors that split at lib.rs:5738/5766) and beta across its Johnk region, 15 parameter settings, compared BIT-FOR-BIT rather than at the suite's usual 1e-12.

That bound matters: the PCG64DXSM contract is bit-exactness, and assert_f64_seq's 1e-12 would let a stream that had diverged into a different-but-plausible sequence pass. Falsified - perturbing scale by 4e-11 relative fails at the tenth significant digit - so the strict comparison is doing work.

RESULT for gamma/beta: no defect, both arms agree bit-for-bit.

REMAINING distributions with known or likely parameter-dependent arms, none of which have a boundary sweep:
  standard_gamma  - same shape<1 split as gamma, reached directly
  chisquare       - routes through gamma(df/2), so it inherits the split at df=2
  standard_t      - chisquare-based, same inherited boundary
  f               - ratio of two chisquares, two boundaries
  noncentral_chisquare / noncentral_f - additional nonzero-nonc branches
  binomial        - numpy switches between inversion and BTPE around n*p
  poisson         - numpy switches at lam = 10
  geometric       - inversion vs search
  hypergeometric  - HIN vs H2PE
Each is the same shape of test as the gamma/beta one: enumerate parameters straddling the documented switch, one oracle subprocess, bit-exact compare. poisson (lam=10) and binomial (n*p threshold) are the highest value because their switch points are documented constants in numpy's source, so the boundary is known exactly rather than inferred.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THIRD PASS (CreamGlen, 2026-08-09). geometric_hypergeometric_chisquare_boundary_sweep_matches_live_numpy_oracle covers three more documented splits, 18 parameter sets, values straddling each threshold and sitting exactly on it:
  geometric       p < 1/3 inversion vs search        (7 p values incl. exactly 1/3)
  hypergeometric  10 <= sample <= total-10 -> HRUA   (sample 9/10/30/50/51 against total 60, i.e. both edges)
  chisquare       gamma(df/2), inheriting the shape=1 arm split at df=2  (6 df incl. 1.999_999_999, 2.0, 2.000_000_001)
Integers compared exactly; chisquare compared BIT-EXACT, since it inherits gamma's arm split and a tolerance would hide a switched algorithm.

RESULT: no defect in any of the three. Reporting that plainly - binomial's BTPE arm being broken (36ilk) made these suspect, and the suspicion did not pay out here.

Non-vacuity: perturbing geometric's p by 1e-9 relative fails the sweep, so numpy ran and the comparison bites.

REMAINING on this bead, none yet swept: standard_gamma (same shape<1 split reached directly), standard_t and f (chisquare-based, so they inherit the df=2 boundary through one or two levels), noncentral_chisquare and noncentral_f (additional nonzero-nonc branches). Those are the last of the enumerated set; after them the branching-distribution surface is covered.

title: [perf][fnp-python] ma.allequal zero-copy early-exit fold (beats numpy 2.6x masked, ~1000x differ)
close_reason: Shipped. ma.allequal(a,b) extracted BOTH operands' data+mask into owned f64 UFuncArrays before folding (85ms @4M, 7.9x slower than numpy); because that extract is O(n) up front, the later early-exit never paid off. New zero-copy fast path for f64 (MaskedArray or plain ndarray, equal shape): folds straight over the data/mask PyBuffers with a genuine short-circuit. Masks fetched only for MaskedArray operands (plain ndarray has no mask; calling getmaskarray on it would alloc a needless all-False pass). No-mask case folds in 2048-elt SIMD-friendly chunks (inner AND-reduction autovectorizes; per-chunk break short-circuits). IEEE x==y is already False for any NaN so no explicit NaN test needed. Score @4M: masked-equal 0.39x (2.56x FASTER than numpy), plain-equal 0.90x (FASTER), differ cases ~1000x (early exit, 4us vs ~3800us). Value parity verified across plain/masked/nan/all-masked/fill_value T+F/2d/mixed ma-vs-plain. allequal conformance test green. Found via gap_sweep24.

title: [perf][fnp-python] Measure the f64 divide fast-path cost of the FE-hazard branch added by 2nmd1
description:
deadlock-audit-2nmd1 made fnp.divide's native f64 kernel defer to numpy on any element that would raise an IEEE FP exception (divide-by-zero, invalid, overflow, underflow), because bit-identical VALUES are not parity when numpy also emits a RuntimeWarning that a pure-Rust kernel cannot raise into numpy's error state.

The check is FUSED into the existing pass over a and b (no second read of the divisor), and the clean path short-circuits on a single q.is_normal() test — a normal quotient rules out all four exceptions at once. Expected cost is therefore ~one predictable test per element on an op whose per-element work is an f64 divide.

NOT MEASURED. The fleet was saturated (no admissible rch workers) when the fix landed and the correctness fix was non-negotiable regardless of the delta, so no ratio was taken. This bead is to close that gap honestly, not to reconsider the deferral.

WHAT TO MEASURE: f64 divide, same-shape C-contiguous ndarrays, both the serial branch (n < 1<<21) and the rayon branch (n >= 1<<21), hazard-free input only. Use the standing harness — common::run_median_ci_contract with the A/A null in the same invocation, --profile release-perf, ELF sha self-reported from inside the process. Compare against the parent commit of the 2nmd1 fix: that is a same-binary former/candidate A/B, so any result is a maintenance-self-speedup class row, NOT an incumbent-win.

RETRY PREDICATE: if the measured clean-path regression exceeds the null envelope, the lever to try is hoisting the hazard test out of the element loop into a per-chunk any() over the already-loaded quotients, or widening the fast accept — NOT removing the deferral, which is a correctness requirement with a named probe (cargo test -p fnp-python --test conformance_diagnostics).
close_reason: MEASURED. The FE-hazard branch is a DECIDABLE_REGRESSION on the serial f64 divide kernel, replicated on two quiet hosts: vmi1293453 ratio_median 0.511 (null [0.9606,1.0136]) and hz1 ratio_median 0.295 with the harness printing verdict=DECIDABLE_REGRESSION against a very tight null [0.9947,1.0098]. Direction and decidability replicate; magnitude is host-dependent (~1.96x vs ~3.39x) so quote each host's row separately. Parallel arm: one clean sample, ratio_median 0.703 (~1.42x) on vmi1293453, PROVISIONAL - hz1 blocked before reaching it. Route share measured alongside so the kernel ratio is not read as the call's: 0.941 serial on vmi1293453, 0.615 on hz1, 0.601 parallel. Class is maintenance-self-speedup (a regression) - base arm is our own former code, never quotable against NumPy. Checksums matched former vs candidate every round, so the cost buys identical bits. Leading explanation (NOT confirmed against disassembly): the per-element q.is_normal() blocks auto-vectorisation of the divide loop. The bead's retry predicate is therefore triggered and correctly aimed - hoist the test to a per-chunk any() over already-computed quotients. The deferral itself is a correctness requirement and is not reopened by this; the measurement prices it. Instrument landed in 59332fac; five of six runs were refused by the quiescence gate on a saturated fleet and the gate was not weakened.

but do not publish a kernel ratio as if it were the call's regression. FRAME % is not REMOVABLE %.

  crates/fnp-python/benches/criterion_python_elementwise.rs
    bench_divide_fe_hazard_serial     n = 1<<20, below the kernel's 1<<21 rayon threshold
    bench_divide_fe_hazard_parallel   n = 1<<22, above it, chunked exactly as the kernel does
  Run with:
    RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- \
      env FNP_BENCH_GROUPS=bench_divide_fe_hazard \
      cargo bench --profile release-perf --bench criterion_python_elementwise

DESIGN DECISIONS WORTH NOT RE-DERIVING:
  - Operands are hazard-free by construction (every quotient in (0.5, 2), hence normal), so the
    candidate's `q.is_normal()` fast accept is taken on EVERY element. That is deliberately the
    worst case for the added branch: the path that pays the test and never gets to skip work.
  - Reading commit 47b8ad17 rather than its summary changed the instrument. The Div arm is a
    SEPARATE loop from the generic `op.apply` loop, not the old loop plus a branch. The former arm
    reproduces the old loop's SHAPE, so the ratio cannot quietly bundle in a devirtualization
    difference.
  - Each arm also times the real end-to-end fnp.divide at the same size and prints
    DIVIDE_ROUTE_SHARE, because a kernel-only ratio is a FRAME % masquerading as a REMOVABLE % and
    this repo has already retracted a row for exactly that. Read the two together or not at all.
  - The route-share arm asserts at runtime that fnp.divide is NOT numpy's object (trap 1).
  - The predicate in the bench is a REPLICA. A bench crate cannot reach that crate-root item, and
    making it `pub` to suit a benchmark is the wrong trade - I tried it, reverted it, and the
    lib.rs change in 59332fac is comment-only. The replica is pinned by DIVIDE_HAZARD_TRUTH_TABLE,
    asserted BEFORE any timing, covering every arm in both directions; lib.rs's existing unit test
    f64_divide_hazard_predicate_flags_exactly_the_ieee_exceptions pins the shipped side, and a
    comment at the predicate says both must move together.

RESULT CLASS, fixed before any number exists: the base arm is OUR OWN FORMER CODE, so whatever this
eventually measures is `**Campaign result class:** maintenance-self-speedup`. It is not an
incumbent-win and must never be quoted against NumPy.

WHY THERE IS NO NUMBER - the gate's own words, verbatim, one line per attempt:
  ovh-a  HOST_WIDE_QUIESCENCE verdict=blocked reason=host_not_quiet_after_settle:timeout_ms=30000:
         samples=100:quiet_streak=0/2:maximum_allowed_busy_pct=20.0:busy_cpus=cpu9=100.0%
  ovh-a  ...busy_cpus=cpu0=67.7%,cpu1=29.0%,cpu2=24.1%,cpu3=29.0%,cpu6=23.3%,cpu7=70.0%,
         cpu8=31.0%,cpu9=70.0%,cpu10=73.3%,cpu11=73.3%
  hz2    ...busy_cpus= all 16 CPUs, several at 100.0% (cpu1, cpu4)
Two further attempts were still in flight when I stopped; every attempt that has reported has
blocked. Direct-ssh hosts were no better: hz1 load 2.80 on 8 cores, hz2 load 6.98 on 16, and BOTH
are at 94% disk (15G and 36G free), so building a release-perf tree there is not available either.
ovh-a refuses direct ssh from this box (publickey), so the drain-one-worker-and-ssh route is not
open on the host rch keeps selecting.

I DID NOT LOWER THE BAR. Weakening or bypassing the quiescence gate to obtain a number is the named
forbidden pattern, and a ratio taken with one core pegged at 100% is exactly the trap-4 contention
artefact the gate exists to stop. A blocked gate on a saturated fleet is the correct outcome and is
reported as such.

PROVENANCE NOTE FOR WHOEVER RUNS IT: the ELF sha is NOT reproducible across builds of identical
source - three release-perf builds of commit 8f9b9e0c/59332fac produced
8c9dac06b129d0ce..., 663b41b24074698b... and c5dca743fcbd98a7... (sizes 224205496, 224205536 and
224146640 bytes). Debuginfo paths differ per worker pool. Quote the sha the harness self-reports
from inside the process, next to the worker that built it; do not expect it to match a rebuild.

MEASUREMENT HOST CAVEAT ALREADY VISIBLE: ovh-a is an 8-core/16-thread Ryzen 5800X and hz2 a
16-core EPYC-Genoa. The parallel arm's absolute numbers will be core-count sensitive, but the
former/candidate RATIO is taken on one host at one thread count, so it stays valid for the branch
cost. Name the host in the row regardless.

comments.author: CoralOak
comments.text:
MEASURED. CoralOak 2026-08-08, instrument at commit 59332fac. The branch is NOT the "~one
predictable test per element" this bead expected — it costs roughly HALF the serial kernel's
throughput. Reporting a regression plainly, which is the success condition here.

**Campaign result class:** maintenance-self-speedup (a REGRESSION). The base arm is OUR OWN FORMER
CODE, so this number says nothing about NumPy and must never be quoted against it.

HOST AND PROVENANCE. Worker vmi1293453, AMD EPYC (with IBPB), 8 physical / 8 logical, governor
unavailable. Quiescence CLEAR at both phases with maximum_observed_busy_fraction=0.000 (settle 76
samples / 22.9 s at process preflight). --profile release-perf.
bench_elf_sha256=ef96889fc55772db8fe1e9e46dbce2eb7331d2a27a5913608d36f7fd246b3b45, self-reported
from inside the process, built by vmi1293453.

SERIAL, n = 1<<20 (below the kernel's 1<<21 rayon threshold):
  null_base_aa                  ratio_median 0.997901  ci95 [0.960594, 1.013642]  cv 8.390%
  effect_former_over_candidate  ratio_median 0.511247  ci95 [0.461884, 0.531033]  cv 19.012%
  arm medians: former 0.745165 ms, candidate 1.331632 ms
  Effect CI excludes 1.0; deviation from unity 0.4888 against a required 2x-null delta of 0.0788.
  Reading: the shipped kernel takes about 1.96x the former kernel's time (1/0.511).

PARALLEL, n = 1<<22 (above the threshold, chunked as the kernel does):
  null_base_aa                  ratio_median 1.019391  ci95 [0.930542, 1.062053]  cv 23.376%
  effect_former_over_candidate  ratio_median 0.702888  ci95 [0.667230, 0.771515]  cv 23.965%
  arm medians: former 1.081207 ms, candidate 1.525291 ms
  Effect CI excludes 1.0; deviation 0.2971 against a required 2x-null delta of 0.1389.
  Reading: about 1.42x the former kernel's time.
Both nulls sit near unity and both effects clear twice the null half-width, so both rows are
decidable. cv is provenance only.

CHECKSUMS MATCHED between former and candidate in every round (the harness asserts it), so the two
arms computed bit-identical output — the regression is pure cost, not a different answer.

THE ROUTE SHARE, which is the number that stops this being a FRAME % dressed up as a REMOVABLE %:
  serial    end_to_end 1,414,937 ns   kernel 1,331,632 ns   kernel_share 0.941
  parallel  end_to_end 2,537,486 ns   kernel 1,525,291 ns   kernel_share 0.601
At 1M the kernel IS essentially the whole call, so the kernel regression passes through almost
undiluted. ARITHMETIC ESTIMATE, clearly labelled as such because the former ROUTE no longer exists
to be called end to end: substituting the former kernel's time into the measured call gives roughly
0.83 ms vs 1.41 ms serial (~0.59) and 2.09 ms vs 2.54 ms parallel (~0.83). Do not quote those as
measured A/Bs.

WHY IT IS THIS BIG — HYPOTHESIS, NOT MEASURED. A per-element `q.is_normal()` almost certainly
blocks auto-vectorisation of the divide loop: the former loop is a straight `*s = x / y` that
vectorises to vdivpd, the candidate interleaves a scalar predicate and a data-dependent OR. That
would explain ~2x on the serial path and a smaller ratio on the parallel path, where memory
bandwidth caps the win vectorisation could give. I did NOT confirm this against the disassembly, so
treat it as the leading explanation, not a finding.

THE RETRY PREDICATE IS TRIGGERED. This bead's own predicate says: if the clean-path regression
exceeds the null envelope, the lever is hoisting the hazard test out of the element loop into a
per-chunk any() over the already-loaded quotients, or widening the fast accept — NOT removing the
deferral. That is exactly the right lever if the vectorisation hypothesis holds: compute the
quotient vector first, then test normality across the vector, which keeps both the divide and the
test vectorised. Worth a follow-up bead; I am not opening it speculatively without the disassembly.

WHAT IS NOT ON THE TABLE. The deferral is a correctness requirement with a named probe
(cargo test -p fnp-python --test conformance_diagnostics). A 2x kernel regression does not reopen
it — 2nmd1 traded throughput for a warning numpy raises and we cannot, and that trade stands. This
measurement prices it; it does not relitigate it.

REPLICATION STATUS, stated rather than implied: this is ONE clean run. The standing rule here is to
replicate before quoting a sub-2x ratio, and the parallel row (1.42x) is sub-2x. A replication was
launched and had not returned when I wrote this. Treat the parallel row as provisional until a
second quiet-host sample lands; the serial row's effect is far enough outside its null that a
second sample is confirmation rather than adjudication.

GETTING A QUIET HOST WAS MOST OF THE WORK: six attempts, five refused by
require_host_wide_benchmark_exclusivity on a saturated fleet — ovh-a twice (cpu9 at 100%, then 10
CPUs busy), hz2 twice (all 16 busy, several at 100%), vmi1293453 once (all 8 at ~100%) — and one
clear window on vmi1293453. I did not weaken the gate; the blocked runs are what a shared fleet
looks like and the gate is doing its job.

FOLLOW-UP NOT DONE: a docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md row for this. The preflight was CLEAR so nothing
blocks writing one, and the numbers above are what it would carry, but the ledger's REJECT-row
contract is written for rejected hypotheses and this is a priced correctness fix; someone should
decide which heading it belongs under rather than have me improvise one.

comments.author: CoralOak
comments.text:
REPLICATION ADDENDUM, same day. The SERIAL row replicated on a SECOND quiet host and the harness printed its own verdict; the PARALLEL row did not get a second sample.

hz1 (hetzner1, AMD EPYC-Milan, 4 physical / 8 logical), --profile release-perf, bench_elf_sha256=c3043d7bb72fb7016aa83ca0626ea3dec7a6d1a4cb63fe3afd9a0cad3d94f8fc:
  null_base_aa   ratio_median 1.002236  ci95 [0.994719, 1.009837]  cv 10.505%   <- a very tight null
  effect         ratio_median 0.295495  ci95 [0.267860, 0.305764]  cv 11.847%
  MEDIAN_CI_GATE row=divide_fe_hazard_branch_serial_1m verdict=DECIDABLE_REGRESSION
    effect_ci_excludes_one=true null_half_width=0.009837 required_2x_delta=0.019675
  DIVIDE_ROUTE_SHARE serial end_to_end 2,661,744 ns  kernel 1,638,203 ns  kernel_share 0.615
Checksums matched former vs candidate in every round again.

SO THE DIRECTION AND THE DECIDABILITY REPLICATE; THE MAGNITUDE DOES NOT, and that is expected rather than alarming. vmi1293453 read 0.511 (~1.96x) and hz1 reads 0.295 (~3.39x) for the same ELF-equivalent build on the same source. This repo's standing finding is that the HOST MOVES RATIOS materially and that cross-entry ratio comparison is invalid — prefer same-invocation rows. Quote each host's row with its host named; do not average them and do not treat 3.39x as an upgrade of 1.96x. The kernel share also moved with the host (0.941 on vmi1293453, 0.615 on hz1), which is most of why the end-to-end consequence differs.

PARALLEL IS STILL A SINGLE SAMPLE. The hz1 run reached the serial arm, then exited 2 when the parallel arm's own quiescence preflight blocked — hz1 had gone busy again. So the 1.42x parallel figure from vmi1293453 stands unreplicated and remains provisional, exactly as flagged in the previous comment. The serial figure no longer needs that caveat.

Neither host is large: 8 logical on vmi1293453, 8 logical on hz1. A ratio measured where vectorisation is the suspected mechanism is not obviously core-count sensitive, but the parallel arm's absolute times certainly are, so a big-host sample would still be worth having.

comments.author: CoralOak
comments.text:
LIMITATION OF MY OWN INSTRUMENT, found while designing the follow-up (deadlock-audit-ae85t) and recorded here rather than left for someone to trip over.

The bench arms operate on plain &[f64] / &mut [f64]. The shipped PARALLEL path does the same - par_chunks_mut over real slices - so the parallel row (ratio_median 0.703) transfers to production directly. The shipped SERIAL path does NOT: it iterates output.iter().zip(a_in.iter()).zip(b_in.iter()) over Cell<f64> / ReadOnlyCell<f64>, not plain slices.

So the serial ratios I reported (0.511 on vmi1293453, 0.295 on hz1) are the cost of the LOOP SHAPE measured on plain slices. They are a sound measurement of the branch's cost in that shape, and the DECIDABLE_REGRESSION verdict stands for what was measured - but they are not a measured property of the shipped serial loop, because Cell access may vectorise differently. My closing summary said the former arm 'reproduces the old loop's shape'; that is exact for the parallel arm and approximate for the serial one, and I should have said so.

This does not change the conclusion that the branch is expensive, the retry predicate is still triggered, and the parallel row is unaffected. It does mean nobody should quote 1.96x-3.39x as the shipped serial regression without re-measuring in the Cell shape. Carried into ae85t's description as a bound on what that lever can claim.

comments.author: CoralOak
comments.text:
MECHANISM RESOLVED BY DISASSEMBLY - my 'blocks auto-vectorisation' explanation was WRONG, and the correct one is better. Full detail on deadlock-audit-ae85t; recorded here because this bead is where the hypothesis was published.

objdump of the release-perf bench ELF on hz1, per #[inline(never)] kernel:
  divide_former_serial     insns=40   vector=7   vdivpd=1
  divide_candidate_serial  insns=186  vector=91  vdivpd=1
Both vectorise; the candidate still emits vdivpd. Vectorisation was never lost.

What costs the time is that LLVM if-converted the WHOLE predicate into branchless vector masks and evaluates every arm on every block - the NaN checks, b == 0, both infinity tests and the subnormal comparison - for elements that will never need them (vpor 7, vpand 7, vandpd 5, vpcmpeqq 3, vpandn 2, vcmpneqpd 2, vptest 1, vpcmpgtq 1, ...). 7 vector instructions became 91 around one vdivpd. That explains 1.96x-3.39x without any vectorisation story.

Corollary worth knowing: the source-level 'fast accept' (if q.is_normal() { return false }) buys NOTHING after if-conversion - there is no branch left to take, the rare arms run anyway and get masked away. 2nmd1's comment describes it as 'the only test a clean divide pays', and at source level that is true; at machine level it is not.

The measured numbers in this bead are unaffected - they were always end-of-kernel timings, not a mechanism claim. Only the explanation changes.

title: [ci][conformance] G2 red: 2 diagnostic tests need numpy in G2 + 4 differential suites have STALE goldens (fnp is correct vs numpy 2.4.3)
description:
G1 was fixed (deadlock-audit-ha63z) which UNBLOCKED G2 (cargo test --workspace), revealing 6 PRE-EXISTING fnp-conformance failures (209 passed, 6 failed) — none caused by the lint/loadtxt commits. Two independent root causes:

(1) NUMPY-ENV GAP: G2 has no numpy (only G3 runs setup-python + pip install numpy). Tests diagnostic_oracle::tests::diagnostic_oracle_evaluates_success_exception_and_warnings and dtype_shape_diagnostics::tests::dtype_shape_diagnostics_oracle_report_matches_expectations genuinely require a live numpy oracle (the latter sets require_numpy:true; the former expects numpy-produced ValueError/reshape exceptions). Fix: add actions/setup-python@v5 +  to the g2-unit-property job in .github/workflows/ci.yml, mirroring g3-differential lines 75-78.

(2) STALE GOLDEN FIXTURES: tests::{fft,polynomial,signal}_differential_suite_is_green + core_suites_are_green fail on hardcoded expected_values in crates/fnp-conformance/fixtures/{fft,polynomial,signal}_differential_cases.json that no longer match numpy. VERIFIED with local numpy 2.4.3 that FNP IS CORRECT and the GOLDENS ARE WRONG:
  - chebint([2,3]) deg1: numpy=[0.75,2,0.75]=fnp, golden(WRONG)=[0.0,2,0.75]
  - legint([2,3]): numpy=[0.5,2,1]=fnp, golden(WRONG)=[-1,2,1]

  Pattern: goldens carry a first-coefficient (integration constant) of 0 that current numpy does not produce. Likely captured under an older numpy or a k=0/lbnd convention that changed. Also affects fft (hfft_n6_golden) and signal (kaiser_10_golden). No regeneration binary exists; expected_values are hand-authored JSON consumed by ufunc_differential.rs/lib.rs. Fix: recompute expected_values from numpy 2.4.3 for every failing case and update the fixtures (fnp already matches numpy, so this is pure golden correction, NOT masking an fnp bug — confirm each against numpy before writing). Then G2 goes green with the numpy addition from (1). Scope: enumerate ALL failing cases (not just the 4 named), verify each against numpy, update JSON, re-run cargo test -p fnp-conformance --lib via rch.

(1) numpy added to G2 in ci.yml; (2) polynomial+signal stale goldens corrected to numpy 2.4.3 (fnp was correct); (3) uncovered+fixed a REAL fnp bug — irfft two-for-one path leaked a complex Nyquist into a DC offset (hfft +1.0), gated fast path on real DC/Nyquist (commit cabb00e5). rch: all 4 differential suites + 14 fft roundtrip tests green.

title: [perf][fnp-ufunc][no-gaps] convolve/correlate large-N short-kernel tail ~10x — cache/profiling
description: After the short-kernel gather (8f1c9473), convolve/correlate match numpy at moderate N (50K-200K, parity-to-faster for m=8..96) but the LARGE-N tail (n>=1M, short m) is still ~10x slower. numpy scales LINEARLY (200K 273us -> 1M 1382us = 5x for 5x data); our gather is SUPERLINEAR = cache thrashing, despite +avx2 and single-write streaming. Needs perf stat cache-miss profiling on a QUIET box (load was 20+ when characterized, perf A/B unreliable). Candidate causes: (1) vec![0.0;full_len] zero-init is WASTED for the gather (each output written exactly once with =, not +=) — 2x write traffic + page faults at 8MB; safe-Rust uninit is the blocker. (2) overlapping-window redundant L1 loads (each input read ~m times). (3) write-allocate on output stores (no non-temporal). Likely fix: avoid the zero-init waste and/or a cache-blocked output tiling. See memory convolve-short-kernel-gather.
close_reason: Measured no-ship. Added a temporary Criterion row for production convolve large-N short-kernel gather, then removed it after rejection. Baseline on vmi1149989 with RAYON_NUM_THREADS=16: convprod_short_tail_1000000x8/prod_convolve [1.2476, 1.4414, 1.5998] ms. Trialed one source lever: replace the short-kernel gather output vec![0.0; full_len] plus slice writes with Vec::with_capacity(full_len) and ordered pushes/extend_from_slice, preserving the same scalar and SIMD accumulation order. Proof passed on vmi1149989: convolve_1d_parallel_matches_scatter_reference bit-reference test. Rebench on same worker rejected the lever: [1.3989, 1.6441, 1.9545] ms, about 14.1% slower by center with wider noise. Source and temporary benchmark hunks manually unwound; no fnp-ufunc code kept. Next route: do not retry allocation-construction for this tail; profile cache misses and attack true redundant input-window traffic with output tiling or a different streaming primitive.

title: [perf][fnp-python] extend the no-op reshape skip to HIGHER RANKS by allocating at the final shape
description:
NEXT LEVER on the campaign's worst measured vs-incumbent ratio - the ~7-8 us PyUFunc per-call floor, 7.97x slower than NumPy at n=256 (deadlock-audit-isnd2).

WHERE THIS COMES FROM. finish_flat_output (landed caaa50ae, deadlock-audit-omyno) skips the reshape only at rank 1, because that is the only rank where the flat buffer already has the target shape. deadlock-audit-6twge measured that skip at 200 ns per call. Every HIGHER-rank call still pays a real reshape.

THE LEVER: allocate the output at its FINAL shape instead of flat-then-reshape. numpy.empty accepts a shape tuple directly, so a route that knows its output shape up front never needs the reshape at all. If numpy.empty(shape) costs about the same as numpy.empty(n) - which is the open question - this extends a 200 ns saving from the 1-D case to every rank, at every one of the 62 sites.

WHAT MUST BE MEASURED FIRST, and the bench is already written and registered: bench_output_construction_decomposition in criterion_python_elementwise.rs (landed adff2036, NOT yet run). It times, in ONE invocation on ONE worker: getattr('empty') alone, allocation alone, allocation + the no-op reshape, allocation + a REAL reshape to a different rank, and allocation DIRECTLY at the final 2-D shape. Run it with FNP_BENCH_GROUPS=bench_output_construction_decomposition.

DECISION RULE:
  allocating_at_final_shape_saves_ns clearly positive -> the lever is real; change the *_flat helpers to take the target shape and allocate at it, and finish_flat_output collapses to an identity for every rank except 0-D.
  about zero -> the reshape is not where the cost is; do NOT make the change, and the remaining output-construction cost is in the allocation itself, which is a different and harder problem.
Bank either way.

WHY THE MEASUREMENT CANNOT BE SKIPPED: the numbers that suggest this lever (220 ns empty, 1310 ns empty+reshape, 200 ns isolated reshape) come from THREE different workers with THREE different harnesses and do not add up - 220+200=420, not 1310. Subtracting across rows like that already overstated one lever by 5.5x in this same chain. The ~890 ns gap is not evidence until it is reproduced in one invocation.

CONSTRAINT: /data sits at 59G against a 59G build floor. Check df -h /data yourself before starting - the number moves within seconds and has been stale in both directions.
close_reason:
MEASURED then IMPLEMENTED, both landed in 7c04bef0 with the row and the test. The decision rule in this bead was written BEFORE the measurement and it came out clearly positive, so the lever was taken.

WORKER hetzner1, ONE invocation, batched 256 reps minus a measured empty loop, HARNESS batched_min_of_401_minus_empty_loop:
  numpy.empty(n) flat                382.44 ns
  numpy.empty(shape) at final rank   372.23 ns   NOT more expensive - slightly cheaper
  + a REAL reshape to rank 2         435.43 ns   what this removes
  + a NO-OP reshape to rank 1        417.59 ns
  allocating at final shape saves    445.65 ns
  getattr('empty') alone             110.09 ns
  empty loop                           0.43 ns

CHANGE: zerocopy_f64_binary_flat allocates at the final shape, so the route reshapes at NO rank. finish_preshaped_output is left with only the 0-D rule, where NumPy returns a scalar rather than a 0-D array. finish_flat_output, which I had added earlier this session for the rank-1-skip plan, is REMOVED rather than left dead - it was the right abstraction for the wrong fix, and leaving it would also have breached the allow(dead_code) budget at 65/65.

THE TELL, worth carrying forward: a NO-OP reshape costs 417.59 ns against a REAL one's 435.43 ns - 96%. The price is the Python call, not the shape work. That is why removing the call is the whole lever and why optimising the reshape's arguments would have bought nothing.

SAFETY CHECKED BEFORE MOVING THE ALLOCATION because the failure mode is SILENT: PyO3's PyBuffer::as_mut_slice requires only !readonly() && is_c_contiguous() and returns item_count() elements - it does NOT require ndim == 1 (pyo3-0.29.2 src/buffer.rs). numpy.empty(shape) is C-contiguous by default so the flat write loop is unchanged at any rank. Had that been wrong, as_mut_slice returns None, the route returns Ok(None) and defers to NumPy, and every conformance test still passes while the fast path quietly disappears.

TWO THINGS THIS BEAD LEAVES BEHIND:
  deadlock-audit-omyno's fix shape is SUPERSEDED - the 62-site conversion should move each allocation to the target shape, not add a rank-1 skip. Its site audit and type contract carry over unchanged.
  A second lever fell out of the same row and is filed as deadlock-audit-v8nx6: getattr('empty') is 110.09 ns, 29% of the shaped allocation, and cydda separately measured py.import('numpy') at 310 ns per call. Same mechanism, different risk class.

NOT DONE, and named rather than implied: the code is rustfmt-checked only. The conformance test written for it (shape/ndim/dtype/type/bytes at ranks 0/1/2/3 plus a size above the parallel gates) has NOT been run - /data fell to 58G and this turn's one permitted build went to the measurement. Gate with cargo test -j2 -p fnp-python --test conformance_ufunc_edge. The 445.65 ns is also single-worker; replicate before quoting it as a fleet figure.
