title: perf(matmul/dot): seventeen gates each re-read shape+dtype before declining - one shared classification takes the 1-D dot product from 4.474x to 1.434x and 8x8 f64 from 4.561x to 1.790x
description:
MEASURED, TanBridge, thinkstation1, numpy 2.4.3 live, fnp .so sha256 096aaf7cfaf38735efe0c452...
(shipped `3eec9440`; BEFORE `6426b4c8a40a` at `d1b1429d`).

## THE DEFECT: SEVENTEEN GATES, NO SHARED FACTS

`matmul` is a chain of ELEVEN `try_*` gates and `dot` is SIX. Each one opens by re-reading `shape`
- a FRESH `Vec<usize>` per operand per gate - plus its own dtype (several `extract::<String>()` the
kind, which allocates) and its own `flags.c_contiguous`, before it can decline. Nothing was cached
between them, and each gate also re-ran its own `kwargs.is_empty()` / `out is None` check.

An operand pair that NO gate can accept therefore paid the whole chain. Two 1-D operands - the
plain dot product - are exactly that pair: every gate needs at least one operand of rank >= 2.

The excess is FLAT in n, which is what identifies it as the chain and not the arithmetic:

```
  matmul 1-D @ 1-D f64  2^8   +2540.8 ns    2^13  +2740.7 ns    2^16  +3287.8 ns
```

## THE FIX

One read of `(rank, dtype kind, itemsize)` per operand, once, up front - the question every gate
asks first - then a plan of six NECESSARY conditions lifted straight from the gates:
`{f64,int,f16} x {flat, batched}`. `_flat` gates need both ranks <= 2 (the lowest-rank of them is
the integer vecmat, 1-D @ 2-D); `_batched` gates need one operand of rank >= 3. The gates are
otherwise UNCHANGED - the plan only decides which are worth calling.

An operand that is not an EXACT ndarray classifies as UNKNOWN and still walks the whole chain,
because the f64 GEMM gate admits ndarray SUBCLASSES through `is_instance` where every other gate
uses `is_exact_instance`. That asymmetry is the one thing that makes a blanket shortcut unsafe.

## MEASUREMENT (same invocation, ABBAABBA, 25 rounds, dual A/A null, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1)

```
  case                     BEFORE                      AFTER
  matmul 1-D 2^8    4.474x [4.340,4.492]  ->  1.434x [1.362,1.489]
  matmul 1-D 2^10   4.396x [4.031,4.444]  ->  1.437x [1.377,1.482]
  matmul 1-D 2^13   2.648x [2.470,2.691]  ->  1.222x [1.140,1.247]
  matmul 1-D 2^16   1.378x [1.304,1.388]  ->  1.052x [0.998,1.145]
  dot    1-D 2^8    3.775x [3.713,3.867]  ->  1.590x [1.435,1.664]
  dot    1-D 2^10   3.642x [3.327,3.746]  ->  1.577x [1.464,1.649]
  dot    1-D 2^13   2.006x [1.907,2.041]  ->  1.224x [1.148,1.263]
  matmul 8x8   f64  4.561x [4.319,4.621]  ->  1.790x [1.703,1.849]
  matmul 32x32 f64  2.341x [2.307,2.390]  ->  1.329x [1.264,1.353]
  matmul 64x64 f64  1.337x [1.328,1.346]  ->  1.077x [0.968,1.102]
  matmul 8x8   i64  3.780x [3.551,3.848]  ->  1.904x [1.747,1.937]
  matmul 4x256@256x4 3.350x [3.157,3.464] ->  1.559x [1.512,1.581]
  matmul 70x70 i64  0.881x WIN (BIASED)   ->  0.811x WIN [0.704,0.898]
```

Every BEFORE/AFTER pair of ranges is DISJOINT. All AFTER nulls PASS except `matmul 8x8 i64`
(candidate null 0.9768) - disclosed, not dropped. The 70x70 i64 cell's BEFORE null was BIASED
(1.0266) and its AFTER null passes, so only the AFTER figure is quotable there.

STAGED, and the stages are separable: a first build carried only the three dtype-family booleans
(sha `548eb928a6f2`) and read 8x8 f64 at 2.209x; adding the flat/batched rank split took the same
cell to 1.790x and 8x8 i64 from 2.460x to 1.904x. The rank split is worth roughly as much as the
dtype split on the small 2-D shapes.

PARITY: 10 dtypes x 10 shape pairs x {matmul, dot}, plus mixed dtypes, strided, F-order,
transposed, lists, 0-d scalars, `np.matrix`, nan/inf payloads, empty k=0 and m=0, shape mismatch,
`out=` at three shapes and a `casting=` kwarg - compared on dtype, shape and RAW BYTES, and on
exception type+message where numpy raises. BEFORE 4 divergences, AFTER 4, all four the same
pre-existing longdouble padding-byte artifact of the probe's own `tobytes()`. 0 INTRODUCED.
654 lib tests pass; `cargo clippy -p fnp-python --lib --tests` clean; `cargo fmt` a no-op.

MEMORY: largest operand 512 KB (2^16 f64); host `used` 57 GB of 215 throughout.

RETRY PREDICATE / WHAT IS LEFT. The residual is now the ordinary small-n entry floor plus whatever
the SURVIVING gates read:
  - `matmul 8x8 f64` at 1.790x still runs the f64 GEMM metadata gate, which re-reads shape AND
    `extract::<String>()`s both dtype kinds. Threading `MatmulOperandFacts` INTO that gate is the
    obvious next lever and is NOT attempted here.
  - `np.inner` has the same shape of loss (2.670x at 2^8, +986 ns flat) and was NOT touched.
  - `np.vdot` is already at 1.019-1.196x; leave it.
Do not re-attack the gate ORDER or the per-gate kwargs checks - both are gone.
close_reason: SHIPPED 3eec9440 (+ a comment-only follow-up fixing the bead id). matmul 1-D 4.474x -> 1.434x at 2^8 and 1.378x -> 1.052x at 2^16; dot 1-D 3.775x -> 1.590x; matmul 8x8 f64 4.561x -> 1.790x, 32x32 2.341x -> 1.329x, 64x64 1.337x -> 1.077x; 8x8 i64 3.780x -> 1.904x; 4x256@256x4 3.350x -> 1.559x. All BEFORE/AFTER ranges DISJOINT, all AFTER nulls PASS except 8x8 i64 (0.9768, disclosed). Parity 0 introduced across 10 dtypes x 10 shape pairs x 2 ops plus 20 edge cases, raw-byte compared. elf 096aaf7cfaf3. Next lever NOT taken: thread the facts INTO the f64 GEMM metadata gate, and np.inner has the same shape of loss (+986 ns flat, 2.670x at 2^8).

title: [perf][fnp-python][no-gaps] zero-copy np.ma.filled f64 — 25x self, beats numpy
close_reason: Shipped. np.ma.filled on a float64 MaskedArray was 13x SLOWER than numpy (87ms vs 12.9ms@4M): the generic path extracts data AND mask into owned Vecs (extract_numeric_masked_array), builds a MaskedArray, clones the data, then builds the output = ~3+ full-size 32MB copies. Pure element selection -> bit-identical to the generic path (np.array_equal incl nan). Gates: f64 MaskedArray, contiguous, scalar-float fill (explicit arg or array fill_value); else defer. close_reason: Shipped 12178cb9. Root cause was a mis-tuned panel width: cholesky_blocked factors each nb-wide diagonal block with an UNBLOCKED scalar kernel (O(nb^3/3) scalar flops/panel), and the fixed CHOL_PANEL_NB=128 for n>=896 serialized far more scalar work than the parallel trailing GEMM saved. n<896 already used a 32/64 mid panel near parity. title: perf(fnp-ufunc): merge-based f64 setxor1d (2.6-4.0x)
close_reason: Shipped. f64 setxor1d was the worst set op (~5x vs numpy): it did THREE comparator-closure sorts (a, b, then the result) plus TWO per-element binary-search passes. Replaced with the integer-key sort-unique (sorted_dedup_float_set, from the prior set-op commit) + a single linear two-pointer merge that emits the symmetric difference already sorted. Each side's NaN kept once (NaN!=NaN; np.setxor1d([nan],[nan])==[nan,nan]); +-0.0 equal. Score old/new: 3.98x[20k]/2.64x[200k]. Parity: 600 randomized cases (NaN/+-0/inf/empty/dup) + 1203-case unique/union/setxor sweep byte-match numpy; 54 unit tests. NOTE: a unique()/union1d f64 fast-path was tried+REVERTED — the key-transform's 2 extra passes (build keys, map back) LOSE to those ops' existing PARALLEL in-place f64 sort at large n (union1d regressed to 0.76x@200k). setxor wins because its old path had no parallel sort, just 3 serial sorts.

title: [perf][fnp-python] cov/corrcoef: zero-copy Gram into numpy buffer + parallel centering (unlocks fused mirror; est. flips cov 2000x500 to a win)
description:
Follow-up to the MR=4 Gram tile (cc_fnp, 2026-07-09). See docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md '2026-07-09 - REJECT: fusing the symmetric mirror'.

STATE: cov 2000x500 is the ONLY remaining loss in the cov/corrcoef/batched-LU lane vs ORIG NumPy 1.26 (fnp 39.9ms vs ORIG 19.9ms = 0.50x). The MR=4 tile made the Gram 1.87x faster (25.3 -> 13.5ms) but ~26ms of the call is NOT the Gram.

WHERE THE ~26ms GOES (measured, 2000x500):
  - serial mirror pass at end of cov_gram_from_centered: ~8.5ms cold (8M strided page-faulting scalar writes)
  - build_square_f64_matrix: SERIAL scalar copy of the 32MiB result into numpy.empty via
      for (slot, val) in output.iter().zip(values) { slot.set(val) }
    plus a redundant intermediate 32MiB Vec allocation
  - cov_gram_rowvar_f64 / cov_gram_two_rowvar_f64: per-row centering loop is SERIAL (mean + subtract)

PLAN (3 sub-levers, each measurable):
  1. build_square_f64_matrix -> parallel copy using the existing from_raw_parts_mut idiom (as used by try_native_string_searchsorted et al).
  2. Better: compute the Gram DIRECTLY into the numpy empty buffer. Introduce build_square_f64_matrix_with(py, numpy, n_vars, fill: impl FnOnce(&mut [f64])) and a cov_gram_into(centered, .., out). Kills the intermediate Vec AND the copy. corrcoef_normalize_in_place then operates on that same &mut [f64]. Blast radius: 4 call sites (lib.rs ~33357/33506/33552/33570).
  3. Parallelize the centering loop (par_chunks_mut over rows).
  THEN re-enable the FUSED symmetric mirror in the kernel: it is 1.27x faster standalone (13.54 -> 10.62ms) but currently a NET LOSS (pipeline 31.2 -> 47.1ms) because the serial consumer must snoop 32MiB of dirty lines back across the 5975WX's 8 CCDs. With a parallel/zero-copy consumer that penalty disappears.

BUDGET: Gram ~10.6ms (fused) + centering ~0.5ms + numpy alloc ~1-3ms = 13-15ms vs ORIG 19.9ms -> 1.3-1.5x WIN, flipping the last loss in the lane.

GATES: cov parity bar is np.allclose and NOTHING pins its bits; the MR=4 tile is bit-identical (sha256 80883e51...f3bf over 13 shapes x cov/corrcoef x ddof). Keep that property if cheap. NEVER link C BLAS/LAPACK/XLA (standing directive; supersedes bead deadlock-audit-cblas-large-gram-lever-8lnzn).
MEASURE: interleaved old/new processes, min-over-N rounds, carry an untouched matmul 2048^2 gauge (this box swings; a gauge != 1.0 invalidates the run). Bench the KERNEL AND ITS CONSUMER together.
close_reason: Zero-copy Gram lever REJECTED with numbers (ledger 2026-07-10); premise corrected (cov 2000x500 never a loss, fnp 2.4x faster than ORIG); profile-led successor lever SHIPPED: check-free chunks_exact Gram strip micro-kernel, bit-identical, 1.05-1.08x e2e interleaved / 1.06-1.17x criterion (659e1793+fd00461c). Follow-ups: fault-storm root-cause in deadlock-audit-83ldf; rayon-imbalance + j-panel questions in ledger OPEN section.

title: perf: MISSING SIZE FLOORS ARE A FAMILY DEFECT, not a concatenate one - eight more routes engage at every size and lose to numpy below their crossover
description:
OPENED BY THE ROUTE-FLOOR SWEEP (crates/fnp-python/examples/h2h_route_floors.rs), written after
the concatenate crossover shipped in deadlock-audit-66w2d. worker hz4 (64 cores, loadavg 23),
numpy 2.5.2 live in the same invocation, seed 555, twelve routes x seven sizes, interleaved
ABBAABBA with dual A/A nulls and the incumbent-spread criterion.

THE CONCATENATE DEFECT WAS NOT CONCATENATE-SHAPED. Every route below engages natively at EVERY
size and none of them marks a crossover, so each loses to numpy under it. Ratios, f64:

  route     2^3     2^8     2^12    2^16    2^18    2^20    2^22     verdict
  sqrt     2.067   1.597   0.696   0.540   0.483   0.271   0.400    CROSSOVER ~2^10
  abs      1.699   1.527   1.204   0.933   0.952   0.899   0.552    CROSSOVER ~2^14
  isnan    1.899   1.837   1.351   1.028   1.010   0.977   0.911    CROSSOVER ~2^15
  max      1.152   1.209   1.476   1.182   1.052   1.022   0.199    CROSSOVER ~2^21
  argmax   1.048   1.121   1.638   1.150   1.055   1.013   0.164    CROSSOVER ~2^21
  sum      1.113   1.122   1.091   1.039   1.015   1.057   0.190    CROSSOVER ~2^21
  mean     1.080   1.086   1.074   1.036   1.019   1.127   0.187    CROSSOVER ~2^21
  divide   1.431   1.362   1.128   1.022   1.007   1.004   0.493    CROSSOVER ~2^21
  add      1.348   1.285   1.096   1.015   1.014   1.002   1.001    NEVER WINS
  multiply 1.319   1.305   1.109   1.015   1.015   1.013   1.007    NEVER WINS
  asarray  1.260   1.282   1.296   1.212   1.235   1.227   1.309    NEVER WINS
  clip     0.810   0.799   0.813   0.690   0.708   0.821   0.521    WINS EVERYWHERE - leave alone

Nulls are clean and incumbent spreads are 1.1-11% on essentially every losing cell, so the losses
are decidable; the 2^22 win rows are the noisy ones (16-31% spread, several VOID) and are quoted
only to LOCATE the crossover, not as win claims.

THREE DISTINCT ACTIONS FALL OUT, and they are not the same action:
  1. ROUTES WITH A CROSSOVER need a floor at it: sqrt (~2^10), abs (~2^14), isnan (~2^15), and the
     reduction family max/argmax/sum/mean plus divide (~2^21). Worst absolute excesses are
     max +2199 ns at 2^16, argmax +1958 at 2^12, max +1706 at 2^12.
  2. ROUTES THAT NEVER WIN should not have a native path in the measured range at all: add,
     multiply, asarray. add and multiply are PARITY above 2^16 (1.00-1.015x, NOISE>EFFECT) and a
     1.10-1.35x LOSS below it, so there is no size where the native route earns its keep.
  3. clip WINS AT EVERY SIZE (0.52-0.82x). It is the control that proves this is not 'native is
     always bad' - and it must not be touched.

DELEGATING IS NOT FREE, and the concatenate work priced it: recovering the excess is partial
because our wrapper still pays its own argument handling plus numpy's call on top. For concatenate
that recovered 68% (f32 +4618 -> +1457). For these smaller excesses the wrapper floor may eat most
of the gain, so EVERY floor here has to be measured after landing, not assumed. The concatenate
lane also proved the placement matters: a floor put above a CHEAP native route made it slower.

METHOD: h2h_route_floors.rs, same seed, and a MANY-CORE host. A first run of this same probe on
vmi1227854 (1-2 cores) produced VOID or NOISE>EFFECT on nearly every cell - rayon cannot engage
there, so the native routes are measured in a regime that is not the shipping one. Name the worker.

ACCEPTANCE: per route attacked, either the excess drops by more than the control floor with tests
green, or an honest null recorded saying the wrapper cost dominates.
notes:
HONEST NULL: sum/mean are NOT gateable, because their only above-the-floor cell is not measurable.

By the excess-to-wrapper-floor criterion this vein established, sum and mean looked like the next
targets: the route sweep put them at +13399 (sum) and +29479 (mean) ns at 2^20, comfortably above
the ~700-1450 ns wrapper floor, while their small-n excesses (+354 to +917) sit below it and are
therefore out of scope by the same rule. So the whole case rested on the 2^20 cell.

RE-MEASURED with rounds raised from 4 to 8, hz4 at loadavg 10.1 - the quietest this worker has
been all session, numpy 2.5.2 live in the same invocation:

  op    2^19              2^20                      2^21              2^22
  sum   1.003x (2.5%)     1.191x SPREAD 268.5% VOID  0.275x (49.4%)    0.224x (47.2%)
  mean  1.005x (33.1%)    1.137x SPREAD  23.0%       0.244x VOID       0.222x VOID
  std   0.779x            0.449x                     0.383x (2.9%)     0.457x (9.7%)
  sqrt  0.281x (control)  0.235x VOID                0.223x (2.9%)     0.396x (6.6%)

THE INCUMBENT'S OWN ARM SWINGS 268.5% WITHIN A SINGLE RUN AT 2^20. That is not a ratio with error
bars on it; it is not a measurement. Raising rounds did not help, and the quiet host did not help.
2^19 is parity (1.003x/1.005x) and 2^21/2^22 are large wins, so there is no decidable loss to gate
anywhere on these two routes.

*** THIS INDEPENDENTLY RE-CONFIRMS deadlock-audit-qpylx BY A DIFFERENT ROUTE. *** That bead closed
sum/mean at f64 2^20 as not decidable after four dedicated measurements spanning 1.094-1.456x. A
different harness, a different session, five months of shipping in between, and the same cell is
still un-measurable - now with the mechanism visible as a 268.5% incumbent spread rather than
inferred from run-to-run disagreement. The 8 MiB band on this fleet is a measurement trap and the
right response to it is to decline to rank, not to average harder.

RETRY PREDICATE: do not open a lever on sum or mean at 2^20 from any harness on this fleet. Their
small-n excess is real but BELOW the wrapper floor, so the unary reject already covers it. If the
wrapper floor is ever reduced, both become interesting again - and that is the bead to write.

RUNNING TALLY FOR THIS VEIN: 2 ships (minmax entry c58b353f, predicates fb0d73b2), 2 honest nulls
(the f64 unary floor, and now sum/mean), 1 dead conformance test revived. The law that came out of
the first null - gate only where the excess is several times the wrapper's own delegation cost -
has now correctly predicted both a ship (predicates, 3-150x the floor) and a null (sum/mean, whose
only qualifying cell cannot be measured).
close_reason:
VEIN WORKED OUT: 2 ships, 2 honest nulls, 1 dead conformance test revived, and a LAW that now governs the successor.

SHIPPED
  c58b353f  min/max/argmin/argmax entry - the 16 MiB floor read FIRST instead of last in a
            five-way disjunction, and the delegate lookup moved into the fallback.
            max n=2^3 1.152x -> 1.007x; argmax n=2^3 1.048x -> 0.845x (a WIN).
  fb0d73b2  the f64 predicate family - signbit and isinf NEVER win and now delegate; isfinite and
            isnan gated at the size each was measured to cross.
            signbit 2^20 +87373 -> +699 ns; isinf 2^22 +220656 -> +7488 ns.

REJECTED, both recorded with retry predicates
  the f64 unary floor at 2^11 - implemented at both call sites, tests green, and REVERTED because
  half of it was inert and the rest sat at the noise boundary.
  sum/mean at 2^20 - the only cell above the floor, and the incumbent arm swings 268.5% within a
  single run on the quietest hz4 of the session. Independently re-confirms deadlock-audit-qpylx.

*** THE LAW, which is the durable output: A FLOOR ONLY PAYS WHERE THE NATIVE ROUTE COSTS SEVERAL
TIMES THE WRAPPER OWN DELEGATION COST. *** Delegating is not free - the wrapper still pays its
argument handling plus numpy's call, ~700-1450 ns on this host. concatenate's byte mover cost
+4650 and the floor recovered 68%; the predicates cost +4700 to +220000 and recovery was
near-total; the unary family cost +530 to +1025 against the same floor and there was nothing to
recover. The law predicted both the ship and the null before either was run. It also puts
add/multiply/divide/asarray/sum/mean OUT OF SCOPE for gating - not because those routes are fine,
but because the floor is what is left in them.

CONSOLIDATED SESSION RESULT on the small-n board (hz4, seed 555, h2h_decompose, same harness at
both ends; six untouched control routes moved -21 to +68 ns, and numpy's own arm is stable to
1.2%):
  sort n=64     +2076 -> +475    2.040x -> 1.241x        concat n=64   +1825 -> +754   2.417x -> 1.589x
  sort n=1024   +2258 -> +545    1.278x -> 1.069x        concat 2^14   +2131 -> +795   1.236x -> 1.090x
  argsort n=64  +2049 -> +468    1.657x -> 1.152x        max n=64       +645 -> +111   1.214x -> 1.038x
  isnan n=64     +725 -> +397    1.884x -> 1.500x        argmax n=64    +186 -> -322   1.081x -> 0.858x WIN
  abs n=64       +718 -> +552    1.866x -> 1.689x        sum n=64       +477 -> +383   1.153x -> 1.126x

SUCCESSOR: deadlock-audit-1uf80 - reduce the wrapper floor itself, which is now the binding
constraint on this whole surface and the stated reason four separate levers were rejected.

title: bug: np.cross on int32/uint32 loses precision (f64 products) — wrong wraparound
description: np.cross computes a×b in f64; for int32/uint32 inputs the component products (a[i]*b[j]) exceed 2^53 and the f64 result wraps WRONG when cast back to the narrow int dtype. Repro: cross(uint32[max,1,2], uint32[3,max,1]) -> numpy [3,7,4294967294] but fnp [3,7,0] (the max*max term loses low bits in f64). numpy computes cross in the input integer dtype with two's-complement wraparound. FIX: when UFuncArray::cross inputs carry/synthesize an integer sidecar (incl narrow ints promoted to i64/u64), compute the 2x2 determinant components (a1*b2 - a2*b1 etc.) in i64/u64 with wrapping_mul/wrapping_sub and carry an exact sidecar — same pattern as the trace/prod fixes. Found via fnp-vs-numpy tobytes differential (cross 56/300, int32/uint32 BYTES + float32 ULP-expected). Part of the f64-accumulate/product-then-cast bug class (cf. trace, vdot, prod-axis).
close_reason: Fixed in 8eb265aa. Integer cross fast path (wrapping i64/u64 + native ArrayStorage); 0 divergences vs numpy across 800 cases incl mixed dtype + overflow; unit test added; lib green 2191.

title: PROFILE: baseline benchmarks captured + geterr inline
description:
## Summary
Established baseline performance metrics for core operations and added profiling infrastructure.

## Changes
1. Added `[profile.release-perf]` to workspace Cargo.toml for profiling with debug symbols
2. Added `#[inline]` to `geterr()` - called at start of every fast path to check error state

## Baseline Benchmarks (ts2 remote)
| Operation | Time | Elements | ns/elem |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|
| ufunc_add_broadcast 1024x1024_by_1024 | 14.7-15.2ms | 1M | ~15 |
| reduce_sum_axis1_1024x1024 | 666-674µs | 1M | ~0.67 |
| matmul_256x256_by_256x256 | 2.58-2.60ms | 16M ops | - |
| sort_quicksort_1m | 4.27-4.47ms | 1M | ~4.3 |
| fft_65536 | 2.47-2.49ms | 64K | ~38 |
| astype_f64_to_i32 1024x1024 | 750-794µs | 1M | ~0.77 |
| reshape_1024x1024_to_2048x512 | 159-165µs | - | - |
| io_npy_save_load_512x512_f64 | 117-122µs | 256K | ~0.46 |

## Analysis
- Hot paths already have dedicated fast paths (same-shape, tail-contiguous broadcast)
- Fast paths skip error checking when `geterr().is_all_ignore()` is true
- `is_all_ignore` already had `#[inline]` hint, `geterr` was missing it
- Broadcast ops are memory-bound (~15ns/elem includes allocation)
- Reduction is extremely fast at <1ns/elem (likely cache-friendly)

## Next Steps
- Monitor for regressions using these baselines
- Profile with samply/flamegraph to identify deeper hotspots if needed

title: Centralize QR iteration limit coefficients and document rationale
description:
## Problem

Two different iteration limit coefficients exist for QR iteration:
- SVD bidiagonal QR: `100 * n * n` (used in svd_nxn)
- Symmetric eigenvalue QR: `60 * n * n` (used in tridiag_eig_qr AND hessenberg QR for general eigenvalues)

Named constants were already created in the audit:
- `SVD_QR_ITERATION_COEFF = 100`
- `EIGEN_QR_ITERATION_COEFF = 60`

But the actual loop code still uses the literal expressions `100 * n * n` and `60 * n * n` rather than the named constants. The constants exist but aren't wired in yet.

## Why Different Coefficients?

SVD uses a larger coefficient (100) because bidiagonal QR can require more iterations for convergence than symmetric tridiagonal QR (60). LAPACK uses similar ratios. The 60 coefficient for eigenvalue QR appears in both the symmetric (tridiag_eig_qr) and non-symmetric (Hessenberg QR) paths, which is correct — both use implicit shifted QR on similar matrix structures.

## Proposed Fix

1. Find all `100 * n * n` occurrences in SVD code → replace with `SVD_QR_ITERATION_COEFF * n * n`
2. Find all `60 * n * n` occurrences in eigenvalue code → replace with `EIGEN_QR_ITERATION_COEFF * n * n`
3. Add doc comments explaining why the coefficients differ
4. Verify no other hard-coded iteration limits exist in QR loops

## Validation

- All linalg tests must pass
- All conformance tests must pass
- The actual iteration counts should be unchanged (this is a naming refactor, not a behavioral change)

## Files to Modify

- `crates/fnp-linalg/src/lib.rs` — SVD bidiagonal QR loop, tridiag_eig_qr loop, Hessenberg QR loop
close_reason: Wired SVD_QR_ITERATION_COEFF (100) and EIGEN_QR_ITERATION_COEFF (60) into all 3 QR iteration loops. Constants documented at top of file.

title: Fast fft_pow2 kernel (split-radix/SIMD) + transpose-based N-D FFT — unblocks 2-D FFT-conv + speeds all FFT ops
description:
fnp's radix-2 fft_pow2 (the core behind fft/ifft/rfft/fft2/fftn/Bluestein + the 1-D FFT convolution 8fd90e76) is a SLOW SCALAR kernel: per-butterfly twiddle recurrence (serial dep, no vectorize) + fft_mul branch per multiply. It is the bottleneck behind two REJECTED FFT levers this session:

1. TWIDDLE TABLE (reverted): precompute tw[j]=exp(i·TAU·j/n), index tw[k·(n/len)] per pass = 0.52x (2x SLOWER) at 2^20. The table (n/2 = 8MB) exceeds cache and tw[k·step] is a STRIDED cache-missing gather; the recurrence keeps w in registers (cache-optimal). So a naive table is WRONG.

2. 2-D FFT convolve2d (reverted): fft_linear_convolve_2d via fftn_along_axis row+col passes = 0.46x (2x SLOWER) at [256,256]*[64,64] vs the parallel-direct gather. The COLUMN pass (axis 0) is STRIDED (fftn_along_axis gathers/scatters each column per line) + slow fft_pow2. 1-D FFT-conv WORKS (4.6x) because it is contiguous; 2-D loses to strided columns.

THE REAL LEVERS (advanced-math / alien-artifact zone, target ~2-3x on fft_pow2 → unblocks 2-D FFT-conv + speeds every FFT op):
- SPLIT-RADIX or RADIX-4 butterflies: ~25-33% fewer real multiplies than radix-2, fewer passes. Keeps the cache-friendly recurrence. Intricate bit-correct impl with inf/NaN (fft_mul) handling.
- SIMD butterflies (portable_simd): vectorize the butterfly inner loop. The twiddle recurrence blocks it; reorganize as `for k {w=twiddle(k); for block {butterfly}}` so the inner block loop has CONSTANT twiddle and vectorizes (helps outer passes), or use a per-pass CONTIGUOUS small twiddle table (len/2 entries, cache-fits) indexed contiguously.
- TRANSPOSE-BASED N-D FFT: replace fftn_along_axis's strided column gather with an explicit transpose between passes so every 1-D FFT is on CONTIGUOUS data. This is what makes 2-D FFT-conv viable (re-enable fft_linear_convolve_2d, gated, after this lands).
- FINITE FAST PATH: if all data finite (one O(n) scan), use plain `*` instead of fft_mul in the butterfly (bit-identical for finite data) to drop 4 branches/butterfly.

PARITY: all fft tests are TOLERANCE-based (1e-9..1e-15, no golden), so a kernel swap is permitted as long as it stays within tolerance AND is actually faster (the twiddle table was within tolerance but slower).

title: [perf][no-gaps] SIMD polynomial native transcendentals (sin/log/sqrt/tanh) — target 2-4x per-core, compute-bound
description:
CONTEXT (2026-06-09, cc analysis after the parallelize-a-serial-op well ran dry):
The recent perf wins all had real per-element COMPUTE (binary search, division, decode) or a complexity-class reduction (pairwise einsum O(n^4)->O(n^3)). Three levers attempted-and-REJECTED this turn all hit the MEMORY-BANDWIDTH wall (sub-2.0):
 - bincount privatized-fold: 0.5-0.6x (cheap cast+increment, serial scatter already at bandwidth floor; per-thread alloc+merge dominates).
 - set-op (intersect/union/setdiff/setxor) parallel sort: ~1.3x (dominated by linear clone/dedup/merge/f64-convert, not the sort).
 - einsum single-operand reduction routing to reduce_sum_axes: ~1.5-1.8x, 'ijk->i' possibly regresses (both general loop and reduce read the full input once = memory-bound).

NEXT PRIMITIVE (compute-bound, real gap vs numpy's SIMD ufuncs):
fnp's NATIVE unary transcendentals (UnaryOp::Sin/Log/Sqrt/Tanh in native_unary_promoting_or_passthrough) call scalar Rust libm per element + rayon across cores. numpy uses per-core SIMD polynomial ufuncs. For transcendentals the per-element compute (tens of cycles) dominates over memory, so a portable-SIMD (std::simd f64x4/f64x8) polynomial approximation with range reduction is a genuine 2-4x PER CORE win and closes a real gap. NOTE: np.exp is a pure numpy passthrough (core_numpy_passthrough) — NO gap there; only the native ops qualify.

BLOCKER TO RESOLVE FIRST: determine whether native transcendental parity is BIT-EXACT (tobytes/array_equal vs numpy) or TOLERANCE (allclose). A SIMD poly approx is ~1-2 ULP, so:
 - if tolerance-based -> implement SIMD poly (Cephes/Sleef-style minimax coeffs), target 2-4x, prove allclose + golden sha256 of fnp's own bits.
 - if bit-exact vs numpy/libm -> a poly approx WILL break parity; would need to match numpy's exact SIMD algorithm (hard) -> likely a no-ship, document and move to the next primitive.

OTHER BIG PRIMITIVES ON THE SHELF (for reference): SIMD complex FFT butterfly across blocks (FFT is tolerance-based but fft_pow2 radix-4 is already register-blocked + finite-fast-path = near-optimal per prior analysis); Strassen GEMM (shelved, needs an architectural tolerance-relaxation decision per bead ix117); randomized SVD (fnp-linalg, contended by the SVD agent).
close_reason: NO-SHIP: investigated with 2 de-risking experiments. (1) Branchless autovec ln is accurate (1.06e-13 rel err) but 0.53x SPEED vs libm — i32->f64 exponent convert + 4 edge selects block clean 4-wide avx2-no-fma autovec, and libm ln is already ~10-15cyc. (2) NO GAP vs numpy: fnp transcendentals already rayon-parallel across ~10 cores while numpy SIMD ufuncs are single-threaded, so fnp already comparable-or-faster. (3) Hand-intrinsic wide SIMD needs std::arch=unsafe, blocked by forbid(unsafe_code). Also refuted: naive LSD radix sort 0.35-0.64x vs sort_unstable (scatter cache-thrash; pdqsort excellent). Next genuine primitives all need architectural decisions: relax forbid-unsafe for vetted SIMD module, cache-aware parallel radix, Strassen (shelved ix117), randomized SVD (linalg agent).

Extended metamorphic test suite for fnp-io with 13 new tests covering

- **Large array roundtrip**: 100K element stress test
- **Integer boundary values**: i8/i16/i32/u8/u16/u32 MIN/MAX roundtrip
- **Float special values**: 0.0, -0.0, INF, -INF, NaN, MAX, MIN roundtrip

title: [idea-wizard] Diagnostic parity and upstream drift wave
description:
Context:
- The prior idea-wizard many-core conformance/performance wave is closed, including sharded fnp-python conformance, API coverage gates, benchmark telemetry, RaptorQ stress/parallelism, and evidence-link validation.
- Current live work is concentrated on fnp-python I/O wrappers and a recfunctions structured-dtype bug, so this wave avoids duplicating that active implementation surface.
- FrankenNumPy's stated goal is drop-in NumPy compatibility. Value/shape parity is well represented, but exception classes, warning behavior, version-specific upstream drift, and intentional divergence documentation are still comparatively informal.

Phase 2 summary: generated 30 candidate improvements and winnowed to the best five: (1) exception/warning parity harness, (2) structured dtype/record-array oracle corpus, (3) cross-version NumPy drift matrix, (4) view/stride mutation error parity, and (5) agent-readable validation recipes. Phase 3 next-best ideas included IO parser diagnostic goldens, oracle environment capsules, masked/object dtype diagnostic matrices, adversarial NPY/NPZ fuzz interop, and generated divergence docs.

Goal:
- Make diagnostic behavior a first-class compatibility contract: capture NumPy exception class/warning/category/message-shape behavior, gate high-risk surfaces, track upstream-version drift, and document intentional divergences so future agents do not silently normalize away observable NumPy behavior.

Non-negotiables:
- Preserve strict NumPy observable behavior unless a divergence is explicitly documented and gated.
- Keep heavy validation behind rch.
- Add deterministic JSON/JSONL reports suitable for bv/br triage and agent handoff.
- Do not duplicate the closed many-core/performance wave or the active fnp-python I/O wrapper beads.

Done when:
- Child beads form an acyclic graph, each with clear acceptance criteria and validation commands.
- New gates distinguish code failure from oracle/environment drift.
- Any discovered behavior gaps are filed as follow-up beads instead of hidden in prose.
close_reason: Completed diagnostic parity/upstream drift wave: all child beads are closed and dependency graph has no cycles.

title: Build exception and warning oracle capture schema
description:
Context:
- Many conformance tests compare returned values, shapes, or dtypes, but drop-in compatibility also depends on exception class, warning category, warning count/order, and stable message fragments.
- This is the foundation bead for the diagnostic parity wave; downstream surface-specific gates should reuse its schema instead of each inventing local formats.

Scope:
- Add a deterministic fnp-conformance schema for diagnostic cases: input id, API/surface, strict/hardened mode if applicable, expected NumPy exception class or warning category, message fragment policy, version guards, and whether a divergence is intentional.
- Add a small oracle runner that executes Python snippets under NumPy and emits JSON/JSONL observations for success, exception, and warning paths.
- Include environment metadata: FNP_ORACLE_PYTHON, numpy.__version__, platform, and interpreter path, so agent handoffs can separate oracle drift from code regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover success, exception, single-warning, multi-warning, and version-guarded diagnostic cases.
- The report is deterministic and stable under repeated runs.
- Missing/unknown diagnostic expectations fail closed unless the case is explicitly marked exploratory.
- Validation commands include: rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-conformance diagnostic_oracle; rch exec -- cargo clippy -p fnp-conformance --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo fmt --check for touched files or a documented unrelated fmt blocker.
close_reason: Completed: added diagnostic oracle schema, Python-backed warning/exception capture runner, smoke CLI, and validation tests.

title: Gate dtype and shape diagnostic parity
description:
Context:
- Dtype promotion/casting and shape/stride legality are crown-jewel compatibility surfaces. A wrong exception class or warning path can break downstream NumPy callers even when successful cases match.
- This task should build on the diagnostic oracle schema from franken_numpy-33vtd.1.

Scope:
- Add diagnostic conformance cases for fnp-dtype and fnp-ndarray high-risk paths: invalid casts, unsafe casts, reshape -1 errors, broadcast failures, overflowed element counts, invalid strides/views, and unsupported dtype descriptors.
- Compare NumPy exception class, warning category, and stable message fragments where practical. Use version guards for known NumPy 1.x/2.x differences.
- Emit a report section that future agents can map directly to the dtype/SCE contract surface.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least 20 diagnostic cases across dtype and ndarray surfaces.
- Tests include empty shape, overflow, multi -1 reshape, incompatible broadcast, and invalid cast policy examples.
- Failures distinguish target mismatch from oracle execution failure.
- Validation commands include: rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-conformance dtype_shape_diagnostics; rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-dtype; rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-ndarray; rch exec -- cargo clippy -p fnp-conformance -p fnp-dtype -p fnp-ndarray --all-targets -- -D warnings.
close_reason: Completed: added 22 NumPy-backed dtype and ndarray diagnostic cases with surface summary and oracle evaluation tests.

title: Gate IO parser and NPZ diagnostic parity
description:
Context:
- fnp-io is a security and compatibility boundary. Existing tests cover many successful NPY/NPZ/text paths, but malformed input behavior needs diagnostic parity so strict mode does not mask user-visible NumPy behavior.
- This extends the new diagnostic schema into parser and archive surfaces.

Scope:
- Add diagnostic cases for malformed NPY headers, unsupported object/pickle settings, truncated payloads, invalid descriptors, EOCD/ZIP central-directory defects, duplicate/invalid NPZ member names, and text parsing failures for loadtxt/genfromtxt/fromfile.
- Compare exception class and stable message fragments against NumPy where a public NumPy API has a matching path; otherwise classify the case as hardened-only with explicit rationale.
- Emit JSONL suitable for later fuzz/minimization work.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least 20 IO diagnostic cases, with both NPY and NPZ represented.
- Include at least one compressed NPZ and one uncompressed NPZ malformed-path case.
- Strict-vs-hardened divergence is explicit; no unknown diagnostic path passes silently.
- Validation commands include: rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-io npy_npz_diagnostic; rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-conformance io_diagnostics; rch exec -- cargo clippy -p fnp-io -p fnp-conformance --all-targets -- -D warnings.
close_reason: Completed: added IO/NPZ diagnostic oracle runner, 22 NumPy diagnostic cases, JSON/JSONL output, and fnp-io malformed-boundary reason-code tests.

title: Add fnp-python warnings and exceptions conformance shard
description:
Context:
- fnp-python is the user-facing drop-in surface. Many wrappers delegate to NumPy for unsupported paths, but wrappers still need to preserve exception class, warning category, and argument validation order.
- This task should wait for active fnp-python I/O and recfunctions work to settle before editing shared files.

Scope:
- Add a new shard or extend the fnp-python conformance shard manifest with warning/exception-focused cases.
- Cover representative wrappers from array creation, dtype utilities, IO, recfunctions, masked/object helpers, and deprecation paths such as aliases that should warn.
- Use the diagnostic oracle schema from franken_numpy-33vtd.1, and mark intentional divergences explicitly instead of hiding them in test code.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least 30 fnp-python diagnostic cases across 5+ API families.
- Tests verify warning category/count/order and exception class for selected cases.
- The shard has a deterministic rch runner entry and JSON/JSONL output.
- Validation commands include: rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-python --test <diagnostic shard> -- --nocapture; rch exec -- cargo run -p fnp-conformance --bin run_fnp_python_conformance_shards -- --list-shards; rch exec -- cargo clippy -p fnp-python --tests -- -D warnings.
close_reason: Completed: added fnp-python diagnostic conformance shard covering warnings and exception classes across API families; filed follow-up beads for discovered diagnostic gaps.

title: Add cross-version NumPy oracle drift matrix
description:
Context:
- Prior work added NumPy version detection for specific tests, but the project still lacks a first-class matrix that records how diagnostic/value expectations differ across supported NumPy versions.
- Without this, agents can mistake upstream NumPy changes for FrankenNumPy regressions or accidentally bake one local oracle version into long-lived fixtures.

Scope:
- Add a conformance runner that can execute a selected fixture subset against multiple configured NumPy interpreters: repo default, optional NumPy 1.x, optional NumPy 2.x, and optional nightly/dev when available.
- Emit a drift matrix showing stable expectations, version-gated differences, new upstream warnings/errors, and unsupported/missing oracle environments.
- The runner must degrade clearly when an interpreter is unavailable: environment missing is not a code failure, but a missing required matrix lane should fail if the gate is configured as required.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover matrix merge logic, missing interpreter handling, stable case, and version-divergent case.
- A smoke e2e command runs against the available repo oracle and writes deterministic JSON.
- Existing version-detection tests are integrated or referenced, not duplicated.
- Validation commands include: rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-conformance oracle_drift_matrix; rch exec -- cargo run -p fnp-conformance --bin <matrix runner> -- --smoke --report-path target/oracle_drift_matrix.json; rch exec -- cargo clippy -p fnp-conformance --all-targets -- -D warnings.
close_reason: Completed in 0c86f14: added oracle drift matrix runner with remote validation and smoke JSON report evidence.

title: Document intentional divergences from diagnostic gates
description:
Context:
- The project currently has scattered comments and README limitations, but no single generated/checked divergence ledger that tells future agents whether a diagnostic mismatch is intentional, temporary parity debt, or an upstream-version split.
- This task should use outputs from the diagnostic oracle and cross-version matrix instead of hand-written speculation.

Scope:
- Add or generate a docs artifact such as docs/DIVERGENCES.md or an artifacts/compatibility divergence report that records intentional diagnostic/value/warning divergences with rationale, affected NumPy versions, strict/hardened behavior, and follow-up bead IDs.
- Add a checker that fails when a diagnostic gate marks a divergence as intentional but the divergence ledger lacks an entry.
- Link the report from the relevant README/FEATURE_PARITY location only if that avoids stale manual claims.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least one synthetic/unit fixture proves missing-ledger entries fail closed.
- The report distinguishes intentional divergence from unimplemented parity debt.
- The checker emits deterministic JSON or Markdown and is usable by future agents without reading old conversations.
- Validation commands include: rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-conformance divergence_ledger; rch exec -- cargo run -p fnp-conformance --bin <divergence checker> -- --fail-on-missing; ubs on touched docs/code files.
close_reason: Completed: divergence ledger docs, parser/checker, fail-closed missing-ledger diagnostics, and run_divergence_ledger validation landed in d5bf59d; closeout was waiting on tracker reservation.

title: Expand structured dtype and recfunctions oracle corpus
description:
Context:
- The active franken_numpy-86iws bug shows that structured dtype and recfunctions behavior is fragile: flatten=False promotion/wrapping semantics differ for single-field inputs.
- This task should start after that bug is resolved, then broaden coverage so the same class of regression does not recur.

Scope:
- Add a structured dtype and recfunctions oracle corpus covering merge_arrays, unstructured_to_structured, repack_fields, rename/drop/append fields, nested fields, duplicate names, object fields, byte order, and empty records.
- Include diagnostic expectations for invalid field layouts and duplicate-name behavior using the diagnostic schema when available.
- Produce a report that maps each corpus case to the fnp-python/fnp-dtype/fnp-io surface it protects.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least 25 structured dtype/recfunctions cases with live NumPy oracle comparison.
- Includes single-field, multi-field, nested-field, duplicate-name, and flatten=True/False scenarios.
- The active franken_numpy-86iws regression is represented as a permanent conformance case after it is fixed.
- Validation commands include: rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-python --test conformance_dtype_utils; rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-conformance structured_dtype_corpus; rch exec -- cargo clippy -p fnp-python -p fnp-conformance --tests -- -D warnings.
close_reason: Completed: added 32-case live NumPy structured dtype/recfunctions oracle corpus in fnp-python conformance tests.

title: Add agent-readable validation recipe selector
description:
Context:
- Agents repeatedly need to choose the smallest trustworthy rch validation set for a changed surface. The closed many-core wave created shards and coverage reports, but there is still no single command that maps changed files or bead labels to the recommended validation recipe.
- This should be a thin selector over existing manifests, not a new test framework.

Scope:
- Add a deterministic recipe selector that accepts changed paths, bead labels, or crate names and emits the recommended rch commands, expected reports, and known environment prerequisites.
- Integrate existing fnp-python shard manifest, API coverage gate, performance/packet gates, and the new diagnostic parity reports when available.
- Emit JSON suitable for agent mail handoffs and markdown suitable for final session summaries.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover path-to-crate mapping, fnp-python conformance shard selection, fnp-io parser selection, docs-only changes, and unknown paths.
- The selector never claims workspace-wide proof is required when a narrower scoped proof is sufficient, and never suppresses required gates for high-risk surfaces.
- Validation commands include: rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-conformance validation_recipe_selector; rch exec -- cargo run -p fnp-conformance --bin <recipe selector> -- --changed crates/fnp-io/src/lib.rs --format json; ubs on touched files.

title: [perf] fnp-ufunc::fft radix-2 first butterfly uses generic twiddle path
description: Continuation pass-3 profile on rch worker vmi1149989 after 30a6f57c: fft_65536 is the second-largest remaining core_ops hotspot at center 4.5750 ms, CI [4.2350 ms, 4.9701 ms], after sort_quicksort_1m 6.1723 ms. Sort's next obvious zero-based pre-scan was rejected under proof rules, so this bead targets the next high-score profiler-evident hotspot. Source trace: fft_pow2 starts at len=2 even though w=(1,0) for every butterfly in that pass; the generic loop still calls fft_mul four times per pair and updates an unused twiddle recurrence. title: [no-gaps][POLICY][P1] Enable +fma (with tolerance-parity for non-reproducible float ops) to unlock BLAS-class GEMM speed
description: ROOT-CAUSE of the matmul/dot-vs-OpenBLAS gap (and a ceiling on ALL float-op perf vs numpy). numpy's matmul/exp/etc. use FMA+AVX (OpenBLAS/SVML). Our kernels CANNOT use hardware FMA because: (1) .cargo/config enables +avx2 but NOT +fma — enabling +fma is known to break ~16 conformance tests that assert array_equal (BIT-EXACT) on inherently-non-bit-reproducible float ops (matmul, einsum, transcendentals); (2) #[target_feature(enable=fma)] needs unsafe, forbidden by forbid(unsafe_code) in all crates except fnp-python. So our GEMM stays ~4-5x slower than OpenBLAS at n=512 (FMA ~2x + microkernel/packing ~2x; B-packing alone REGRESSED 2.3x, NC-panel already L2-resident). THE UNLOCK: (a) AUDIT the ~16 float conformance tests using array_equal -> relax to allclose where numpy itself is non-reproducible (matmul/einsum/dot/exp/log/trig/...); numpy's BLAS results already vary by thread count, so bit-exact-vs-numpy is the WRONG contract for these. (b) Enable +fma in .cargo/config (or x86-64-v3). (c) Re-audit kernels that NEED bit-exact (integer ops, exact reductions) to ensure they're unaffected or use explicit non-FMA paths. PAYOFF: ~2x across every FMA-able float kernel (GEMM, transcendentals, dot, conv, cov), enabling np.matmul/dot routing to BEAT numpy. RISK: project-wide; needs orchestrator/multi-agent sign-off (BlackThrush/IndigoFrog maintain many goldens). This is the single highest-leverage no-gaps lever — gated on a parity-policy decision, not engineering. Found by cc-numpy 2026-06-04 while closing 7put0 (einsum/histogram2d routing shipped; matmul blocked here).

title: [parity] histogram_full uses floor-division binning (FP-edge divergence vs numpy/basic histogram)
description: Reality-check finding. UFuncArray::histogram (basic, bins-only) bins via partition_point over the edge array — the code comment explicitly states this matches numpy and that naive ((v-min)/width) as usize mis-bins values on internal edges under FP rounding (e.g. (1.2-1.0)/0.2=0.9999..->bin0 instead of bin1). BUT UFuncArray::histogram_full (the range/weights/density path) still uses the buggy floor: idx=((v-lo)/width) as usize. So the two histogram implementations can disagree at FP-edge values, and histogram_full diverges from numpy there. Low user-facing impact today because fnp-python np.histogram fast-paths ONLY the simple integer-bins/no-range/no-weights/no-density case (-> basic histogram, correct) and FALLS BACK to real numpy for range/weights/density/edges (lib.rs ~10685-10720). So the bug is reachable only via the direct Rust histogram_full API. FIX: build edges first, bin via edges.partition_point(|e| *e<=v)-1 clamped to [0,bins-1], keeping the range filter (exclude v<lo||v>hi) and weights/density. Validate against numpy.histogram with explicit range + weights at exact internal-edge values. Lock with a test that feeds values exactly on internal edges and asserts basic histogram == histogram_full (no-range) bin-for-bin.

title: AUDIT: deadlock-finder static analysis - codebase safe
description:
## Summary
Full deadlock-finder audit of franken_numpy concurrency primitives found NO deadlock hazards.

## Scope
- fnp-ufunc: UFuncArrayView (SharedBuffer, SharedSidecar)
- fnp-python: PY_TEST_MUTEX (test serialization only)
- fnp-conformance: FILE_LOG_MUTEX (log serialization only)

## Findings

### UFuncArrayView Lock Ordering (SAFE)
Two Arc<RwLock<...>> fields: buffer and integer_sidecar

Contract documented at line 2228-2234:
> When acquiring both `buffer` and `integer_sidecar` locks, always acquire
> `integer_sidecar` first, then `buffer`.

Analysis of all lock acquisitions in impl block:
- `itemset()` (line 2437): sidecar.write() FIRST, then buffer.write() SECOND ✓
- `itemset_cow()` (line 2488): buffer.read() → drop → sidecar.read() → drop (sequential, not held simultaneously) ✓
- All other methods acquire only one lock ✓

### No AB-BA Pattern Possible
The only function holding both write locks (`itemset`) follows the documented ordering.
Read-only paths (`itemset_cow`) release each lock before acquiring the next.

## Action Taken
Added concurrent regression test: `shared_view_concurrent_itemset_no_deadlock`
- 4 threads × 25 itemset calls = 100 concurrent writes
- Would deadlock within seconds if ordering violated
- Passes in <1s

## Verdict
✅ CODEBASE SAFE - consistent lock ordering, no AB-BA deadlock possible

title: [HIGH] fnp-python lib tests flaky under parallel test threads — numpy state pollution
description:
Three fnp-python lib tests fail intermittently when run with cargo's default parallel test threads. They all pass reliably with '--test-threads=1'.

Affected tests:
- tests::count_nonzero_matches_numpy_axis_none            (left: 'np.int64(3)', right: '3')
- tests::count_nonzero_matches_numpy_keepdims_none_and_scalar_inputs (left: 'np.int64(0)', right: '0')
- tests::frompyfunc_live_callable_matches_numpy_reduce_scalar_where_and_direct_out (left/right swap between 'output must be an array' and 'return arrays must be of ArrayType')

Reproducer:
  export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_franken_numpy_cc
  cargo test -p fnp-python --lib               # 3 FAILED
  cargo test -p fnp-python --lib -- --test-threads=1  # 380 PASSED

Suspected cause: multiple pyo3 tests sharing the embedded CPython interpreter across threads. Symptoms include 'fnp_python::PyOGridClass is unsendable, but is being dropped on another thread' RuntimeErrors printed during the failing run. Possible contributors:
- tests::frompyfunc_reduce_does_not_delegate_to_numpy_frompyfunc poisons numpy.frompyfunc via setattr and restores it at end — if another test runs in parallel while numpy.frompyfunc is poisoned, the global replacement leaks.
- Custom PyClass instances registered by early tests linger in numpy's object cache.

Priority [HIGH]: Not a correctness bug but blocks clean 'cargo test --workspace' runs; CI almost certainly flakes on these three. Fix direction:
1. (Quick) Document --test-threads=1 requirement in crates/fnp-python/README.md or Cargo.toml [[bin]] entry.
2. (Better) Move the poison/restore dance in frompyfunc_reduce_does_not_delegate_to_numpy_frompyfunc into a process-exclusive section via a Mutex<()> shared across the three affected tests.
3. (Best) Rework tests that depend on numpy state comparisons to NOT use 'with_python' across threads; use a per-test embedded interpreter.

title: DISC-012: uint8+int8 dtype promotion returns float64 instead of int16
description:
## Summary
Mixed unsigned/signed integer dtype promotion differs from NumPy:
- `np.add(uint8, int8)` returns int16 (smallest type holding both ranges)
- `fnp.add(uint8, int8)` returns float64

## Impact
Affects all binary ufuncs with mixed unsigned/signed integer operands.

## Root Cause
fnp-dtype's promotion rules fall back to float64 for safety instead of computing the minimal compatible integer type.

## Fix Location
crates/fnp-dtype - type promotion logic

## Tests
- `add_dtype_promotion_unsigned_signed` (#[ignore] with DISC-012)

## Reference
DISCREPANCIES.md DISC-012

title: [parity-gap] fnp.where bypasses ndarray subclass dispatch
description: Review of commits 449b560, 9b41323, and 8b84f31 found fnp.where uses an isinstance(np.ndarray) fast-path guard for condition/x/y. ndarray subclasses that implement __array_function__ are therefore coerced through np.asarray and computed natively, while np.where dispatches to the subclass override. Repro: build fnp-python, then run a Python script that imports fnp_python and defines class WhereOverride(np.ndarray) with __array_function__ returning 'OVERRIDE' for np.where; x=np.asarray([1,2]).view(WhereOverride); np.where(np.array([True,False]), x, np.array([10,20])) returns 'OVERRIDE', but fnp.where(...) returns array([1,20]). The same mismatch occurs when condition is the subclass and in the one-argument fnp.where(condition) form. Expected: fnp.where should fall back to NumPy for ndarray subclasses / __array_function__ participants, or otherwise honor the same dispatch surface.
close_reason: Fixed fnp.where subclass dispatch parity by falling back to NumPy for non-exact ndarray participants and added conformance coverage.

title: [bug][no-gaps][fnp-python] np.cov((1,N), rowvar=False) returns scalar, numpy returns (N,N)
description: Found by cc 2026-06-09 while shipping cov/corrcoef Gram (d53dee38/a6858af3). np.cov of a (1,N) 2-D array with rowvar=False: numpy treats the N COLUMNS as N variables (1 observation each) -> returns an (N,N) matrix. fnp returns a 0-d scalar. Root: native_cov_unweighted's orientation guard 'if !rowvar && stacked.shape()[0] != 1 { transpose }' SKIPS the transpose when shape[0]==1, so a (1,N) rowvar=False input is mis-read as 1 variable x N obs instead of N variables x 1 obs. numpy does NOT have that shape[0]==1 special-case for the transpose (it always transposes when rowvar=False for a 2-D input). NOT a regression from the Gram work (the new fast path is rowvar=True only; this is the pre-existing rowvar=False path). Fix: drop/correct the shape[0]==1 guard so (1,N) rowvar=False transposes to (N,1) -> N variables. Verify vs numpy across (1,N)/(N,1) x rowvar T/F; add conformance. Low perf impact (degenerate 1-obs case) but a real parity gap.
close_reason: FIXED db14f928 (cc, 2026-06-09): np.cov of a genuine 2-D (1,N) array with rowvar=False now returns (N,N) (was a scalar). Root: native_cov_unweighted's 'stacked.shape()[0] != 1' guard conflated a true 1-D input (reshaped to (1,N), stays 1 variable) with a real 2-D (1,N) matrix (rowvar=False => N variables, always transpose). Fix: capture original ndim, transpose for rowvar=False whenever genuinely 2-D (no-y path); y path unchanged. ALSO fixed a sibling: corrcoef of a single variable now squeezes to 0-d scalar 1.0 (was (1,1)). 0 parity mismatches across cov/corrcoef x {(1,N),(N,1),1-D,(N,N),(1,1),y} x rowvar T/F. 25 conformance_statistics + new regression test green.

title: [MEDIUM] fnp-python hermite/laguerre wrapper value mismatches vs numpy
description:
Two fnp-python polynomial tests fail on workspace test battery with value mismatches that suggest a convention or implementation bug in the Rust-native Hermite/Laguerre polynomial operations (hermadd/hermsub/hermmul, lagadd/lagsub/lagmul, or related).

## Observed failures

### hermite_wrappers_match_numpy

```
left:  [2.0, 6.5, 1.0, 1.5]
right: [4.0, 13.0, 2.0, 3.0]
```

Exact 2× ratio between `right` and `left`. Classic physicist's H_n vs probabilist's He_n convention difference. The test compares against numpy.polynomial.hermite.\* (physicist's H), so our Rust 'herm\*' wrappers may be implementing probabilist's convention.

### laguerre_wrappers_match_numpy

```
left:  [-1.0, -1.0, 11.0, -9.0]
right: [2.0, 3.0, -8.0, 9.0]
```

No obvious scalar ratio; values differ in sign and magnitude. Likely a sign or recurrence-ordering bug in lagadd/lagsub/lagmul's Rust implementation.

## Reproduction

```
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_franken_numpy_cc
cargo test -p fnp-python --lib hermite_wrappers_match_numpy
cargo test -p fnp-python --lib laguerre_wrappers_match_numpy
```

## Scope

Tests touch a mix of operations (hermadd/hermsub/hermmul + hermval + hermroots). Test setup runs them in order and reports the FIRST mismatch — true root cause may require narrowing down which specific op produces the divergence. Suggest adding temporary prints or running individually.

## Priority rationale

P2/MEDIUM — these are Rust-side implementation bugs in fnp-ufunc's polynomial family. Not blocking CI because they were pre-existing before kuh8 was filed, but they represent functional divergence from numpy in the polynomial API, which is a user-facing regression vs. the README's parity claim.

## Ownership

cod-numpy is currently rust-porting fnp-python passthroughs. The Hermite/Laguerre wrappers may have been rust-ported already (check recent commits for hermadd/hermsub/hermmul/lagadd/lagsub/lagmul sites in crates/fnp-python/src/lib.rs and crates/fnp-ufunc/src/lib.rs). If they are still passthroughs to numpy, the failure might indicate a pyo3 boundary bug rather than a math bug.

## Related

Previously noted in UPGRADE_LOG.md 2026-04-22 session as 'pre-existing test drift' — this bead extracts them as an actionable followup.
close_reason:
Closed by cc-numpy — root cause identified and fixed. The failures were test-side off-by-basis errors, NOT Rust implementation bugs. Both fnp-python wrappers (hermmul, lagmul, hermmulx, lagmulx) are pure passthroughs to numpy.polynomial.hermite.* / numpy.polynomial.laguerre.*, so the math was always correct.

Actual bug: the test asserted  mulx(c) == mul(c, [0.0, 1.0])  which is the 'x = basis_1' identity. This only holds for Chebyshev T and probabilist's HermiteE He. For physicist's Hermite: x = H_1/2 → coefficient [0, 0.5] (2× factor matches the observed ratio). For Laguerre: x = L_0 - L_1 → coefficient [1, -1] (explains the sign+magnitude drift).

Fix (landed in cod's commit 20b669c which absorbed my edits to lib.rs):
- hermite test arg changed [0.0, 1.0] → [0.0, 0.5]
- laguerre test arg changed [0.0, 1.0] → [1.0, -1.0]

Verified via cargo test -p fnp-python --lib on CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rch_target_franken_numpy_cc: both hermite_wrappers_match_numpy and laguerre_wrappers_match_numpy now pass (1 ok / 0 failed each). No code changes needed to fnp-python wrappers; underlying numpy passthrough was always mathematically correct.

title: Preserve non-finite determinant parity
description:
## Problem
`det_2x2`, `slogdet_2x2`, `det_nxn`, and `slogdet_nxn` currently reject non-finite matrices. NumPy instead returns `nan` / `inf` values with deterministic sign handling for these APIs.

## Evidence
- `np.linalg.det([[nan,1],[2,3]]) -> nan`
- `np.linalg.slogdet([[nan,1],[2,3]]) -> (sign, nan)` with sign determined by cofactors / permutation
- `np.linalg.det([[inf,1],[2,3]]) -> inf` and `slogdet -> (1, inf)`
- off-diagonal infinity placements produce `-inf` with negative sign

## Goal
Match NumPy’s non-finite determinant and slogdet behavior for 2x2 and NxN paths without disturbing singular finite-matrix handling.

## Files
- `crates/fnp-linalg/src/lib.rs`
close_reason: Completed

title: [modes-of-reasoning] ufunc-completeness
description:
## Synthesis

The ufunc surface is extensive: 837 public functions in fnp-ufunc and 590 PyO3-exposed functions in fnp-python. The compliance matrix shows MUST=243, SHOULD=119, MAY=11 (373 total conformance cases). Zero unimplemented!/todo! markers in fnp-python indicates no known gaps in the exposed API. Deprecated API aliases are properly maintained (trapz→trapezoid, tostring→tobytes, random_integers with warning), ensuring backward compatibility with existing NumPy codebases.

The einsum implementation provides three strategies (basic, greedy, optimal), and gufunc signature validation exists via GufuncSignature. However, the complex dtype story needs verification - while abs_complex, iscomplex, iscomplexobj, and sort_complex exist, the breadth of complex-number operations across all ufuncs should be audited. Some SHOULD-level functions in the compliance matrix (concat_split=6, structured=4, testing=3) have lower coverage than critical MUST categories.

## Bead Suggestions

1. **Audit complex dtype coverage across ufuncs** - Verify that all arithmetic, comparison, and transcendental ufuncs handle complex128/complex64 inputs correctly

2. **Expand SHOULD-level conformance coverage** - Prioritize concat_split (hstack/vstack/dstack edge cases) and structured array operations for parity

3. **Add ufunc signature completeness test** - Create automated check that all numpy ufunc names exposed in fnp-python have matching signatures (arg count, kwarg names)
close_reason: Completed the ufunc signature-completeness slice: core fnp-python ufunc wrappers now accept NumPy-style keyword signatures, expose concrete ufunc text signatures, and have regression coverage for out=/where= behavior. title: perf(fnp-ufunc): eytzinger branchless searchsorted for many-needle large-array queries
description: searchsorted already parallel-over-needles with branchy binary search (O(q log n)). LEVER: eytzinger (BFS) layout + BRANCHLESS probe + prefetch = known 2-4x over std branchy binary search for large sorted arrays with many queries (cache-optimal access + no 50%-unpredictable branch). PLAN: when q (needles) and n both large, build eytzinger array of the sorted data once (O(n), amortized over q needles), run branchless probe (lo/hi via cmov, __builtin_prefetch-equivalent via slice indexing hints), map eytzinger position -> rank. PARITY-SAFE: returns the same integer insertion indices (deterministic), handle side=left/right + duplicate ties + the optional sorter permutation exactly. TARGET >=2x at n>=1e6, q>=1e5. Proof: searchsorted output bit-identical to current branchy path (integer indices) across left/right/ties/sorter + golden + same-process A/B. Feeds digitize/histogram/interp/percentile. ~1-2hr.
close_reason: Rejected with data: parallel branchy already optimal (eytzinger needs unavailable prefetch; merge loses to 64-way MLP). See comment + benches/searchsorted.rs.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
REJECTED with data (cc, 2026-06-09). Implemented eytzinger BFS-layout branchless probe + a sort-needles two-pointer merge; benched both vs the current per-needle rayon-PARALLEL branchy binary search at n=2^20/q=2^17 and n=2^18/q=2^16 (64-core, load ~6).

Results (criterion, benches/searchsorted.rs):
- branchy_par (current): 1.10ms @ n=2^20,q=2^17 ; 0.65ms @ n=2^18,q=2^16
- merge_par:             4.84ms                  ; 2.06ms   -> ~4x SLOWER
- eytzinger (serial):    27-59ms vs branchy serial 11-24ms -> ~2.5x SLOWER even single-threaded

WHY eytzinger loses: its entire win comes from software prefetch hiding deep-level cache misses; fnp-ufunc is #![forbid(unsafe_code)] so no prefetch intrinsic. Without it the BFS layout is pure overhead (full-depth probes, no early exit, +O(n) build).
WHY merge loses parallel: merge wins ~2-2.5x SINGLE-THREADED (sequential streaming beats random probes) but the amortization gate forces large q, which also engages want_parallel. Parallel branchy's 64-way memory-level parallelism converts the latency-bound random gather into a bandwidth-bound one (~1.1ms). Merge must pay an O(n) sequential scan + O(q log q) needle sort, both exceeding 1.1ms; merge can only beat branchy when q>>n AND sort is free, which never holds.

CONCLUSION: parallel branchy is the right algorithm on this hardware; eytzinger/merge rejected. Kept benches/searchsorted.rs as reproducible evidence + a guard against naive kernel swaps. lib.rs reverted to original (verified byte-identical to HEAD).

title: Define deterministic parallel partition contracts for ufuncs and reductions
description:
Context:
- Parallel array execution is only acceptable if chunking cannot change observable NumPy behavior. Floating reductions, signed zeros, NaN propagation, dtype promotion, broadcasting, and alias-sensitive views all need explicit contracts before implementation.
- This bead is the plan-space correctness gate for future parallel hot paths.

Scope:
- Specify deterministic partition contracts for broadcasted binary ufunc loops and sum-like reductions, including chunk boundaries, dtype accumulation, NaN/signed-zero handling, empty axes, keepdims, and alias/view restrictions.
- Add conformance or property tests that compare single-lane and partitioned execution plans without necessarily enabling worker threads yet.
- Document which operations are safe for initial parallelization and which remain serial until a stronger proof exists.

Acceptance criteria:
- Tests include broadcast add, broadcast multiply or comparable binary op, sum reduction, empty reduction edge, signed zero / NaN edge, and non-contiguous input/view planning.
- The partition planner is deterministic across repeated runs and independent of host CPU count unless an explicit thread-count parameter is supplied.
- Validation commands include: rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-ufunc <new partition tests>; rch exec -- cargo test -p fnp-conformance <new partition conformance tests>.
- The closeout references the many-core telemetry bead franken_numpy-8zhbh and explains remaining risks before enabling parallel workers.
close_reason: Completed deterministic parallel partition contracts for ufuncs and reductions. Added explicit config validation, deterministic C-order chunk planning, binary add/multiply planning gated on all-ignore float error state/no sidecars/no complex interleaved storage, sum-axis output-lane partition contracts, and view safety records for non-contiguous/overlap cases. Added replay tests against serial ufunc/reduction behavior plus conformance differential cases, invalid public config rejection, and tampered chunk rejection. This is planner/proof only: no worker execution is enabled. Remaining enablement risk belongs in franken_numpy-8zhbh/many-core telemetry: axis=None stays serial until a reproducible accumulator tree exists, direct view writeback stays serial, and broader ops need per-op error-order/sidecar/complex proofs before parallel workers are turned on.

title: [perf] fnp-dtype::ArrayStorage::to_f64_vec:1204 — per-element get_f64 in F64 result construction; elementwise add 14.86ms vs 0.53ms arithmetic (27x)
description:
## Scenario
core_ops baseline (run tests/artifacts/perf/2026-06-01_perf_baseline). ufunc_add_broadcast 1024x1024 (+) 1024 -> 1M f64 output.

## Baseline (criterion n=30, Threadripper 5975WX, taskset-pinned)
- ufunc_add_broadcast: 14.863 ms  CI[14.780, 15.007], MAD 0.254 ms, 67.3 M elem/s
- reduce_sum (same 1M elems): 0.699 ms -> add is 21.3x slower for identical element count.

## Profiler evidence (stage isolation, levelsplit_errstate.txt)
- raw_handwritten_add_1m: 0.526 ms  (the arithmetic alone, memory-bound)
- alloc_zero_8mb: 0.092 ms  (allocation negligible)
- construct_from_vec_1m: 18.90 ms  (building ONE UFuncArray from a 1M Vec)
- add(): ~14.5 ms ~= construction. errstate default-vs-all-ignore ratio 0.97-1.02x (irrelevant).
Triangulated; H1 (float-error checking), H2 (broadcast fast-path miss), H3 (add loop), H4 (alloc) all REJECTED; H5 (construction) SUPPORTED. See 30_hypothesis_ledger.md.

## Root cause (file:line)
fnp-ufunc/src/lib.rs:4764 UFuncArray::from_storage_with_dtype has a move-fast-path only for I64/U64 storage; for F64 it runs cast_to(F64) -> to_f64_vec() -> Self::new(). cast_to returns a cheap clone for matching dtype, but fnp-dtype/src/lib.rs:1204 ArrayStorage::to_f64_vec rebuilds the Vec<f64> via (0..n).map(|i| self.get_f64(i)) -- a per-element 15-arm enum match + bounds check + Result (fnp-dtype/src/lib.rs:974). ~19 ns/elem, unvectorizable. EVERY elementwise op that returns an F64 array pays this on its output.

## Hypothesized fix (one lever)
Add an already-matching-dtype fast path in from_storage_with_dtype (at least F64) that MOVES the inner Vec straight into Self::new, skipping cast_to+to_f64_vec; and/or specialize ArrayStorage::to_f64_vec for the F64 variant to return v.clone() instead of the per-element get_f64 loop. Expected: elementwise F64 ops drop from ~14.5 ms toward the ~0.5-1 ms memory-bound floor (order of magnitude), lifting the whole ufunc surface.

## Verify
Re-baseline against tests/artifacts/perf/2026-06-01_perf_baseline (criterion core_ops + examples/perf_levelsplit_errstate.rs). Gate with differential/conformance + ufunc invariants. Profiling pass owner: BlackThrush (measurement only).

description:
## Problem

In fnp-linalg's eigenvalue/eigenvector computation (eig_nxn_full), multiple absolute tolerance constants are used for different but related purposes:

- Line ~2086: `1e-10` — checks if sub-diagonal element in Schur form exceeds this threshold to identify complex eigenvalue pairs
- Line ~2329: `1e-10` — same check during eigenvector computation for 2×2 blocks
- Line ~2350: `1e-10` — block detection during eigenvector computation
- Line ~2342: `1e-15` — denominator check in eigenvector back-substitution (already partially fixed to use sign-preserving epsilon)
- Line ~2363: `1e-30` — complex denominator threshold

These absolute thresholds fail for matrices with very large or very small entries. A matrix with entries ~1e20 would have sub-diagonal elements ~1e10 that are mathematically zero but exceed the 1e-10 threshold. Conversely, a matrix with entries ~1e-20 might have genuine complex eigenvalues whose sub-diagonal elements are below 1e-10.

## What NumPy/LAPACK Does

LAPACK's DHSEQR and DTREVC routines use relative thresholds:
- `smallnum = DLAMCH('S') / DLAMCH('P')` (safe minimum / precision ≈ 1e-292 / 1.1e-16)
- Sub-diagonal test: `|H(i+1,i)| <= max(eps * (|H(i,i)| + |H(i+1,i+1)|), smlnum)`
- This scales with the diagonal elements, not absolute thresholds

## Proposed Fix

1. Compute matrix 1-norm or Frobenius norm at function entry
2. Define `eps_relative = f64::EPSILON * matrix_norm` (or `f64::EPSILON * max(|diag elements|)`)
3. Replace absolute `1e-10` thresholds with `eps_relative`
4. Replace absolute `1e-15` back-substitution threshold with `f64::EPSILON * matrix_norm`
5. Replace `1e-30` complex denominator threshold with `f64::MIN_POSITIVE`

## Consistency Issue

The current code uses THREE different thresholds (1e-10, 1e-15, 1e-30) for conceptually similar "is this value negligible?" checks. After the fix, all should use a single scale-relative approach.

## Validation

- All 201 fnp-linalg tests must pass
- All 114 conformance tests must pass (especially linalg_differential suite)
- Test with both well-conditioned and ill-conditioned matrices
- Test with matrices having entries of very different magnitudes (1e-10 to 1e10)

## Files to Modify

- `crates/fnp-linalg/src/lib.rs` — eig_nxn_full function and related eigenvector extraction
close_reason: Replaced all 7 absolute thresholds in eig_nxn_full and extract_schur_eigenvalues with scale-relative eps computed from matrix infinity-norm. Added matrix_inf_norm helper. All 201 linalg tests + full workspace pass.

title: [modes-of-reasoning] upstream-numpy-divergence-management
description:
## Synthesis

Divergence management is handled pragmatically but informally. NumPy 2.x compatibility is addressed (trapz→trapezoid, tostring→tobytes deprecation warnings), and deprecated API warnings are emitted via PyO3 for random_integers. Comments document specific divergences (e.g., "fnp.vectorize has a different API than np.vectorize"). The conformance test suite compares against live NumPy output, with explicit checks like "shape diverged from live NumPy" and "value length diverged from live NumPy".

However, there is no formal DIVERGENCES.md or compatibility matrix tracking intentional behavioral differences. Version-specific behavior (NumPy 1.x vs 2.x) is not gated behind feature flags or detected at runtime. The project tracks numpy oracle tests but lacks a mechanism to detect when upstream NumPy changes behavior in a new release. The README lists "Known Limitations" but doesn't distinguish between "not yet implemented" vs "intentionally different". For long-term maintenance, upstream tracking tooling would help catch breaking changes.

## Bead Suggestions

1. **Create DIVERGENCES.md tracking document** - Enumerate all intentional behavioral differences from NumPy with rationale (performance, safety, API clarity)

2. **Add numpy version detection in conformance tests** - Gate version-specific test expectations based on detected numpy.__version__ to prevent false positives

3. **Implement upstream change detection CI job** - Weekly job that runs conformance suite against numpy nightly to catch behavioral changes before release
close_reason: Implemented live NumPy version detection in fnp-conformance tests and gated trapezoid/trapz oracle expectations by detected numpy.__version__; validated with rch cargo test -p fnp-conformance and clippy.

title: recfunctions_merge_arrays flatten=False over-wraps single-field inputs as fN

Fix in crates/fnp-python/src/lib.rs around line 18029-18056: detect single-field unique-name case and emit flat dtype; fall back to numpy on duplicate-name conflicts. Re-run conformance_dtype_utils to verify.

title: [arch-decision][no-gaps] Relax forbid(unsafe_code) for a vetted std::arch SIMD module to unlock hand-written AVX2 kernels
description:
WHY (cc, 2026-06-09): The parallelize-a-serial-op perf well is dry — every hot op is already rayon-parallel. The remaining no-gaps frontier is COMPUTE-BOUND kernels (transcendentals, custom GEMM microkernel, sort), where the win requires WIDE hand-written SIMD. Two de-risking experiments this session proved the safe-Rust autovectorization route does NOT clear it:
 - branchless autovec ln: accurate (1e-13) but 0.53x vs libm (edge selects + i32->f64 convert block clean 4-wide avx2-no-fma autovec; libm already ~10-15cyc).
 - naive LSD radix u64 sort: 0.35-0.64x vs sort_unstable (cache-thrash; pdqsort excellent).

THE BLOCKER: real wide-SIMD (sleef-style transcendentals, register-blocked GEMM microkernels, cache-aware radix with SW write-combining) needs `std::arch` intrinsics, which are `unsafe`. The workspace pins #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. NOTE: std::arch SIMD is still 100% SAFE-RUST per the no-gaps directive's intent (no C/BLAS/MKL linkage) — `unsafe` here is the Rust keyword for intrinsics, not an FFI/C dependency.

PROPOSAL (needs user/orchestrator sign-off): allow ONE narrowly-scoped, heavily-tested module (e.g. crates/fnp-simd) with #![allow(unsafe_code)] containing only:
 - runtime is_x86_feature_detected! dispatch + safe scalar fallback (parity-preserving),
 - vetted std::arch AVX2 kernels with safe wrapper fns,
 - Miri-exempt but fuzzed + differential-tested vs the scalar path (bit-parity where required, allclose where the op is tolerance-based like transcendentals/FFT).
Everything else stays #![forbid(unsafe_code)].

EXPECTED PAYOFF once unblocked: AVX2 transcendentals (sin/log/tanh) ~3-4x/core; autotuned GEMM microkernel closing the BLAS gap; cache-aware radix sort > pdqsort for large integer keys. Keep the discipline (one lever/commit, isomorphism/golden, Score>=2.0).

ALTERNATIVE if forbid-unsafe is non-negotiable: accept that compute-bound transcendental/GEMM-microkernel gaps vs hand-tuned BLAS are bounded by what LLVM autovectorization + rayon deliver (which, for transcendentals, already roughly matches single-threaded-SIMD numpy via core count).
notes: PARITY AUDIT (2026-06-12, cc, clean fresh-array methodology at low load): the 'matmul 1.65-1.97x gap' cited for many turns was MEASUREMENT NOISE. Clean re-measure: matmul fnp 0.82x[n=2048]/1.07x[n=1536] = AT PARITY with numpy BLAS. solve/inv ratios are meaningless (numpy LAPACK thrashes to 331-1845ms here). Basic elementwise ALL ~1.0x (add/mul/div/sub/power/max/sum/where 0.97-1.04). Only residual gaps are SUB-1.5x SIMD-elementwise (square 1.29, rint 1.43, abs 1.22, floor/recip 1.15) where numpy's dedicated SIMD round/abs edges fnp's autovec. So this bead's scope is now NARROWER than thought: not a broad GEMM/BLAS gap (fnp already matches), but the last 20-40% on simple SIMD-elementwise ops (square/rint/abs/floor) via hand-SIMD round/abs intrinsics. Still needs user sign-off, but the urgency is LOWER — fnp is already competitive across heavy linalg + elementwise + reductions.
close_reason: Completed as safe-Rust policy enforcement: rejected the obsolete std::arch/unsafe relaxation path, added hygiene gates for unsafe blocks/items, allow(unsafe_code) overrides, and core/std::arch intrinsic references, while preserving portable safe-SIMD as the allowed direction.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: TRIAGE (cc 2026-06-15): premise appears obsolete + conflicts with the standing safe-Rust mandate. fnp-ufunc ALREADY has #![feature(portable_simd)] (lib.rs:27) AND #![forbid(unsafe_code)] (lib.rs:26), with std::simd::{Simd,SimdFloat,SimdPartialOrd,Select} actively used in live kernels (e.g. lib.rs:19322, 23485, 23569). So AVX2-class vectorization is ALREADY available in 100% safe Rust under forbid(unsafe_code) — the 'SIMD needs unsafe std::arch' premise no longer holds. Relaxing forbid(unsafe_code) for hand-written std::arch AVX2 would also directly contradict the no-gaps/no-ceiling directive ('We build our OWN 100% safe-Rust BLAS/LAPACK ... never link C BLAS/MKL/XLA' + 'THERE IS NO safe-Rust CEILING'). Recommend the orchestrator close as wontfix OR re-scope to 'find portable_simd kernels not yet vectorized' (a safe-Rust lever) rather than relaxing the unsafe ban. Not actioning unilaterally — this is a project-wide-invariant arch-decision the human owns.
